children.title: Contaminated Noise
children.top_down_role: Feedback regimes containing outliers or adversarially corrupted observations.

assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon>0\).
The nominal distribution has a finite mean for the finite-bias comparison.
The contaminating law is unrestricted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_Q|\mathbb E_RY-\mathbb E_PY|=\infty\), and some contaminating laws make \(\mathbb E_RY\) undefined.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mean-estimation boundary under unrestricted contaminating distributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every nominal distribution P with finite mean, every \(\varepsilon>0\), and every \(M>0\), there is a contaminating distribution Q such that \(R=(1-\varepsilon)P+\varepsilon Q\) has a finite mean differing from that of P by more than M. A sufficiently heavy-tailed Q can instead make the mixture mean undefined. Contamination proportion alone therefore gives no empirical-mean confidence radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even an arbitrarily small unrestricted contamination fraction can cause arbitrarily large mean bias or destroy the mean entirely.
knowledge_statements.title: Arbitrary Contamination Destroys Mean Control

assumptions_latex: \(0\le\varepsilon<1\).
Total variation is defined as \(\operatorname{TV}(P,Q)=\sup_A|P(A)-Q(A)|\).
Contaminating distributions are unrestricted.

notation.meaning: total-variation distance under the stated convention

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifiability boundary for two nominal feedback laws.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a probability measure P, define \[\mathcal H_\varepsilon(P)=\{(1-\varepsilon)P+\varepsilon Q:Q\text{ is a probability measure}\}.\] If \[\operatorname{TV}(P_0,P_1)\le\frac{\varepsilon}{1-\varepsilon},\] then \(\mathcal H_\varepsilon(P_0)\cap\mathcal H_\varepsilon(P_1)\ne\varnothing\). Consequently, observations from the common contaminated law cannot uniformly distinguish the two nominal laws without additional separation or restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sufficiently close nominal laws can generate exactly the same contaminated distribution, creating an information-theoretic identification failure.
knowledge_statements.title: Overlap of Huber Contamination Neighborhoods

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon pathwise contamination, distinct from stochastic mixture contamination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nominal feedback \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_T\), an observed sequence \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_T\) is \(m\)-replacement contaminated if some \(C\subseteq\{1,\ldots,T\}\) with \(|C|\le m\) satisfies \(Y_t=Z_t\) for \(t\notin C\), while \((Y_t)_{t\in C}\) are arbitrary. Unlike Huber mixture contamination, the number of replacements is controlled pathwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Budgeted replacement contamination permits arbitrary replacement of at most a fixed number of observations.
assumptions_latex: A finite horizon and nominal feedback sequence are specified.
Replacement values are unrestricted.
knowledge_statements.title: Budgeted Replacement Contamination

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential contamination with a history- and query-dependent corruption probability bounded by epsilon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Conditionally on \((\mathcal F_{t-1},x_t)\), let \(Z_t\sim P_{x_t}\), let \(C_t\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\alpha_t)\) be independent of \(Z_t\), where \(0\le\alpha_t\le\varepsilon\), and let \(W_t\) be an arbitrary replacement. Define \[Y_t=(1-C_t)Z_t+C_tW_t.\] The nonanticipating choices of \(\alpha_t\) and the conditional replacement law may depend on the permitted history and query. Equivalently, \[\mathcal L(Y_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},x_t)=(1-\alpha_t)P_{x_t}+\alpha_tQ_{t,x_t},\qquad0\le\alpha_t\le\varepsilon.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive contamination mixes nominal feedback with an arbitrary history-dependent corrupting law at a conditional rate no greater than epsilon.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t\) is measurable before \(Y_t\) is observed.
\(P_x\) is the declared nominal feedback kernel.
The contamination mechanism is nonanticipating, and the clean draw is conditionally independent of the corruption indicator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal L(Y_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},x_t)\in\bigcup_{0\le\alpha\le\varepsilon}\{(1-\alpha)P_{x_t}+\alpha Q:Q\text{ is a probability law}\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Probability-Budget Contamination
Contaminated Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Huber contamination model for Bayesian-optimization observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the nominal observation at query \(x_t\) have distribution \(P_{x_t}\). The feedback is \(\varepsilon\)-contaminated if, conditionally on the past \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\) and \(x_t\), its law satisfies
\[\mathcal L(Y_t\mid \mathcal F_{t-1},x_t)=(1-\varepsilon)P_{x_t}+\varepsilon Q_{t,x_t},\qquad 0\leq\varepsilon<1,\]
where \(Q_{t,x_t}\) is an arbitrary probability distribution that may depend on the query and history. Equivalently, each observation is nominal with probability \(1-\varepsilon\) and otherwise is generated by an unrestricted contaminating mechanism; no moment bound on the contaminated component is implied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An epsilon-contaminated observation follows the nominal noise law with probability one minus epsilon and an arbitrary, possibly adaptive, corrupting law otherwise.
assumptions_latex: \(P_x\) is a probability distribution for every admissible query \(x\).
\(Q_{t,x}\) is an arbitrary probability distribution measurable with respect to the permitted contamination mechanism.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal L(Y_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},x_t)\in\{(1-\varepsilon)P_{x_t}+\varepsilon Q:Q\text{ is a probability distribution}\}.\)

notation.meaning: nominal observation distribution at query x

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard Huber epsilon-contamination definition specialized to sequential feedback

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Contaminated Noise leaf and is mathematically coherent, but no citation with an inspectable locator supports the sequential, history-dependent Huber contamination formulation.

children.title: Robust-Feedback Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits of confidence calibration under nonstandard feedback distributions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded-influence mean estimation for heavy-tailed or replacement-contaminated scalar feedback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\tau>0\), define \(\psi_\tau(z)=\max\{-\tau,\min\{z,\tau\}\}\) and \(\widehat\mu_\tau=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\psi_\tau(Z_i)\). Each replacement changes the estimate by at most \(2\tau/n\). If clean observations satisfy \(\mathbb E|Z|^{1+\alpha}\le V\), then \(|\mathbb E\psi_\tau(Z)-\mathbb EZ|\le V\tau^{-\alpha}\); at most \(m\) arbitrary replacements add at most \(2m\tau/n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clipping bounds individual influence and separates finite-moment bias from replacement-contamination error.
assumptions_latex: The clean distribution has a finite \((1+\alpha)\)-moment for the bias bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Clipped-Mean Robustification

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample bound separating stochastic, tail-bias, and replacement terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the clean counterfactual observations are independent with common mean \(\mu\) and \((1+\alpha)\)-moment at most \(V\), and at most \(m\) observed values are replaced, then for \(0<\delta<1\), \[\Pr\!\left(|\widehat\mu_\tau-\mu|\le \tau\sqrt{\frac{2\log(2/\delta)}{n}}+V\tau^{-\alpha}+\frac{2m\tau}{n}\right)\ge1-\delta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clipped feedback has a confidence radius containing concentration, tail-bias, and replacement-contamination terms.
assumptions_latex: Clean counterfactual observations are independent with common mean \(\mu\) and \((1+\alpha)\)-moment at most \(V\).
At most \(m\) observations are arbitrarily replaced.
knowledge_statements.title: Clipped-Mean Confidence Decomposition

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No Distribution-Free Mean Confidence Without Uniform Tail Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample impossibility over unrestricted finite-mean distributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(n\ge1\), \(0<\delta<1/2\), and a finite radius \(r\). Over all distributions having a finite but otherwise unrestricted mean, no estimator based on \(n\) observations has a uniform \((1-\delta)\) confidence radius \(r\). Rare sufficiently large observations make a distribution nearly indistinguishable in \(n\) samples from a point mass while changing its mean arbitrarily.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite mean alone cannot support a uniform finite-sample mean-confidence radius.
assumptions_latex: The distribution class has no uniform moment, tail, support, or contamination restriction.
knowledge_statements.title: No Distribution-Free Mean Confidence Without Uniform Tail Control

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-robust scalar location estimator for weak-tailed clean feedback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Partition \(n\) observations into \(k\) nonempty disjoint blocks \(B_1,\ldots,B_k\), form \(M_j=|B_j|^{-1}\sum_{i\in B_j}Z_i\), and return a declared median \[\widehat\mu_{\mathrm{MOM}}\in\operatorname{median}(M_1,\ldots,M_k).\] If strictly more than half of the block means lie in \([a,b]\), every compatible median lies in \([a,b]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Median-of-means averages within blocks and takes a median, so a strict majority of accurate block means controls the result.
assumptions_latex: The blocks are nonempty and disjoint.
A median convention is declared when \(k\) is even.
knowledge_statements.title: Block Median-of-Means Construction

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-statistic robustification whose protection depends on the clean distribution and corruption model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For ordered observations \(Z_{(1)}\le\cdots\le Z_{(n)}\) and an integer \(0\le q<n/2\), define \[\widehat\mu_{\mathrm{trim}}=\frac{1}{n-2q}\sum_{i=q+1}^{n-q}Z_{(i)}.\] Trimming alone does not remove arbitrary corruptions that remain within the central order statistics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A symmetrically trimmed mean discards extreme observations, but arbitrary central corruptions may survive the trimming step.
assumptions_latex: The observations are real valued.

notation.meaning: number of observations removed from each tail

knowledge_statements.title: Symmetrically Trimmed Mean

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Population-Median Identification Radius under Gaussian Huber Contamination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contamination-dependent population location ambiguity for a Gaussian nominal family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=(1-\varepsilon)N(\mu,\sigma^2)+\varepsilon Q\), where \(0\le\varepsilon<1/2\), \(\sigma>0\), and \(Q\) is arbitrary. Every median \(m_F\) satisfies \[|m_F-\mu|\le \sigma\Phi^{-1}\!\left(\frac{1}{2(1-\varepsilon)}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under arbitrary Huber contamination of a Gaussian location model, every population median lies within a contamination-dependent radius of the nominal mean.
assumptions_latex: \(F=(1-\varepsilon)N(\mu,\sigma^2)+\varepsilon Q\).
\(0\le\varepsilon<1/2\), \(\sigma>0\), and \(Q\) is any probability law.

notation.meaning: a population median of the contaminated law

knowledge_statements.title: Population-Median Identification Radius under Gaussian Huber Contamination

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Empirical-Median Confidence under Gaussian Huber Contamination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample location bound displaying sampling and contamination contributions for an explicit nominal family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) be i.i.d. from \(F=(1-\varepsilon)N(\mu,\sigma^2)+\varepsilon Q\), where \(0\le\varepsilon<1/2\), \(\sigma>0\), and \(Q\) is arbitrary. Let \(\widehat m\) be an empirical median and put \(a=\sqrt{\log(2/\delta)/(2n)}\). If \(a<1/2-\varepsilon\), then \[\Pr\!\left(|\widehat m-\mu|\le \sigma\Phi^{-1}\!\left(\frac{1/2+a}{1-\varepsilon}\right)\right)\ge1-\delta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For Gaussian location feedback under stochastic Huber contamination, the empirical median has a high-probability radius containing both sampling and contamination effects.
assumptions_latex: \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) are i.i.d. from the displayed contaminated law.
\(0<\delta<1\) and \(\sqrt{\log(2/\delta)/(2n)}<1/2-\varepsilon\).
For even \(n\), the empirical median lies between the two central order statistics.
knowledge_statements.title: Empirical-Median Confidence under Gaussian Huber Contamination

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample confidence theorem for independent finite-variance scalar feedback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z_1,\ldots,Z_n\) be independent with common mean \(\mu\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(Z_i)\le\sigma^2\). Partition retained observations into \(k\) nonempty equal blocks of size \(m=\lfloor n/k\rfloor\), discarding any remainder, and let \(\widehat\mu_{\mathrm{MOM}}\) be a declared median of the block means. Then \[\Pr\!\left(|\widehat\mu_{\mathrm{MOM}}-\mu|>\frac{2\sigma}{\sqrt m}\right)\le e^{-k/8}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With independent observations of common mean and bounded variance, a block median-of-means estimator has exponentially small failure probability in the number of blocks.
assumptions_latex: The observations are independent, share mean \(\mu\), and each has variance at most \(\sigma^2\).
\(1\le k\le n\), all retained blocks have size \(m=\lfloor n/k\rfloor\), and remainder observations are discarded.
The median convention returns a value inside any interval containing strictly more than half of the block means.

notation.meaning: Number of retained observations per block.

knowledge_statements.title: Median-of-Means Confidence under Finite Variance
Robust-Feedback Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifiability boundary under unrestricted Huber contamination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a probability law \(P\), define its contamination neighborhood by \(\mathcal H_\varepsilon(P)=\{(1-\varepsilon)P+\varepsilon Q:Q\text{ is a probability law}\}\). If two nominal laws satisfy \(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P_0,P_1)\leq \varepsilon/(1-\varepsilon)\), then \(\mathcal H_\varepsilon(P_0)\cap\mathcal H_\varepsilon(P_1)\neq\varnothing\). Consequently, feedback alone cannot uniformly distinguish the two nominal models under unrestricted \(\varepsilon\)-contamination. Any Bayesian-optimization guarantee requiring such distinction must retain a contamination-dependent error floor or impose additional separation, structural, or contamination assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unrestricted contamination makes sufficiently close nominal feedback laws observationally indistinguishable, forcing an error floor unless extra structure or separation is assumed.
assumptions_latex: \(0\leq\varepsilon<1\).
The adversary may select any contaminating probability law.
\(d_{\mathrm{TV}}(P_0,P_1)\leq\varepsilon/(1-\varepsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal H_\varepsilon(P_0)\cap\mathcal H_\varepsilon(P_1)\neq\varnothing\), so uniform exact identification of \(P_0\) versus \(P_1\) is impossible from contaminated feedback.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the leaf, and the stated total-variation threshold is plausible. An authoritative locator is required for the contamination-neighborhood intersection result, while the Bayesian-optimization error-floor consequence also needs problem-specific support.

children.title: Noise Dependence-State Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Temporal, spatial, or simulation-induced dependence between observations.

children.title: Temporally Dependent Noise
children.top_down_role: Observation dependence induced across evaluation times.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Temporally dependent feedback that remains centered relative to the adaptive history.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\) contain the information available before \(x_t\) is selected, with \(x_t\) measurable relative to \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\). A dependent noise process may satisfy \[\mathbb E[\eta_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=0.\] For integrable products this implies \(\mathbb E[\eta_s\eta_t]=0\) for \(s<t\), but it does not imply independence. Concentration additionally requires declared conditional-tail or bounded-increment assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Temporal dependence is compatible with martingale-difference noise; orthogonality does not imply independence, and concentration needs additional tail control.
assumptions_latex: \(\eta_t\) is integrable and adapted after the t-th observation.
\(x_t\) is \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable.
Products used in the orthogonality statement are integrable.
knowledge_statements.title: Martingale-Difference Dependent Noise

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Variance of a Mean under Stationary Temporal Correlation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample precision of an average of consecutive correlated errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For second-order stationary errors with \(\operatorname{Var}(\eta_t)=\sigma^2\) and autocorrelation \(\rho_h\), \[\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^n\eta_t\right)=\frac{\sigma^2}{n}\left[1+2\sum_{h=1}^{n-1}\left(1-\frac hn\right)\rho_h\right].\] Thus the independent-replication value \(\sigma^2/n\) is valid only when the weighted autocorrelation contribution vanishes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Temporal autocorrelation changes the precision of a replicate mean, so nominal replicate count need not equal effective sample size.
assumptions_latex: \((\eta_t)\) is second-order stationary.
All displayed covariances are finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Variance of a Mean under Stationary Temporal Correlation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Test-Function Certificate for a Declared Innovation Kernel
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent measurable identities for verifying a declared one-step conditional kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The identity \(\mathcal L(\eta_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=K_{t,x_t}\) holds if and only if, for every bounded measurable \(\varphi\), \[\mathbb E[\varphi(\eta_t)\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=\int\varphi(z)K_{t,x_t}(dz)\quad\text{a.s.}\] Equivalently, for every bounded \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable \(G\), \[\mathbb E[G\varphi(\eta_t)]=\mathbb E\!\left[G\int\varphi(z)K_{t,x_t}(dz)\right].\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A declared innovation kernel is certified by equality of all bounded conditional test-function expectations.
assumptions_latex: The variables and kernels lie in measurable spaces supporting regular conditional laws.
The test functions are bounded and measurable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal L(\eta_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=K_{t,x_t}\iff\mathbb E[\varphi(\eta_t)\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]=K_{t,x_t}\varphi\ \text{for every bounded measurable }\varphi.

notation.meaning: integral of the test function against the innovation kernel

knowledge_statements.title: Test-Function Certificate for a Declared Innovation Kernel

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predictable-history criterion for absence of additional temporal dependence at one round.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_t\) be \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable and let \(K_{t,x}\) be a declared noise kernel. The round-t innovation is fresh relative to the adaptive history when, for every measurable set \(A\), \[\Pr(\eta_t\in A\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})=K_{t,x_t}(A)\quad\text{a.s.}\] Past feedback then affects the innovation law only through the declared predictable arguments of the kernel. If \(K_{t,x}\) is constant in \(t,x\), this reduces to independence of \(\eta_t\) from \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fresh innovation has a conditional law determined only by its declared round and predictable query, with no additional dependence on earlier realized feedback.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t\) is \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable.
Regular conditional distributions exist on the declared measurable spaces.
knowledge_statements.title: Fresh-Innovation Kernel Criterion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Martingale Differences Need Not Be Independent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit dependent, conditionally centered two-round noise construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\xi_1,\xi_2\) be independent Rademacher variables, choose \(0<a<1\), and set \(\eta_1=\xi_1\) and \(\eta_2=(1+a\xi_1)\xi_2\). Then \[\mathbb E[\eta_2\mid\eta_1]=0\quad\text{and}\quad\mathbb E[\eta_1\eta_2]=0,\] but \(|\eta_2|=1+a\eta_1\), so \(\eta_2\) is not independent of \(\eta_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A noise process can be a martingale difference and temporally uncorrelated while remaining dependent through its conditional scale.
assumptions_latex: \(\xi_1\) and \(\xi_2\) are independent and uniform on \(\{-1,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Martingale Differences Need Not Be Independent

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Temporally dependent subclass with a finite dependence horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A noise sequence \((\eta_t)_{t\in\mathbb Z}\) is \(m\)-dependent if, for every integer \(s\), \[\sigma(\eta_t:t\le s)\quad\text{and}\quad\sigma(\eta_t:t\ge s+m+1)\] are independent. For \(m>0\), dependence may persist within windows of length \(m+1\) but not beyond them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An m-dependent process may be dependent at nearby times but has independent past and future blocks separated by more than m lags.
assumptions_latex: The sequence is defined on a common probability space.
\(m\) is a nonnegative integer.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Range Temporal Dependence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General positive predicate relative to a declared predictable innovation kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_t\) be \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable and let \(K_{t,x}\) be the declared fresh-noise kernel. The noise process has temporal dependence beyond the declared predictable arguments if, for some \(t\) and measurable set \(A\), \[\Pr(\eta_t\in A\mid\mathcal F_{t-1})\ne K_{t,x_t}(A)\] on an event of positive probability. This predicate avoids conditioning on future adaptively selected queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Temporal dependence is present when past realized information changes the next-noise law beyond the round and query arguments declared by the innovation model.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t\) is measurable with respect to the pre-observation history.
Regular conditional laws exist on the declared measurable spaces.
The reference kernels \(K_{t,x}\) are specified before applying the predicate.

notation.meaning: Declared fresh-noise kernel for round t and query x.

knowledge_statements.title: Filtration-Based Temporal Dependence Predicate
Temporally Dependent Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional-law definition of time-dependent sequential feedback noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In observations \(Y_t=f(x_t)+\eta_t\), the noise is temporally dependent when its conditional joint law does not factor into one-step laws given the selected queries. Thus, for some horizon \(T\),
\[\mathcal L(\eta_{1:T}\mid x_{1:T})\neq\prod_{t=1}^{T}\mathcal L(\eta_t\mid x_t).\]
A common admissible subclass is conditionally centered dependent noise satisfying \(\mathbb E[\eta_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1},x_t]=0\), together with a specified mixing, martingale, or conditional-sub-Gaussian condition. Temporal dependence alone supplies none of these concentration properties; they must be assumed separately for confidence guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noise is temporally dependent when its joint conditional law does not factor across evaluations; concentration requires additional martingale, mixing, or tail assumptions.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t\) is selected using information available before observing \(Y_t\).
The conditional laws of \(\eta_{1:T}\) exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For some \(T\), \(\mathcal L(\eta_{1:T}\mid x_{1:T})\neq\prod_{t=1}^{T}\mathcal L(\eta_t\mid x_t)\).

source_refs.locator: 3.4.1 Adaptive Noise Cancellation and Disturbance Rejection p. 77

source_witnesses.locator: 3.4.1 Adaptive Noise Cancellation and Disturbance Rejection p. 77

This matters because conditioning only on the selected query sequence can interact subtly with adaptive query selection.

children.title: Spatially Dependent Noise
children.top_down_role: Observation dependence linked to locations in the search domain.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Spatial Covariance Does Not Imply Independence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Non-Gaussian boundary of covariance-based dependence diagnostics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U\) be uniform on \([-1,1]\), set \(\eta(x)=U\), and set \(\eta(x')=U^2-1/3\) at a distinct location. Then \(\operatorname{Cov}(\eta(x),\eta(x'))=\mathbb E[U^3]=0\), yet \(\eta(x')\) is a nonconstant function of \(\eta(x)\). Thus zero covariance implies independence only with additional structure such as joint Gaussianity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Non-Gaussian errors at distinct locations can be dependent despite zero covariance.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is uniform on \([-1,1]\).
knowledge_statements.title: Zero Spatial Covariance Does Not Imply Independence

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Variance of an Average Under Spatial Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effective replication precision with correlated errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite-second-moment errors with covariance matrix \(\Sigma_\eta\), \[\operatorname{Var}\!\left(\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\eta_i\right)=\frac1{n^2}\mathbf1^\top\Sigma_\eta\mathbf1.\] With common variance \(\sigma^2\) and common pairwise correlation \(\rho\), this is \(\sigma^2[1+(n-1)\rho]/n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The variance of an average depends on all cross-location covariances, so positive correlation reduces effective sample size.
assumptions_latex: All errors have finite second moments.
For the specialization, marginal variances and pairwise correlations are common.
knowledge_statements.title: Variance of an Average Under Spatial Dependence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-query second-order representation of cross-location observation dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For queried locations \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), a second-order noise field with covariance kernel \(C_\eta\) induces \[\Sigma_\eta=(C_\eta(x_i,x_j))_{i,j=1}^n\succeq0.\] If latent values have covariance \(K\) and are independent of the noise, then \(\operatorname{Cov}(Y\mid X)=K+\Sigma_\eta\). A diagonal noise covariance representation is exact precisely when sampled-location errors are pairwise uncorrelated; under joint Gaussianity this is equivalent to independence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spatial noise field induces a positive-semidefinite sampled covariance matrix added to latent covariance.
assumptions_latex: The noise field has finite second moments.
Latent objective variation is independent of observation noise.
knowledge_statements.title: Spatial Noise Covariance Matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence between covariance diagonality and independence for a finite Gaussian spatial-noise sample.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\eta(x_1),\ldots,\eta(x_n))\) be jointly Gaussian. The sampled errors are mutually independent if and only if \[C_\eta(x_i,x_j)=0\qquad(i\ne j).\] Thus a diagonal sampled covariance is an exact independent-noise representation within the Gaussian class; outside that class it implies only pairwise uncorrelatedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Jointly Gaussian spatial errors are independent exactly when every off-diagonal sampled noise covariance is zero.
assumptions_latex: The sampled noise vector is jointly Gaussian.
Second moments exist.
knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian Spatial Independence Criterion

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Latent–Noise Covariance Decomposition Is Not Identified by Observation Covariance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Second-order nonidentifiability when both latent variation and spatial noise covariance are unknown.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At sampled locations suppose \(Y=F+\eta\), \(F\perp\!\!\!\perp\eta\), \(\operatorname{Cov}(F)=K\succeq0\), and \(\operatorname{Cov}(\eta)=\Sigma_\eta\succeq0\). Observation covariance identifies only \(K+\Sigma_\eta\). For every symmetric \(A\) such that \(K+A\succeq0\) and \(\Sigma_\eta-A\succeq0\), the pair \((K+A,\Sigma_\eta-A)\) yields the same covariance of \(Y\). Additional replication, structural restrictions, or known covariance components are required to identify spatial-noise covariance separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Observed covariance alone generally cannot separate latent-objective covariance from spatially correlated measurement noise.
assumptions_latex: Latent values and observation errors are independent and have finite second moments.
Both covariance components are otherwise unknown.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Cov}(Y)=K+\Sigma_\eta\text{ does not generally identify }K\text{ and }\Sigma_\eta\text{ separately}.

notation.meaning: Admissible covariance transfer between the components.

knowledge_statements.title: Latent–Noise Covariance Decomposition Is Not Identified by Observation Covariance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributional definition of spatial dependence, independent of second-moment availability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{\eta(x):x\in\mathcal X\}\) be a jointly defined noise field. It is spatially dependent on \(\mathcal X\) if some distinct \(x,x'\) satisfy \[\mathcal L(\eta(x),\eta(x'))\ne\mathcal L(\eta(x))\otimes\mathcal L(\eta(x')).\] When second moments exist, \(\operatorname{Cov}(\eta(x),\eta(x'))\ne0\) is sufficient but not necessary for this dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spatial noise is dependent when errors at some distinct locations have a nonproduct joint law; nonzero covariance detects dependence but zero covariance need not exclude it.
assumptions_latex: The noise variables are jointly defined over the query domain.
Covariance statements additionally require finite second moments.

notation.meaning: observation error associated with location x

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Location Distributional Dependence
Spatially Dependent Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cross-location dependence in observation errors over the query domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\eta(x)\) denote the error associated with evaluating location \(x\in\mathcal X\). The noise is spatially dependent if there exist distinct \(x,x'\in\mathcal X\) for which the joint law does not factor:
\[\mathcal L(\eta(x),\eta(x'))\neq\mathcal L(\eta(x))\otimes\mathcal L(\eta(x')).\]
When second moments exist, nonzero covariance \(C_\eta(x,x')=\operatorname{Cov}(\eta(x),\eta(x'))\) is sufficient for spatial dependence. Repeated observations therefore require a joint noise covariance or an equivalent dependence model; an independent diagonal likelihood is generally misspecified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spatially dependent errors at distinct query locations have a nonproduct joint law; with finite second moments, nonzero cross-location covariance is sufficient.
assumptions_latex: \(\eta(x)\) is defined jointly over \(x\in\mathcal X\).
Covariance claims additionally require finite second moments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist \(x\neq x'\) such that \(\mathcal L(\eta(x),\eta(x'))\neq\mathcal L(\eta(x))\otimes\mathcal L(\eta(x'))\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: dependence is defined by failure of factorization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and covariance qualification are mathematically standard and fit the leaf, but the record has no spatial-noise-specific citation with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Generalized Least-Squares Aggregation of Spatially Correlated Replicates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed aggregation assumes a common latent mean and therefore is not intrinsic to cross-location Bayesian-optimization noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(Y=\mu\mathbf1+\eta\), \(\mathbb E\eta=0\), and \(\operatorname{Cov}(\eta)=\Sigma\succ0\). The generalized least-squares weights are \(a^*=\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf1/(\mathbf1^\top\Sigma^{-1}\mathbf1)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: GLS aggregates correlated observations of a common mean, an assumption not generally satisfied by evaluations at distinct optimization locations.
assumptions_latex: All observations share the same latent mean \(\mu\).
\(\Sigma\) is known and positive definite.
knowledge_statements.title: Generalized Least-Squares Aggregation of Spatially Correlated Replicates

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf owns cross-location dependence, sampled covariance representations, effective replication precision, Gaussian criteria, and covariance counterexamples. The proposed GLS record is deferred because its common-mean estimation problem is not intrinsic to distinct-location optimization feedback. Temporal dependence and hidden simulator dynamics are excluded to sibling leaves.

children.title: Stateful Simulator Noise
children.top_down_role: Feedback affected by persistent or evolving simulator state.

knowledge_statements.title: Stateful Simulator Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hidden-state observation model for sequential simulator evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A simulator has stateful noise if there is a latent state process \((S_t)\) such that, conditionally on the history and query,
\[S_{t+1}\sim K_{x_t}(S_t,\cdot),\qquad Y_t\sim G_{x_t}(S_t,\cdot),\]
and the observation law depends nontrivially on \(S_t\). Marginalizing the unobserved state generally makes \((Y_t)\) history-dependent even when the transition and emission innovations are conditionally independent. Independent-noise Bayesian-optimization guarantees apply only after conditioning on, resetting, observing, or otherwise controlling the state sufficiently to recover their stipulated feedback assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stateful simulator carries latent state between evaluations; state-dependent transitions and outputs induce history-dependent observation noise after the state is marginalized.
assumptions_latex: \((S_t,Y_t)\) admits the displayed controlled transition-emission representation.
The query \(x_t\) is chosen before \(Y_t\) is observed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal L(Y_t\mid x_t,Y_{1:t-1},x_{1:t-1})\) may depend on the full history through the conditional law of \(S_t\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient condition eliminating dependence carried by persistent simulator state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose each evaluation starts with an independent reset \(S_t\sim\mu_{x_t}\), followed by \(Y_t\sim G_{x_t}(S_t,\cdot)\), and the reset and emission innovations are conditionally independent across evaluations given \(x_{1:T}\). Then \[\mathcal L(Y_{1:T}\mid x_{1:T})=\prod_{t=1}^T\int G_{x_t}(s,\cdot)\,\mu_{x_t}(ds).\] A partial or history-dependent reset does not establish this factorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent exact resets remove state-carried dependence; partial or history-dependent resets do not certify independent feedback.
assumptions_latex: Each evaluation uses a fresh state drawn from \(\mu_{x_t}\).
Reset and emission innovations are conditionally independent across evaluations given the queries.

notation.meaning: post-reset state law at query x

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Reset Criterion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Controlled-Markov representation obtained by retaining the simulator state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(S_t\) is observed before \(x_t\) is selected and, conditionally on \((S_t,x_t)\), \(S_{t+1}\sim K_{x_t}(S_t,\cdot)\), \(Y_t\sim G_{x_t}(S_t,\cdot)\), with transition and emission conditionally independent. Then \[\mathcal L(S_{t+1},Y_t\mid S_{1:t},Y_{1:t-1},x_{1:t})=K_{x_t}(S_t,dS_{t+1})G_{x_t}(S_t,dY_t).\] The augmented state is controlled Markov, but this alone does not make the observations independent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Observing and retaining the simulator state restores a controlled-Markov representation, not independent observation noise.
assumptions_latex: The next-state and emission laws depend on the history only through \((S_t,x_t)\).
The transition and emission are conditionally independent given \((S_t,x_t)\).
\(S_t\) is observed before selection of \(x_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: S_t\text{ is a sufficient controlled state for }(S_{t+1},Y_t).
knowledge_statements.title: Observed-State Markovization

children.title: Finite-Domain Confidence Control
children.top_down_role: Uniform control over finite alternatives and finite discretizations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unadjusted Marginal Levels Do Not Give Familywise Coverage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicity boundary for a finite confidence family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_1,\ldots,E_K\) be independent events with \(\Pr(E_i)=1-\alpha\). For \(K>1\), \(\Pr(\bigcap_{i=1}^K E_i)=(1-\alpha)^K<1-\alpha\). Thus applying level \(\alpha\) separately to every alternative does not provide level-\(\alpha\) simultaneous coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nominal marginal intervals lose familywise coverage when reused over multiple alternatives.
assumptions_latex: The events are independent with marginal probability \(1-\alpha\).

notation.meaning: number of alternatives or confidence statements

knowledge_statements.title: Unadjusted Marginal Levels Do Not Give Familywise Coverage

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniform error allocation over a finite index set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be finite, let \(w_i>0\) satisfy \(\sum_{i\in I}w_i\le1\), and suppose \(\Pr(E_i^c)\le\delta w_i\) for every \(i\in I\). Then \(\Pr(\bigcap_{i\in I}E_i)\ge1-\delta\). Independence is unnecessary, and \(w_i=1/|I|\) gives uniform allocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite confidence budget may be divided unequally among alternatives while retaining familywise control.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite and \(0<\delta<1\).
\(w_i>0\) and \(\sum_iw_i\le1\).
\(\Pr(E_i^c)\le\delta w_i\) for every i.

notation.meaning: fraction of the total error budget assigned to index i

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Finite Bonferroni Control
Finite-Domain Confidence Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Union-bound confidence control over finitely many locations and times.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal X\) be finite and suppose that, for every \(t\leq T\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\), an estimator \(\mu_{t-1}(x)\) and radius \(r_t(x,\alpha)\) satisfy
\[\Pr\!\left(\lvert f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)\rvert>r_t(x,\alpha)\right)\leq\alpha.\]
Then, with \(\alpha=\delta/(T\lvert\mathcal X\rvert)\), the union bound yields
\[\Pr\!\left(\forall t\leq T,\ \forall x\in\mathcal X:\ \lvert f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)\rvert\leq r_t(x,\alpha)\right)\geq1-\delta.\]
No independence among the individual deviation events is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise confidence bounds become simultaneous over a finite domain and finite horizon by assigning each location-time pair failure probability delta divided by their count.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\delta<1\), \(T\in\mathbb N\), and \(0<\lvert\mathcal X\rvert<\infty\).
The stated marginal deviation inequality holds for every location-time pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With probability at least \(1-\delta\), all \(T\lvert\mathcal X\rvert\) confidence inequalities hold simultaneously.

notation.meaning: pointwise confidence radius at failure level alpha

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind fits this confidence-control leaf, and the finite union-bound statement is correct without independence. No cited source with an inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Continuous-Domain Confidence Control
children.top_down_role: Extension of confidence control through regularity and domain coverings.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Net Coverage Without Regularity Is Insufficient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of finite-net interpolation without a controlled modulus of continuity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any finite \(S\subset[0,1]\), choose \(x_0\notin S\), set \(f(x_0)=1\) and \(f(x)=0\) otherwise, and let \(\mu\equiv0\). Then \(\max_{z\in S}|f(z)-\mu(z)|=0\), while \(\sup_{x\in[0,1]}|f(x)-\mu(x)|=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A function can agree with its estimator at every net point and differ between them, so net-point coverage alone does not control a continuous domain.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a finite subset of \([0,1]\).
No continuity or modulus-of-continuity assumption is imposed.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Net Coverage Without Regularity Is Insufficient

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric quantities governing finite reductions of a continuous domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a metric space \((\mathcal X,d)\), the covering number \(N(\rho,\mathcal X,d)\) is the minimum cardinality of \(S\subseteq\mathcal X\) satisfying \(\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}\inf_{z\in S}d(x,z)\le\rho\). Its logarithm is the metric entropy at resolution \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The covering number is the smallest number of radius-rho balls needed to cover the domain; its logarithm is metric entropy.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal X,d)\) is a metric space.
knowledge_statements.title: Covering Numbers and Metric Entropy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hölder variant of regularity-based continuous-domain confidence extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\) be a finite \(\rho\)-net of \((\mathcal X,d)\). Suppose \(|f(x)-f(z)|\le L_f d(x,z)^\alpha\) and \(|\mu(x)-\mu(z)|\le L_\mu d(x,z)^\alpha\), where \(0<\alpha\le1\). If \(|f(z)-\mu(z)|\le r(z)\) simultaneously for all \(z\in S\), then \(|f(x)-\mu(x)|\le r(\pi(x))+(L_f+L_\mu)\rho^\alpha\) for every \(x\), where \(d(x,\pi(x))\le\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-net confidence extends uniformly under Hölder regularity, with a penalty proportional to the mesh radius raised to the Hölder exponent.
assumptions_latex: \(S\) is a finite \(\rho\)-net.
\(f\) and \(\mu\) are Hölder continuous with common exponent \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.title: Hölder Covering-Net Extension
Continuous-Domain Confidence Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covering-net extension from pointwise to uniform continuous-domain confidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\mathcal X,d)\) admit a finite \(\rho\)-net \(N_\rho\). Suppose \(f\) and \(\mu\) are respectively \(L_f\)- and \(L_\mu\)-Lipschitz, and radii \(r(z)\) satisfy, simultaneously for all \(z\in N_\rho\), \(\lvert f(z)-\mu(z)\rvert\leq r(z)\). For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), choose \(\pi(x)\in N_\rho\) with \(d(x,\pi(x))\leq\rho\). Then
\[\lvert f(x)-\mu(x)\rvert\leq r(\pi(x))+(L_f+L_\mu)\rho\qquad\text{for every }x\in\mathcal X.\]
Thus a finite-net confidence event extends uniformly, with an explicit discretization penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Confidence on a finite covering net extends to the continuous domain when the target and estimator are Lipschitz, at an additive regularity penalty.
assumptions_latex: \(N_\rho\) is a finite \(\rho\)-net of \((\mathcal X,d)\).
\(f\) and \(\mu\) are Lipschitz with constants \(L_f\) and \(L_\mu\).

notation.meaning: selected net point within rho of x

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: covering-net argument using Lipschitz continuity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem correctly states a Lipschitz covering-net extension and fits the continuous-domain confidence leaf, but it lacks a citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Self-Normalized Kernel Confidence
children.top_down_role: Kernelized concentration for adaptively selected observations.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: On Kernelized Multi-armed Bandits
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Self-normalized concentration and improved GP-UCB analysis
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: On Kernelized Multi-armed Bandits

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assumption failures outside the standard kernel confidence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A self-normalized kernel band calibrated under \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B\) and conditionally \(R\)-sub-Gaussian noise has its stated guarantee only under those conditions. If \(f\notin\mathcal H_k\), \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}>B\), or the declared conditional sub-Gaussian inequality fails, the theorem does not control the resulting approximation bias or tail probability; posterior computation alone does not restore coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Standard kernel confidence guarantees do not extend automatically beyond the assumed RKHS ball or conditional sub-Gaussian noise model.
assumptions_latex: The claimed band was calibrated using RKHS radius \(B\) and conditional sub-Gaussian scale \(R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Violation of either calibration assumption removes the stated theorem guarantee unless an explicit misspecification or robust-noise term is supplied.
knowledge_statements.title: Boundary of RKHS Self-Normalized Coverage

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-matrix quantities underlying kernelized self-normalized concentration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For queried points \(x_1,\ldots,x_t\), let \(K_t=(k(x_i,x_j))_{i,j\le t}\), \(k_t(x)=(k(x_1,x),\ldots,k(x_t,x))^\top\), and \(\lambda>0\). Kernel ridge regression uses \(\mu_t(x)=k_t(x)^\top(K_t+\lambda I)^{-1}y_{1:t}\) and the regularized predictive geometry \(\sigma_t^2(x)=k(x,x)-k_t(x)^\top(K_t+\lambda I)^{-1}k_t(x)\). The associated accumulated complexity is represented by \(\log\det(I+\lambda^{-1}K_t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Kernel confidence is expressed through regularized Gram-matrix prediction geometry and a log-determinant complexity term.
assumptions_latex: \(k\) is positive semidefinite.
\(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu_t\), \(\sigma_t\), and \(\log\det(I+\lambda^{-1}K_t)\) provide the finite-matrix representation used in self-normalized kernel bounds.

notation.meaning: kernel Gram matrix of queried points
regularized latent prediction standard deviation under the stated convention

knowledge_statements.title: Kernel Self-Normalization and Log-Determinant Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact feature-space normalization for predictable kernel observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k(x,x')=\langle\phi(x),\phi(x')\rangle_{\mathcal H}\), \(V_{t-1}=\lambda I+\sum_{s<t}\phi(x_s)\otimes\phi(x_s)\), and \(\widehat f_{t-1}(x)=\langle V_{t-1}^{-1}\sum_{s<t}Y_s\phi(x_s),\phi(x)\rangle\). If \(f(x)=\langle\theta,\phi(x)\rangle\), \(\|\theta\|\le B\), \(x_t\) is predictable, and \(\eta_t=Y_t-f(x_t)\) is conditionally \(R\)-sub-Gaussian, then, with probability at least \(1-\delta\), simultaneously for every \(t\ge1\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\), \[|f(x)-\widehat f_{t-1}(x)|\le\left[\sqrt\lambda B+R\sqrt{2\log(1/\delta)+\log\det(I+\lambda^{-1}K_{t-1})}\right]\|\phi(x)\|_{V_{t-1}^{-1}}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed RKHS norm bound and conditional sub-Gaussian noise yield one confidence event valid at every time and every input, with an explicit log-determinant radius.
assumptions_latex: \(\lambda>0\), \(0<\delta<1\), and \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B\).
\(x_t\) is \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable.
\(\mathbb E[\exp(u\eta_t)\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\le\exp(u^2R^2/2)\) for every \(u\in\mathbb R\).

notation.meaning: Gram matrix of the first t-1 queried inputs

knowledge_statements.title: Time-Uniform Self-Normalized RKHS Confidence
Self-Normalized Kernel Confidence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: RKHS confidence sequence for predictable kernelized observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\in\mathcal H_k\) satisfy \(\lVert f\rVert_{\mathcal H_k}\leq B\), let \(x_t\) be \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable, and observe \(Y_t=f(x_t)+\eta_t\), where \(\eta_t\) is conditionally \(R\)-sub-Gaussian. For kernel-ridge posterior mean \(\mu_{t-1}\) and standard deviation \(\sigma_{t-1}\) with regularization \(\lambda>0\), a self-normalized kernel concentration inequality gives, with probability at least \(1-\delta\), simultaneously for all \(t\geq1\) and \(x\in\mathcal X\),
\[\lvert f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)\rvert\leq\beta_t\sigma_{t-1}(x),\]
where \(\beta_t\) is determined by \(B,R,\lambda,\delta\) and the log-determinant information accumulated before time \(t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under an RKHS norm bound and conditionally sub-Gaussian noise, self-normalized concentration gives confidence bands valid for all times and adaptively selected queries.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in\mathcal H_k\) and \(\lVert f\rVert_{\mathcal H_k}\leq B\).
\(x_t\) is predictable and \(\eta_t\) is conditionally \(R\)-sub-Gaussian.
Kernel-ridge regression uses fixed regularization \(\lambda>0\).

notation.meaning: kernel-ridge posterior mean and standard deviation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind is appropriate, but the all-time, all-domain confidence statement depends on the precise kernel-ridge normalization and an explicit formula for the confidence multiplier. An authoritative theorem locator is required to determine whether the stated assumptions and scope are sufficient.

children.title: Anytime Confidence Control
children.top_down_role: Confidence control compatible with random or data-dependent horizons.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Coverage Does Not Survive Repeated Monitoring
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-time coverage failure under repeated data-dependent monitoring.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let independent events \(F_t\) satisfy \(\Pr(F_t)=\delta\), and let the time-\(t\) confidence statement fail exactly on \(F_t\). Each statement has coverage \(1-\delta\), but \(\Pr(\exists t\ge1:F_t)=1\). Hence the stopping time \(\tau=\inf\{t:F_t\}\) exposes failure almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated monitoring of unadjusted fixed-time confidence statements can make eventual failure certain.
assumptions_latex: The events \((F_t)\) are independent and satisfy \(\Pr(F_t)=\delta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pr(\exists t:F_t)=1\), so fixed-time coverage does not imply coverage at \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Coverage Does Not Survive Repeated Monitoring

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition and stopping-time characterization of anytime-valid confidence sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A data-measurable sequence \((C_t)_{t\ge1}\) is a \((1-\delta)\)-confidence sequence for \(\theta\) if \(\Pr_\theta(\forall t\ge1:\theta\in C_t)\ge1-\delta\). This implies \(\Pr_\theta(\theta\in C_\tau)\ge1-\delta\) for every almost surely finite stopping time \(\tau\). Conversely, validity at every bounded stopping time implies simultaneous coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A confidence sequence covers at every time on one event; equivalently, it remains valid under every bounded stopping rule and consequently under every almost surely finite stopping rule.
assumptions_latex: Each \(C_t\) is measurable with respect to the time-\(t\) information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pr_\theta(\forall t:\theta\in C_t)\ge1-\delta\) and \(\Pr_\theta(\theta\in C_\tau)\ge1-\delta\) for every almost surely finite \(\tau\).

notation.meaning: confidence set available at time t

knowledge_statements.title: Confidence Sequences and Stopping-Time Validity

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ville Construction from a Test Supermartingale
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Martingale construction of an anytime-valid confidence sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((E_t)_{t\ge0}\) be a nonnegative supermartingale under the null, with \(E_0\le1\). Ville's inequality gives \(\Pr(\sup_{t\ge0}E_t\ge\delta^{-1})\le\delta\). Therefore, for a parameter-indexed family \(E_t(\theta)\), the inverted sets \(C_t=\{\theta:E_t(\theta)<\delta^{-1}\}\) satisfy \(\Pr_\theta(\forall t:\theta\in C_t)\ge1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Thresholding a nonnegative test supermartingale and inverting the resulting sequential tests produces an anytime-valid confidence sequence.
assumptions_latex: \((E_t)\) is nonnegative and adapted.
\(\mathbb E[E_t\mid\mathcal F_{t-1}]\le E_{t-1}\) and \(E_0\le1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pr(\sup_tE_t\ge1/\delta)\le\delta\), and the inverted sets have simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\delta\).

notation.meaning: confidence set obtained by test inversion

knowledge_statements.title: Ville Construction from a Test Supermartingale
Anytime Confidence Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Summable-error construction for confidence validity at every time.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose that for each deterministic \(t\geq1\), an event \(E_t(\alpha)\) satisfies \(\Pr(E_t(\alpha)^c)\leq\alpha\). Let \((\alpha_t)_{t\geq1}\) be deterministic, positive, and satisfy \(\sum_{t=1}^{\infty}\alpha_t\leq\delta\). Then
\[\Pr\!\left(\bigcap_{t=1}^{\infty}E_t(\alpha_t)\right)\geq1-\delta.\]
Consequently, on this single event every associated confidence statement remains valid at any almost surely finite stopping time \(\tau\). One admissible allocation is \(\alpha_t=6\delta/(\pi^2t^2)\). Independence across times and independence of \(\tau\) from the data are unnecessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocating a summable sequence of failure probabilities produces confidence statements valid simultaneously at all times and therefore at arbitrary finite stopping times.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\delta<1\) and \(\sum_{t\geq1}\alpha_t\leq\delta\).
For every deterministic \(t\), \(\Pr(E_t(\alpha_t)^c)\leq\alpha_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pr(\forall t\geq1:E_t(\alpha_t))\geq1-\delta\), and hence \(E_\tau(\alpha_\tau)\) holds on that event for every almost surely finite stopping time \(\tau\).

notation.meaning: time-t confidence event with failure level alpha

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: countable union bound with summable error allocation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is a correct countable-union construction and appropriately supports arbitrary almost surely finite stopping times on the simultaneous event. It nevertheless has no citation with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Mutual-Information Capacity
children.top_down_role: Information-theoretic representation of sequential learnability under a kernel model.

assumptions_latex: The observation model is jointly Gaussian with conditionally independent Gaussian measurement errors.
Designs are finite ordered multisets, so repeated queries, extensions, and partitions are admissible.

notation.meaning: maximum mutual information obtainable from T noisy evaluations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budget algebra for fixed-design Gaussian-process information capacity with ordered-multiset designs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\gamma_T=\sup_{|A|=T}I(f;Y_A)\) for noisy Gaussian-process observations, with repeated points permitted. Then \(\gamma_0=0\), \(\gamma_T\le\gamma_{T+1}\), and for all integers \(S,T\ge0\),
\[\gamma_{S+T}\le\gamma_S+\gamma_T.\]
Consequently, \(\gamma_T\le T\gamma_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximum information gain is nondecreasing and subadditive in the evaluation budget, and therefore grows at most linearly without further kernel structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotonicity and Subadditivity of Maximum Information Gain
knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity and Subadditivity of Maximum Information Gain
Mutual-Information Capacity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximum information gain for Gaussian-process observations with homoscedastic noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\sim\operatorname{GP}(0,k)\), and for a design \(A=\{x_1,\ldots,x_T\}\subseteq\mathcal X\) observe \(Y_A=f_A+\xi_A\) with \(\xi_A\sim\mathcal N(0,\lambda I)\), independent of \(f\). The order-\(T\) mutual-information capacity is
\[\gamma_T:=\sup_{A\subseteq\mathcal X,\,\lvert A\rvert=T} I(f_A;Y_A)=\frac12\sup_{\lvert A\rvert=T}\log\det\!\left(I+\lambda^{-1}K_A\right).\]
Repeated design points may instead be represented by ordered multisets. The quantity depends on the kernel, domain, noise variance, and evaluation budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximum information gain is the largest mutual information obtainable from T noisy Gaussian-process evaluations, equivalently one half of a kernel log determinant.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is a centered Gaussian process with covariance kernel \(k\).
Observation noise is independent Gaussian with covariance \(\lambda I\), where \(\lambda>0\).

notation.meaning: kernel Gram matrix on design A
maximum information gain at budget T

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the leaf and the Gaussian log-determinant identity is standard. A source locator is required, particularly to establish whether designs are sets, sequences, or multisets when repeated evaluations are allowed.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Maximum information gain under noisy Gaussian-process observations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mutual-information definition of information capacity for homoskedastic Gaussian observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\sim\mathcal{GP}(\mu,K)\), and observe \(\mathbf y=f(\mathbf x)+\boldsymbol\varepsilon\) with independent \(\boldsymbol\varepsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma_n^2I)\), \(\sigma_n>0\). If \(\Sigma=K(\mathbf x,\mathbf x)\), then \(I(\mathbf y;f)=H[\mathbf y]-H[\mathbf y\mid f]=\frac12\log|I+\sigma_n^{-2}\Sigma|\). The information capacity, or maximum information gain, from \(\tau\) observations is \(\gamma_\tau=\sup_{|\mathbf x|=\tau}I(\mathbf y;f)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a Gaussian process observed with independent homoskedastic Gaussian noise, the information gained about the function is one half of the log determinant of the noise-normalized covariance matrix. The information capacity gamma_tau is the supremum of this mutual information over all designs containing tau observations.
assumptions_latex: f\sim\mathcal{GP}(\mu,K)
\mathbf y=f(\mathbf x)+\boldsymbol\varepsilon
\boldsymbol\varepsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma_n^2I)
\sigma_n>0
|\mathbf x|=\tau
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: I(\mathbf y;f)=\frac12\log|I+\sigma_n^{-2}K(\mathbf x,\mathbf x)|,\qquad \gamma_\tau=\sup_{|\mathbf x|=\tau}I(\mathbf y;f).

children.title: Posterior-Variance Information Bridge
children.top_down_role: The named analytical bridge between accumulated posterior uncertainty and information capacity.

assumptions_latex: Observation noise is independent Gaussian with variance \(\lambda>0\).
\(0\le\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\le\kappa^2<\infty\) for every t.
The design and information-capacity conventions are compatible.

notation.meaning: uniform upper bound on latent posterior variance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variance-information inequality without requiring signal variance to be no larger than noise variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(0\le\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\le\kappa^2\) and observation noise has variance \(\lambda>0\). Then
\[\sum_{t=1}^T\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\le \frac{2\kappa^2}{\log(1+\kappa^2/\lambda)}I(f_{1:T};Y_{1:T})\le \frac{2\kappa^2}{\log(1+\kappa^2/\lambda)}\gamma_T.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform posterior-variance bound converts accumulated posterior variance into information gain with an explicit constant, without assuming variance is below the noise level.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Variance Information Conversion
Posterior-Variance Information Bridge
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential identity linking posterior variances to Gaussian information gain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the Gaussian-process observation model with noise variance \(\lambda>0\), let \(x_1,\ldots,x_T\) be a fixed ordered design and let \(\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\) be the latent posterior variance before observing \(Y_t\). Then
\[I(f_{1:T};Y_{1:T})=\frac12\sum_{t=1}^{T}\log\!\left(1+\lambda^{-1}\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\right).\]
If \(\lambda^{-1}\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\leq1\) for all \(t\), then
\[\sum_{t=1}^{T}\lambda^{-1}\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\leq\frac{2}{\log 2}I(f_{1:T};Y_{1:T})\leq\frac{2}{\log 2}\gamma_T.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Gaussian information gain equals a sum of logarithmic posterior-variance reductions and therefore controls accumulated normalized posterior variance.
assumptions_latex: The prior is Gaussian with kernel \(k\), and observation noise is independent \(\mathcal N(0,\lambda)\).
For the linear variance bound, \(\lambda^{-1}\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\leq1\) for every \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accumulated normalized posterior variance is at most \((2/\log 2)\gamma_T\) under the stated normalization.

notation.meaning: latent posterior variance before observation t
maximum information gain at budget T

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the named analytical bridge, and the identity and normalized-variance inequality are internally consistent under the stated bound. The exact posterior-variance convention and constant require an authoritative lemma or theorem locator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Posterior predictive variance bounded by information capacity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bridge from accumulated sequential predictive variance to maximum information gain under uniformly bounded prior variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a sequence of \(\tau\) observation locations selected by an optimization policy, and let \(\sigma_i\) be the predictive standard deviation immediately before observing the response at the \(i\)-th selected location. Under independent Gaussian observation noise with scale \(\sigma_n>0\), \(I(\mathbf y;f)=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^{\tau}\log(1+\sigma_i^2/\sigma_n^2)\). If \(0<K(x,x)\le M\) for every \(x\), then \(\sum_{i=1}^{\tau}\sigma_i^2\le c\gamma_\tau\), where \(c=2M/\log(1+\sigma_n^{-2}M)\); consequently, \(\sum_{i=1}^{\tau}\sigma_i^2=\mathcal O(\gamma_\tau)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mutual information along a selected observation sequence decomposes into log terms involving the predictive variances. When the prior pointwise variance is uniformly bounded, accumulated predictive variance is at most a fixed constant times maximum information gain.
assumptions_latex: \sigma_n>0
0<K(x,x)\le M\quad\forall x
\{x_i\}_{i=1}^{\tau}\text{ is a sequence selected by an optimization policy}
\sigma_i^2\text{ is the predictive variance immediately before observing at }x_i

children.title: Adaptive-Design Information Gain
children.top_down_role: Information accumulation when evaluation locations depend on earlier observations.

assumptions_latex: \(U\perp f\).
\(X_t\) is measurable with respect to the pre-observation history \(H_{t-1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: I(f;Y_{1:T}\mid X_{1:T},U)\text{ need not equal }I(f;X_{1:T},Y_{1:T}\mid U).

notation.meaning: policy randomization independent of the latent function
information available when query t is selected

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning boundary for information identities under observation-dependent query selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(U\) be policy randomization independent of \(f\), let \(H_{t-1}=\sigma(U,X_1,Y_1,\ldots,X_{t-1},Y_{t-1})\), and suppose \(X_t\) is \(H_{t-1}\)-measurable. Then \(X_{1:T}\) can encode earlier observations, so in general
\[I(f;Y_{1:T}\mid X_{1:T},U)\ne I(f;X_{1:T},Y_{1:T}\mid U).\]
For example, if \(X_2=a\) exactly when \(Y_1\ge0\) and \(X_2=b\) otherwise, then \(X_2\) reveals the event \(\{Y_1\ge0\}\). Thus the adaptive-transcript chain rule cannot be replaced by mutual information conditional on the completed realized design.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adaptive design can encode past observations, so information conditional on the final design generally differs from information in the complete adaptive transcript.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Realized-Design Conditioning Is Not Transcript Information
knowledge_statements.title: Realized-Design Conditioning Is Not Transcript Information

assumptions_latex: \(U\) is independent of the latent process and observation noise.
\(X_t\) is \(H_{t-1}\)-measurable, where \(H_{t-1}=\sigma(U,X_1,Y_1,\ldots,X_{t-1},Y_{t-1})\).
The prior is Gaussian and the observation errors are independent \(\mathcal N(0,\lambda)\) with \(\lambda>0\).
\(\gamma_T\) is defined over ordered designs or multisets compatible with repeated realized queries.

notation.meaning: adaptive query-observation transcript through round T
latent posterior variance before round t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correct chain rule and capacity comparison for predictable adaptive Gaussian-process queries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal T_T=(X_1,Y_1,\ldots,X_T,Y_T)\). If \(X_t\) is chosen predictably from \(H_{t-1}\), then query selection adds no conditional information once the preceding history is known, and
\[I(f;\mathcal T_T\mid U)=\sum_{t=1}^T I(f;Y_t\mid H_{t-1})=\frac12\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbb E\!\left[\log\!\left(1+\lambda^{-1}\sigma_{t-1}^2(X_t)\right)\right].\]
For every realized ordered design the corresponding Gaussian log determinant is at most the compatible order-\(T\) capacity, hence \(I(f;\mathcal T_T\mid U)\le\gamma_T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For predictable adaptive queries, transcript information is the sum of expected one-step log posterior-variance gains and is bounded by a capacity defined over compatible ordered designs.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Transcript Chain Rule
Adaptive-Design Information Gain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional information accumulation for predictable Gaussian-process designs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H_{t-1}=\sigma(x_1,Y_1,\ldots,x_{t-1},Y_{t-1})\), and let \(x_t\) be \(H_{t-1}\)-measurable. Under a Gaussian-process prior and independent Gaussian observation noise of variance \(\lambda\), the information revealed by the adaptive transcript satisfies the chain rule
\[I(f;Y_{1:T}\mid x_{1:T})=\sum_{t=1}^{T}I(f;Y_t\mid H_{t-1},x_t)=\frac12\sum_{t=1}^{T}\mathbb E\!\left[\log\!\left(1+\lambda^{-1}\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\right)\right].\]
Thus adaptive sampling accumulates information through the posterior variance at each predictable query; comparison with \(\gamma_T\) requires matching the conditioning and design convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For predictable adaptive queries, transcript information decomposes into expected one-step log posterior-variance gains; capacity comparison must use a compatible adaptive-design convention.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t\) is measurable with respect to the pre-observation history \(H_{t-1}\).
The prior is Gaussian and observation noise is independent \(\mathcal N(0,\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Information accumulation equals the sum of expected conditional gains \(\frac12\log(1+\lambda^{-1}\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t))\).

notation.meaning: adaptive history before query t is observed
posterior variance at the adaptive query

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the leaf, but the displayed equality between information conditional on the realized adaptive design and the sum of history-conditional gains is not automatic: adaptive locations encode earlier observations, and conditioning on the full realized design can change the chain-rule terms. A precise transcript formulation and authoritative source are required before the mathematical statement can be fixed.

children.title: Kernel Capacity Specializations

children.title: Squared-Exponential Kernel Capacity
children.top_down_role: Information-capacity behavior for infinitely smooth stationary kernels.

knowledge_statements.title: Squared-Exponential Kernel Capacity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical maximum-information-gain bound on a compact convex finite-dimensional domain with fixed Gaussian observation noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\subset\mathbb R^d\) be compact and convex, let \(k(x,x')=\exp(-\lVert x-x'\rVert_2^2/(2\ell^2))\) with \(\ell>0\), and let observations have independent noise \(N(0,\sigma^2)\), where \(\sigma^2>0\). For \(A=\{x_1,\ldots,x_T\}\subset D\), write \(K_A=(k(x_i,x_j))_{i,j=1}^T\) and define \(\gamma_T=\max_{|A|=T}\frac12\log\det(I_T+\sigma^{-2}K_A)\). Then, for fixed \(D,d,\ell,\sigma\), \[\gamma_T=O\!\left((\log T)^{d+1}\right)\qquad(T\to\infty).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A squared-exponential kernel on a compact convex d-dimensional domain has maximum information gain growing at most polylogarithmically, with exponent d+1.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb R^d\) is compact and convex.
\(k\) is squared-exponential with fixed length scale \(\ell>0\).
Observation noise is independent Gaussian with fixed variance \(\sigma^2>0\).

notation.meaning: Gram matrix of the selected design points
maximum mutual information obtainable from T noisy observations

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposal asserts a logarithmic-power lower bound for squared-exponential information capacity, but no source was supplied to verify the exponent and domain generality.

children.title: Matérn Kernel Capacity
children.top_down_role: Information-capacity behavior indexed by finite kernel smoothness.

knowledge_statements.title: Matérn Kernel Capacity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical finite-smoothness maximum-information-gain bound for a Matérn covariance on a compact convex Euclidean domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\subset\mathbb R^d\) be compact and convex and let \(k_
u\) be a Matérn kernel with fixed length scale and smoothness \(
u>1\). Suppose observations have independent noise \(N(0,\sigma^2)\), \(\sigma^2>0\), and define \(\gamma_T=\max_{|A|=T} rac12\log\det(I_T+\sigma^{-2}K_A)\). The classical spectral-discretization bound is \[\gamma_T=O\!\left(T^{ rac{d(d+1)}{2
u+d(d+1)}}\log Tight).\] Thus increasing \(
u\) decreases the polynomial capacity exponent, while finite smoothness generally gives slower growth than the squared-exponential specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a Matérn kernel on a compact convex domain, the classical information-capacity bound is polynomial in T, with an exponent that decreases as smoothness increases.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb R^d\) is compact and convex.
The Matérn smoothness satisfies \(\nu>1\).
