children.title: Finite-Dimensional Kernel Capacity Classes
children.top_down_role: Capacity controlled by finite-dimensional feature structure.

children.title: Finite-Rank Kernel Capacity
children.top_down_role: Information capacity controlled by finite covariance rank.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Rank Kernel Capacity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-dependent information-gain bound for uniformly bounded kernels whose Gram matrices have fixed finite rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k\) satisfy \(k(x,x)\le \kappa^2\) and suppose every finite Gram matrix of \(k\) has rank at most \(r\). For independent Gaussian noise of variance \(\sigma^2>0\), define \(\gamma_T=\max_{|A|=T}\frac12\log\det(I_T+\sigma^{-2}K_A)\). Since \(K_A\succeq0\), \(\operatorname{rank}(K_A)\le r\), and \(\operatorname{tr}(K_A)\le T\kappa^2\), \[\gamma_T\le \frac r2\log\!\left(1+\frac{T\kappa^2}{r\sigma^2}\right).\] In particular, fixed rank implies \(\gamma_T=O(r\log T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded rank-r kernel has information capacity at most one-half r times a logarithmic signal-to-noise factor.
assumptions_latex: \(k(x,x)\le\kappa^2\) for every input.
Every finite Gram matrix has rank at most \(r\).
Noise variance satisfies \(\sigma^2>0\).

notation.meaning: uniform upper bound on Gram-matrix rank
uniform bound on the kernel diagonal

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-rank bound is mathematically plausible and correctly typed as a complexity bound, but no source or locator supports it. The explanatory derivation beginning with “Since” should also be removed from a source-backed statement record.

children.title: Linear Kernel Capacity
children.top_down_role: Capacity behavior induced by linear feature representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Kernel Capacity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional specialization for the ordinary linear kernel on a bounded feature domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\), assume \(\lVert x\rVert_2\le R\) for every \(x\in X\), and take \(k(x,x')=x^\top x'\). With independent Gaussian noise of variance \(\sigma^2>0\), let \(X_A\in\mathbb R^{T\times d}\) have the selected points as rows. Then \[\gamma_T=\max_{|A|=T}\frac12\log\det(I_d+\sigma^{-2}X_A^\top X_A)\le\frac d2\log\!\left(1+\frac{TR^2}{d\sigma^2}\right).\] Consequently the linear-kernel capacity is \(O(d\log T)\) when \(d,R,\sigma\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For bounded d-dimensional inputs, the linear kernel has information capacity at most d/2 times a logarithmic signal-to-noise factor.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) and \(\lVert x\rVert_2\le R\).
Noise variance is \(\sigma^2>0\).

notation.meaning: design matrix whose rows are the selected inputs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The linear-kernel specialization and content kind fit the leaf, but the determinant bound has no cited source with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Feature-Dimension Scaling
children.top_down_role: Dependence of kernel capacity on effective feature-space dimension.

knowledge_statements.title: Feature-Dimension Scaling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capacity scaling when a kernel admits a bounded feature map whose dimension may vary with the observation budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(k_T(x,x')=\phi_T(x)^\top\phi_T(x')\), where \(\phi_T:X\to\mathbb R^{m_T}\) and \(\lVert\phi_T(x)\rVert_2\le R\). Under independent Gaussian noise of variance \(\sigma^2>0\), \[\gamma_T(k_T)\le\frac{m_T}{2}\log\!\left(1+\frac{TR^2}{m_T\sigma^2}\right).\] Hence capacity is controlled by the available feature dimension: if \(m_T=o(T)\), then \(\gamma_T=o(T)\); if \(m_T\) is fixed, then \(\gamma_T=O(m_T\log T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded m-dimensional feature representation yields capacity proportional to m times a logarithmic factor; sublinear feature growth gives sublinear capacity.
assumptions_latex: \(k_T(x,x')=\phi_T(x)^\top\phi_T(x')\) with \(\phi_T(x)\in\mathbb R^{m_T}\).
\(\lVert\phi_T(x)\rVert_2\le R\) uniformly.
Noise variance satisfies \(\sigma^2>0\).

notation.meaning: feature dimension available at budget T

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The feature-dimension property is internally consistent, including the implication from sublinear feature dimension to sublinear capacity, but it lacks required source support.

children.title: Structured Kernel Capacity Classes
children.top_down_role: Capacity consequences of structured kernel decompositions.

children.title: Additive Kernel Capacity
children.top_down_role: Capacity consequences of kernels decomposed across additive components.

knowledge_statements.title: Additive Kernel Capacity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-capacity decomposition for sums of positive-semidefinite component kernels observed with common Gaussian noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k=\sum_{j=1}^M k_j\), where every \(k_j\) is positive semidefinite, and let noise variance be \(\sigma^2>0\). For a design \(A\), denote its component Gram matrices by \(K_{j,A}\). The determinant inequality for positive-semidefinite matrices gives \[\frac12\log\det\!\left(I+\sigma^{-2}\sum_{j=1}^M K_{j,A}\right)\le\sum_{j=1}^M\frac12\log\det(I+\sigma^{-2}K_{j,A}).\] Therefore \(\gamma_T(k)\le\sum_{j=1}^M\gamma_T(k_j)\). In particular, additive structure replaces a joint ambient-dimensional bound by a sum of component capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The information capacity of a sum of positive-semidefinite kernels is at most the sum of their individual capacities.
assumptions_latex: \(k=\sum_{j=1}^M k_j\) with each \(k_j\) positive semidefinite.
All components are evaluated on the same T design points.
Observation noise has variance \(\sigma^2>0\).

notation.meaning: component-kernel Gram matrix on design A

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive-kernel inequality is relevant and correctly presented as a complexity bound, but neither the determinant inequality nor its capacity consequence has an authoritative citation and locator.

children.title: Compositional Kernel Capacity
children.top_down_role: Capacity consequences of hierarchical or nested kernel constructions.

knowledge_statements.title: Compositional Kernel Capacity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-feature capacity calculus for kernels formed by sums and products of component kernels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose component kernels have finite feature representations \(k_j(x,x')=\langle\phi_j(x),\phi_j(x')\rangle\) of dimensions \(r_j\). A sum \(k_\oplus=\sum_{j=1}^M k_j\) has a concatenated feature representation of dimension at most \(\sum_j r_j\), whereas a product \(k_\otimes=\prod_{j=1}^M k_j\) has a tensor-product representation of dimension at most \(\prod_j r_j\). If the resulting kernel diagonal is bounded by \(\kappa^2\), its noisy information capacity satisfies \[\gamma_T\le\frac r2\log\!\left(1+\frac{T\kappa^2}{r\sigma^2}\right),\] with \(r=\sum_jr_j\) or \(r=\prod_jr_j\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feature dimensions add under kernel sums but multiply under kernel products, yielding corresponding finite-rank information-capacity bounds.
assumptions_latex: Each component kernel has a finite feature dimension \(r_j\).
The composed kernel satisfies \(k(x,x)\le\kappa^2\).
Noise variance satisfies \(\sigma^2>0\).

notation.meaning: feature dimension of the sum kernel
feature dimension of the product kernel

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-feature sum/product calculus fits the compositional-kernel leaf and is explicitly scoped to finite features, but its rank and capacity claims require an authoritative source.

children.title: Interaction-Structure Effects
children.top_down_role: Influence of component interactions on information capacity.

knowledge_statements.title: Interaction-Structure Effects
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capacity dependence on the number and complexity of active interaction components in an ANOVA-type kernel decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}k_u\), where each positive-semidefinite kernel \(k_u\) depends only on coordinates indexed by \(u\subseteq\{1,\ldots,d\}\). Under Gaussian noise of variance \(\sigma^2>0\), \[\gamma_T(k)\le\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}\gamma_T(k_u).\] If \(|u|\le q\) and \(\gamma_T(k_u)\le g_q(T)\) uniformly, then \(\gamma_T(k)\le|\mathcal U|g_q(T)\). Thus sparsity in the active interaction family controls capacity, while including all interactions through order \(q\) can introduce up to \(\sum_{s=1}^q\binom ds\) component terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Kernel capacity scales with the number of active interaction components; unrestricted higher-order interactions can cause combinatorial growth in the bound.
assumptions_latex: \(k=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}k_u\) with each \(k_u\) positive semidefinite.
Each component depends only on coordinates in \(u\).
Noise variance satisfies \(\sigma^2>0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The interaction-family capacity property is coherent and appropriately scoped, but the additive capacity inequality and combinatorial interaction claim have no cited evidence.

children.title: Spectral-Geometric Capacity Representation Family
children.top_down_role: Alternative representations used to refine or interpret information-gain bounds.

children.title: Kernel Eigenvalue Decay
children.top_down_role: Spectral route from covariance regularity to sequential capacity.

assumptions_latex: \(K_A\succeq0\) has ordered eigenvalues \(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_T\).
Observation noise variance satisfies \(\sigma^2>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-rank truncation bound separating dominant Gram eigenvalues from the spectral tail.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\theta_1\ge\cdots\ge\theta_T\ge0\) be the eigenvalues of a Gram matrix and let \(\sigma^2>0\). For every \(m\in\{0,\ldots,T\}\),
\[I(f_A;Y_A)\le \frac m2\log\!\left(1+\frac{\theta_1}{\sigma^2}\right)+\frac{1}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{i=m+1}^T\theta_i.\]
Thus a rank-\(m\) spectral head contributes logarithmically, while the residual trace contributes linearly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Information gain is bounded by a logarithmic contribution from leading eigenmodes plus a linear residual-trace contribution from the spectral tail.
knowledge_statements.title: Head-Tail Spectral Capacity Bound

assumptions_latex: General measurable positive-semidefinite kernels are allowed.
Observation noise variance satisfies \(\sigma^2>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Identical }L^2(\rho)\text{ operator spectra need not imply identical or uniformly comparable }\gamma_T.

notation.meaning: A measure-null point available to the worst-case design.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measure-null and high-leverage locations show why covariance-operator eigenvalues require pointwise comparison assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Mercer or covariance-operator eigenvalues are unchanged by kernel modifications on \(\rho\)-null sets, whereas \(\gamma_T\) maximizes over point evaluations. For a measurable positive-semidefinite kernel \(k\), define \(k_M(x,x')=k(x,x')+M\mathbf 1_{\{x_0\}}(x)\mathbf 1_{\{x_0\}}(x')\) at a point satisfying \(\rho(\{x_0\})=0\). The \(L^2(\rho)\) covariance operators of \(k\) and \(k_M\) are identical, but their one-point information gains at \(x_0\) differ by \[\frac12\log\!\left(\frac{1+(k(x_0,x_0)+M)/\sigma^2}{1+k(x_0,x_0)/\sigma^2}\right),\] which is unbounded as \(M\to\infty\). Hence operator eigenvalue decay alone cannot uniformly bound worst-case point-design capacity without continuity, bounded leverage, bounded eigenfunctions, or comparable pointwise control.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Measure-dependent operator eigenvalues can miss exceptional high-leverage points, so they do not by themselves bound worst-case point-design information gain.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Operator Spectrum Alone Does Not Control Worst-Case Designs
knowledge_statements.title: Operator Spectrum Alone Does Not Control Worst-Case Designs

assumptions_latex: The displayed Mercer expansion holds relative to a probability measure \(\rho\).
\(k(x,x)\le\kappa^2\) uniformly.
Every Mercer eigenfunction is uniformly bounded in absolute value by \(B\).
Observation noise is independent Gaussian with variance \(\sigma^2>0\).

notation.meaning: Mercer eigenvalues and eigenfunctions relative to the sampling measure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient route from covariance-operator eigenvalue decay to worst-case finite-design information capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k(x,x')=\sum_{j\ge1}\lambda_j\phi_j(x)\phi_j(x')\) be a Mercer expansion in \(L^2(\rho)\), with \(\lambda_1\ge\lambda_2\ge\cdots\ge0\), \(k(x,x)\le\kappa^2\), and \(\sup_x|\phi_j(x)|\le B\) for every \(j\). For any \(T\)-point design, independent Gaussian noise of variance \(\sigma^2>0\), and \(m\in\{0,\ldots,T\}\), \[I(f_A;Y_A)\le \frac m2\log\!\left(1+\frac{T\kappa^2}{m\sigma^2}\right)+\frac{TB^2}{2\sigma^2}\sum_{j>m}\lambda_j,\] where the first term is interpreted as zero for \(m=0\). Maximizing over designs and minimizing over \(m\) converts an operator-eigenvalue tail bound into a maximum-information-gain bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly bounded Mercer eigenfunctions let an operator spectral tail control every finite design, yielding an explicit head-tail information-capacity bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Eigenfunction Mercer-to-Capacity Transfer
Kernel Eigenvalue Decay
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact spectral representation of noisy information gain, exposing how Gram-matrix eigenvalue decay limits capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any design \(A=\{x_1,\ldots,x_T\}\), let \(\theta_1(A)\ge\cdots\ge\theta_T(A)\ge0\) be the eigenvalues of its kernel Gram matrix \(K_A\). With independent Gaussian noise of variance \(\sigma^2>0\), the information gain has the exact spectral representation \[I(f_A;y_A)=\frac12\log\det(I_T+\sigma^{-2}K_A)=\frac12\sum_{i=1}^T\log(1+\sigma^{-2}\theta_i(A)).\] Consequently, any uniform eigenvalue envelope \(\theta_i(A)\le b_i(T)\) yields \(\gamma_T\le\frac12\sum_{i=1}^T\log(1+\sigma^{-2}b_i(T))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noisy information gain is the sum of logarithms of shifted Gram eigenvalues, so a uniform eigenvalue-decay envelope directly bounds capacity.
assumptions_latex: \(K_A\) is the positive-semidefinite Gram matrix on a T-point design.
Observation noise is independent Gaussian with variance \(\sigma^2>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I(f_A;y_A)=\frac12\sum_i\log(1+\sigma^{-2}\theta_i(A))\), with the stated envelope bound for \(\gamma_T\).

notation.meaning: ordered eigenvalues of the design Gram matrix
uniform eigenvalue envelope over T-point designs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact Gram-eigenvalue representation and uniform-envelope consequence fit this representation leaf, but no authoritative source with a locator is supplied.

children.title: Effective Dimension
children.top_down_role: Scale-dependent dimensional representation of kernel complexity.

assumptions_latex: \(L\) is positive, self-adjoint, and trace class.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order, size, and endpoint properties of spectral effective dimension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a positive trace-class operator \(L\) and \(\eta>0\),
\[d_{\mathrm{eff}}(\eta)=\sum_j\frac{\lambda_j}{\lambda_j+\eta}\]
is nonincreasing in \(\eta\) and satisfies
\[0\le d_{\mathrm{eff}}(\eta)\le \min\!\left\{\operatorname{rank}(L),\frac{\operatorname{tr}L}{\eta}\right\}.\]
Moreover, \(d_{\mathrm{eff}}(\eta)\to0\) as \(\eta\to\infty\), while \(d_{\mathrm{eff}}(\eta)\to\operatorname{rank}(L)\) as \(\eta\downarrow0\), with the latter limit interpreted as \(+\infty\) for infinite rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Effective dimension decreases with the resolution scale, is bounded by rank and trace divided by scale, tends to zero at coarse scales, and tends to rank at fine scales.
knowledge_statements.title: Scale Monotonicity, Bounds, and Limits
Effective Dimension
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-dependent spectral dimension of a positive-semidefinite kernel operator or finite Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\) be a positive, self-adjoint, trace-class operator with eigenvalues \((\lambda_j)_{j\ge1}\), and let \(\eta>0\). Its effective dimension at scale \(\eta\) is \[d_{\mathrm{eff}}(\eta)=\operatorname{tr}\!\bigl(L(L+\eta I)^{-1}\bigr)=\sum_{j\ge1}\frac{\lambda_j}{\lambda_j+\eta}.\] For a finite Gram matrix \(K\succeq0\), the same definition is \(d_{\mathrm{eff}}(K,\eta)=\operatorname{tr}(K(K+\eta I)^{-1})\). Each eigenmode contributes a number in \([0,1]\), with modes much larger than \(\eta\) contributing approximately one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Effective dimension counts kernel eigenmodes relative to a resolution scale, weighting each eigenvalue by lambda divided by lambda plus the scale.
assumptions_latex: \(L\) is positive, self-adjoint, and trace class.
The resolution parameter satisfies \(\eta>0\).

notation.meaning: effective dimension at the specified scale

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a standard and internally consistent definition of effective dimension, with the content kind matching the leaf, but it lacks the required textbook or article locator.

children.title: Metric-Entropy Covering Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Geometric complexity used for continuous-domain confidence and optimization analysis.

children.title: Metric Entropy
children.top_down_role: Geometric complexity expressed through resolution-dependent domain size.

assumptions_latex: \((F,\rho)\) is a nonempty totally bounded metric space.
\(\varepsilon>0\).
The cardinality bound additionally assumes \(F\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary scale and finite-cardinality properties of metric entropy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonempty totally bounded metric space \((F,\rho)\), metric entropy is nonincreasing in the covering radius:
\[0<\varepsilon_1\le\varepsilon_2\quad\Longrightarrow\quad H(F,\rho,\varepsilon_1)\ge H(F,\rho,\varepsilon_2).\]
If \(F\) is finite, then for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[0\le H(F,\rho,\varepsilon)\le\log|F|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric entropy decreases as the allowed covering radius grows and, for a finite set, lies between zero and the logarithm of its cardinality.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity and Finite-Cardinality Bounds
Metric Entropy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logarithmic covering complexity of a totally bounded metric space at a prescribed resolution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((F,\rho)\) be a totally bounded metric space and let \(\varepsilon>0\). An \(\varepsilon\)-net is a finite set \(S\subset F\) such that every \(f\in F\) satisfies \(\min_{s\in S}\rho(f,s)\le\varepsilon\). The covering number is \(N(F,\rho,\varepsilon)=\min\{|S|:S\text{ is an }\varepsilon\text{-net of }F\}\). The metric entropy of \(F\) at resolution \(\varepsilon\) is \[H(F,\rho,\varepsilon)=\log N(F,\rho,\varepsilon).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric entropy is the logarithm of the smallest number of radius-epsilon metric balls needed to cover a totally bounded set.
assumptions_latex: \((F,\rho)\) is totally bounded.
\(\varepsilon>0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The metric-entropy definition is standard, precise, and correctly classified, but no source or inspectable locator is provided.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines Euclidean-radius covers and their minimum cardinality for subsets of finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) and \(r\ge 0\). A set \(A'\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) \(r\)-covers \(A\) in the Euclidean metric if \(\forall a\in A\,\exists a'\in A'\) such that \(\lVert a-a'\rVert_2\le r\). The covering number \(N(r,A)\) is the cardinality of a smallest such set \(A'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A set r-covers A when every point of A is within Euclidean distance r of a point in the covering set. The covering number N(r,A) is the smallest cardinality of such a covering set.
assumptions_latex: A\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m
r\ge 0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N(r,A)=\min\left\{|A'|:A'\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m,\ \forall a\in A\ \exists a'\in A',\ \lVert a-a'\rVert_2\le r\right\}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\), \(r>0\), and \(\rho\ge 0\). children.title: Covering-Number Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity controlled through finite covers of continuous search spaces.

assumptions_latex: The relevant metric spaces are totally bounded.
The product uses the maximum metric.
\(\phi\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz with \(L>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard calculus for constructing covers of composite metric spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
If \((X_i,\rho_i)\), \(i=1,2\), are totally bounded and \(\rho((x_1,x_2),(x'_1,x'_2))=\max_i\rho_i(x_i,x'_i)\), then
\[N(X_1\times X_2,\rho,\varepsilon)\le N(X_1,\rho_1,\varepsilon)N(X_2,\rho_2,\varepsilon).\]
If \(\phi:(X,\rho_X)\to(Y,\rho_Y)\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz with \(L>0\), then
\[N(\phi(X),\rho_Y,\varepsilon)\le N(X,\rho_X,\varepsilon/L).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Product covers multiply, while a Lipschitz map transfers a cover after rescaling its radius.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Covering Numbers Under Products and Lipschitz Images
knowledge_statements.title: Covering Numbers Under Products and Lipschitz Images
Covering-Number Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension-like growth law obtained from polynomial covering numbers over a bounded metric domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,\rho)\) be totally bounded. If constants \(C,R,p>0\) satisfy \[N(X,\rho,\varepsilon)\le C\left(\frac R\varepsilon\right)^p\qquad\text{for all }0<\varepsilon\le R,\] then its metric entropy obeys \[H(X,\rho,\varepsilon)\le\log C+p\log(R/\varepsilon).\] Conversely, this entropy inequality implies the displayed covering-number bound after exponentiation. The exponent \(p\) therefore acts as a metric dimension governing how discretization complexity increases as resolution becomes finer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A polynomial epsilon-covering law is equivalent to logarithmic metric-entropy growth, with the polynomial exponent acting as a metric dimension.
assumptions_latex: \((X,\rho)\) is totally bounded.
\(0<\varepsilon\le R\).
\(N(X,\rho,\varepsilon)\le C(R/\varepsilon)^p\) for fixed \(C,R,p>0\).

children.title: Discretization Resolution Effects
children.top_down_role: Impact of approximation resolution on confidence and optimization analysis.

assumptions_latex: \(D=[0,1]\) has its Euclidean metric.
Each \(D_n\) is a finite rational \(\varepsilon_n\)-net and \(\varepsilon_n\to0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of value approximation by increasingly fine nets when the objective lacks an appropriate continuity modulus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D=[0,1]\), choose \(x_0\in[0,1]\setminus\mathbb Q\), and define \(f(x_0)=1\) and \(f(x)=0\) for \(x\ne x_0\). There exist finite rational \(\varepsilon_n\)-nets \(D_n\subset\mathbb Q\cap[0,1]\) with \(\varepsilon_n\downarrow0\). Nevertheless,
\[\max_{x\in D}f(x)=1,\qquad \max_{x\in D_n}f(x)=0\quad\text{for every }n.\]
Thus vanishing covering radius alone does not imply convergence of discretized optimal values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrarily fine nets can miss an isolated maximizer forever, so mesh refinement controls optimization error only under suitable uniform regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vanishing Mesh Without Uniform Regularity Need Not Approximate the Optimum
knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Mesh Without Uniform Regularity Need Not Approximate the Optimum

assumptions_latex: \(f:D\to\mathbb R\) has modulus of continuity \(\omega\), meaning \(|f(x)-f(x')|\le \omega(d(x,x'))\).
\(D_\varepsilon\subset D\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-net and \(x^\star\in\arg\max_{x\in D}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le f(x^\star)-\max_{x\in D_\varepsilon}f(x)\le\omega(\varepsilon)\), and cumulative discretization loss is at most \(\sum_{t=1}^T\omega(\varepsilon_t)\).

notation.meaning: Modulus of continuity of the objective

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic approximation error induced by replacing a metric decision domain with successively finer covers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((D,d)\) be a metric space, let \(f:D\to\mathbb R\), and suppose \(|f(x)-f(x')|\le\omega(d(x,x'))\), where \(\omega\) is nondecreasing and \(\omega(0)=0\). If \(D_\varepsilon\) is an \(\varepsilon\)-net of \(D\), then for every maximizer \(x^\star\) there exists \([x^\star]_\varepsilon\in D_\varepsilon\) satisfying \(d(x^\star,[x^\star]_\varepsilon)\le\varepsilon\), and
\[
0\le f(x^\star)-\max_{x\in D_\varepsilon}f(x)\le\omega(\varepsilon).
\]
Consequently, using resolutions \(\varepsilon_t\) at rounds \(t\le T\) adds at most \(\sum_{t=1}^T\omega(\varepsilon_t)\) to cumulative regret; summable resolution errors contribute only a bounded additive term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An epsilon-net loses at most the objective's continuity modulus at epsilon; over time, discretization contributes the sum of these per-round losses.
knowledge_statements.title: Discretization Resolution Effects

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The discretization property is mathematically plausible and fits the leaf, but no citation supports the modulus-of-continuity and cumulative-loss claims.

children.title: Optimistic Selection
children.top_down_role: Regret analysis organized around selection from upper-confidence assessments.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computationally inexact upper-confidence selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_t(x)=\mu_{t-1}(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}\sigma_{t-1}(x)\). An \(\varepsilon_t\)-approximate optimistic choice satisfies \(U_t(x_t)\ge\sup_{x\in D_t}U_t(x)-\varepsilon_t\). On a simultaneous confidence event covering \(x_t\) and an optimizer \(x^\star\), \(f(x^\star)-f(x_t)\le2\sqrt{\beta_t}\sigma_{t-1}(x_t)+\varepsilon_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate UCB maximization remains analyzable, with acquisition-search error entering the instantaneous bound additively.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t\) is an \(\varepsilon_t\)-approximate maximizer of \(U_t\).
The confidence band covers \(x_t\) and \(x^\star\).
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Optimistic Selection

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign-dual lower-confidence rule for cost minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimizing a latent cost \(f\), define \(L_t(x)=\mu_{t-1}(x)-\sqrt{\beta_t}\sigma_{t-1}(x)\) and choose \(x_t\in\arg\min_{x\in D_t}L_t(x)\). This is the maximization UCB rule applied to reward \(-f\). On the valid confidence event, \(f(x_t)-f(x^\star)\le2\sqrt{\beta_t}\sigma_{t-1}(x_t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cost minimization uses a lower confidence bound, the sign-dual of reward-maximizing UCB.
assumptions_latex: The confidence band is two-sided.
A lower-confidence minimizer exists.

notation.meaning: lower confidence function for cost minimization

knowledge_statements.title: Minimization Form of Optimistic Selection

assumptions_latex: At round \(t\), the posterior mean \(\mu_{t-1}\), standard deviation \(\sigma_{t-1}\), and exploration coefficient \(\beta_t>0\) are available.
The maximization domain \(D_t\) is nonempty and an acquisition maximizer exists.

notation.meaning: Posterior mean after observations through round t-1
Posterior standard deviation after observations through round t-1

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The maximization-form GP-UCB decision rule on a fixed or round-dependent candidate domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given observations through round \(t-1\), form the optimistic acquisition function
\[
a_t(x)=\mu_{t-1}(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}\,\sigma_{t-1}(x),\qquad x\in D_t.
\]
Initialize with the Gaussian-process prior mean and covariance before round \(1\). At each round choose
\[
x_t\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in D_t}a_t(x),
\]
observe \(y_t=f(x_t)+\varepsilon_t\), and update the posterior. After a prescribed horizon \(T\), output the sampled sequence for cumulative-regret analysis, or any specified recommendation derived from the posterior for simple-regret use.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: GP-UCB selects a point maximizing posterior mean plus an exploration multiplier times posterior standard deviation, then updates the posterior from the noisy observation.
knowledge_statements.title: Optimistic Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and GP-UCB selection rule fit Optimistic Selection, but the record supplies no inspectable source for the rule and update protocol.

children.title: Confidence-Width Control
children.top_down_role: Conversion of sequential uncertainty widths into cumulative performance control.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Posterior-Variance Sum Controlled by Information Gain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kernel specialization converting accumulated widths to a log-determinant quantity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(k(x,x)\le\kappa^2\), \(\lambda>0\), and posterior variances computed with the same kernel and regularization convention. Then \(\sum_{t=1}^T\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\le\frac{\kappa^2}{\log(1+\kappa^2/\lambda)}\log\det(I+\lambda^{-1}K_T)\). If \(\gamma_T=\frac12\max_{|A|=T}\log\det(I+\lambda^{-1}K_A)\), then \(\sum_{t=1}^T\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)\le\frac{2\kappa^2}{\log(1+\kappa^2/\lambda)}\gamma_T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accumulated posterior variance is bounded by a convention-explicit constant times maximum kernel information gain.
assumptions_latex: \(k(x,x)\le\kappa^2\) for all x.
\(\lambda>0\).
Posterior variances and \(\gamma_T\) use the displayed regularization convention.

notation.meaning: maximum information gain under the displayed convention

knowledge_statements.title: Posterior-Variance Sum Controlled by Information Gain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic conversion from instantaneous confidence widths to cumulative regret.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(r_t\le2\sqrt{\beta_t}\sigma_{t-1}(x_t)\) for every \(t\le T\), then \(R_T:=\sum_{t=1}^T r_t\le2\sqrt{T\sum_{t=1}^T\beta_t\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)}\). If additionally \(\beta_t\le\beta_T\), then \(R_T\le2\sqrt{T\beta_T\sum_{t=1}^T\sigma_{t-1}^2(x_t)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cauchy-Schwarz reduces cumulative regret to accumulated squared posterior widths.
assumptions_latex: \(r_t\le2\sqrt{\beta_t}\sigma_{t-1}(x_t)\) for every \(t\le T\).
\(\beta_t\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Cumulative Width Reduction

assumptions_latex: For every relevant \(x\) and \(t\), \(|f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)|\le\sqrt{\beta_t}\sigma_{t-1}(x)\).
\(x_t\) maximizes the upper confidence bound and \(x^\star\) maximizes \(f\) on the same domain.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic regret control on the simultaneous confidence event underlying optimistic GP bandit analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
U_t(x)=\mu_{t-1}(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}\sigma_{t-1}(x),\qquad L_t(x)=\mu_{t-1}(x)-\sqrt{\beta_t}\sigma_{t-1}(x).
\]
On the event that \(L_t(x)\le f(x)\le U_t(x)\) for every relevant \(x\), let \(x_t\in\arg\max_x U_t(x)\) and \(x^\star\in\arg\max_x f(x)\). Then
\[
r_t:=f(x^\star)-f(x_t)\le U_t(x_t)-L_t(x_t)=2\sqrt{\beta_t}\sigma_{t-1}(x_t).
\]
Thus cumulative regret is controlled by the sum of posterior widths at the selected points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a valid simultaneous confidence event, the regret of an optimistic choice is at most twice its scaled posterior standard deviation.
knowledge_statements.title: Confidence-Width Control

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The confidence-event width inequality is standard and locally appropriate, but it has no cited source or locator.

children.title: Confidence-Calibration Boundary
children.top_down_role: Failure modes arising when confidence assessments do not reliably cover the objective.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated-testing obstruction below an adequate calibration schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let independent exceedance events satisfy \(\Pr(|Z_t|>\sqrt{\beta_t})=p_t\). If \(\sum_{t\ge1}p_t=\infty\), the second Borel-Cantelli lemma gives \(\Pr(|Z_t|>\sqrt{\beta_t}\ \text{infinitely often})=1\). Thus the proposed band cannot hold at every time on an event of positive probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under independent errors, nonsummable tail probabilities cause infinitely many confidence failures almost surely.
assumptions_latex: The exceedance events are independent.
\(\sum_tp_t=\infty\).
knowledge_statements.title: Nonsummable Repeated-Tail Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of nominal confidence calibration under incorrect standardized-error tails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \((\beta_t)\) is calibrated from \(\Pr(|Z_t|>u\mid\mathcal H_{t-1})\le2e^{-u^2/2}\). If the actual standardized error violates this bound at a used threshold \(u=\sqrt{\beta_t}\), then the nominal allocation understates the actual failure probability. Summability of the nominal allocations alone therefore does not imply the advertised simultaneous coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A summable confidence schedule is insufficient when the assumed standardized-error tail is wrong.
assumptions_latex: The multiplier is calibrated using a declared conditional tail inequality.
The actual standardized error violates that inequality at a used threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nominal summability alone does not establish the claimed simultaneous coverage under tail misspecification.
knowledge_statements.title: Model-Tail Miscalibration Boundary

assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite with cardinality \(|D|\), and each standardized posterior error has a Gaussian tail.
A total failure probability \(\delta\in(0,1)\) is allocated across all point-round pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Choosing \(\beta_t\ge2\log(|D|\pi^2t^2/(3\delta))\) ensures simultaneous coverage with probability at least \(1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite-domain union-bound calibration; numerical constants depend on the adopted Gaussian tail convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\) be finite and suppose conditionally on the history that
\[
\Pr\!\left(\left.|f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)|>\sqrt{\beta_t}\sigma_{t-1}(x)\,\right|\mathcal H_{t-1}\right)\le 2e^{-\beta_t/2}.
\]
A sufficient calibration boundary is
\[
\beta_t\ge2\log\!\left(\frac{|D|\pi^2t^2}{3\delta}\right).
\]
It gives \(2|D|e^{-\beta_t/2}\le6\delta/(\pi^2t^2)\), so the simultaneous confidence event over all \(x\in D\) and \(t\ge1\) has probability at least \(1-\delta\). Below a summable-tail calibration, this uniform guarantee does not follow from the union-bound argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A confidence schedule must offset both domain size and repeated testing; a logarithmic-in-domain, logarithmic-in-time radius gives uniform finite-domain coverage.
knowledge_statements.title: Confidence-Calibration Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-domain union-bound calculation is internally consistent with the stated two-sided tail, but the precise confidence schedule and constants require an authoritative cited convention.

children.title: Information-Ratio Route
children.top_down_role: Bayesian regret analysis comparing expected loss with acquired information.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: An Information-Theoretic Analysis of Thompson Sampling
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: An Information-Theoretic Analysis of Thompson Sampling

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Policy obtained by minimizing the one-step information ratio.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\mathcal H_{t-1}\), let \(\Delta_t(q)\) be posterior expected instantaneous regret and let \(g_t(q)=I(A^\star;(A_t,Y_t)\mid\mathcal H_{t-1})\) when \(A_t\sim q\). Information-directed sampling chooses \(q_t\in\arg\min_{q\in\mathcal P(\mathcal A)}\Delta_t(q)^2/g_t(q)\), using ratio zero when both quantities vanish and infinity when \(g_t(q)=0<\Delta_t(q)\), and then samples \(A_t\sim q_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Information-directed sampling minimizes squared posterior expected regret per unit of information about the optimum.
assumptions_latex: The posterior quantities \(\Delta_t(q)\) and \(g_t(q)\) are well defined.
A minimizing distribution exists, or an explicitly approximate minimizer is used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q_t\) minimizes the conditional information ratio over admissible action distributions.

notation.meaning: randomized action distribution at round t
conditional information gained about the optimal action

knowledge_statements.title: Information-Directed Sampling Rule

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp obstruction to a finite information-ratio guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If at some history every admissible action distribution \(q\) satisfies \(g_t(q)=0\) and \(\Delta_t(q)>0\), then \(\Delta_t(q)^2/g_t(q)=\infty\). No finite information-ratio constant can cover that round.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every available experiment yields zero information about the optimum while incurring positive expected regret, this proof route cannot produce a finite bound.
assumptions_latex: \(g_t(q)=0<\Delta_t(q)\) for every admissible q at some history.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Information Positive-Regret Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conversion of one-step information increments into the horizon information budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\mathcal H_T=((A_1,Y_1),\ldots,(A_T,Y_T))\), the mutual-information chain rule gives \(I(A^\star;\mathcal H_T)=\sum_{t=1}^T I(A^\star;(A_t,Y_t)\mid\mathcal H_{t-1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional information gains sum to the total information acquired about the optimum.
assumptions_latex: The displayed mutual informations are well defined.
knowledge_statements.title: Chain Rule for Acquired Information

assumptions_latex: \(A^\star\) is the latent optimal action and \(\mathcal H_{t-1}\) is the history before round \(t\).
The conditional information ratios \(\Gamma_t=\Delta_t^2/I(A^\star;(A_t,Y_t)\mid\mathcal H_{t-1})\) are bounded by \(\bar\Gamma\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The bounded-information-ratio route to finite-horizon Bayesian cumulative-regret guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
\Delta_t=\mathbb E[f(A^\star)-f(A_t)\mid\mathcal H_{t-1}],\qquad g_t=I(A^\star;(A_t,Y_t)\mid\mathcal H_{t-1}).
\]
Use the convention \(\Gamma_t=0\) when \(\Delta_t=g_t=0\), and assume \(\Gamma_t:=\Delta_t^2/g_t\le\bar\Gamma\) otherwise. Then the Bayesian cumulative regret satisfies
\[
\operatorname{BayesRegret}(T)=\mathbb E\!\left[\sum_{t=1}^T(f(A^\star)-f(A_t))\right]
\le\sqrt{\bar\Gamma T I(A^\star;\mathcal H_T)}.
\]
If \(A^\star\) is discrete, this is at most \(\sqrt{\bar\Gamma T H(A^\star)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When squared expected one-step regret is uniformly bounded by acquired information times a constant, Bayesian cumulative regret is bounded by total information times the horizon.
knowledge_statements.title: Information-Ratio Route

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits the Information-Ratio Route, but the conditional information-ratio theorem and entropy corollary lack a supporting citation and locator.

children.title: Posterior-Sampling Symmetry Route
children.top_down_role: Regret analysis exploiting the posterior relationship between sampled decisions and latent optima.

assumptions_latex: At round \(t\), posterior sampling draws \(A_t\) from the conditional law of the latent optimizer \(A^\star\) given \(\mathcal H_{t-1}\).
The displayed conditional expectations are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal L(A_t\mid\mathcal H_{t-1})=\mathcal L(A^\star\mid\mathcal H_{t-1})\), yielding the posterior-sampling regret decomposition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional distributional symmetry used to analyze Thompson or posterior sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Posterior sampling imposes the conditional identity
\[
\mathcal L(A_t\mid\mathcal H_{t-1})=\mathcal L(A^\star\mid\mathcal H_{t-1}).
\]
Hence, for every history-measurable function \(U_t\) with finite expectations,
\[
\mathbb E[U_t(A_t)\mid\mathcal H_{t-1}]=\mathbb E[U_t(A^\star)\mid\mathcal H_{t-1}].
\]
Its conditional expected regret therefore admits the symmetry decomposition
\[
\mathbb E[f(A^\star)-f(A_t)\mid\mathcal H_{t-1}]
=
\mathbb E[U_t(A_t)-f(A_t)\mid\mathcal H_{t-1}]
+
\mathbb E[f(A^\star)-U_t(A^\star)\mid\mathcal H_{t-1}].
\]
The first term is a sampled confidence width; the second measures confidence failure at the latent optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A posterior-sampled action and the latent optimizer have the same conditional distribution, converting expected regret into confidence-width and confidence-failure terms.
knowledge_statements.title: Posterior-Sampling Symmetry Route

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The posterior-sampling symmetry and displayed decomposition are appropriate for the leaf, but no inspectable source is provided.

children.title: Bayesian GP-UCB Regime
children.top_down_role: GP-UCB analysis under a Gaussian-process sample-path model.

assumptions_latex: \(f\) is sampled from a zero-mean Gaussian process with \(k(x,x)\le1\), and observations have independent \(N(0,\sigma^2)\) noise.
A schedule \(\beta_t\) gives simultaneous posterior confidence with probability at least \(1-\delta\).

notation.meaning: Maximum information gain from T noisy evaluations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: High-probability GP-UCB regret under a correctly specified Gaussian-process sample-path model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\sim\operatorname{GP}(0,k)\), with \(k(x,x)\le1\), and let \(y_t=f(x_t)+\varepsilon_t\), where \(\varepsilon_t\) are independent \(N(0,\sigma^2)\). Suppose GP-UCB uses a nondecreasing \(\beta_t\) for which the simultaneous confidence event holds with probability at least \(1-\delta\). Define
\[
\gamma_T=\max_{A\subset D,\,|A|=T}I(y_A;f_A).
\]
Then, on that event,
\[
R_T:=\sum_{t=1}^T(f(x^\star)-f(x_t))
\le\sqrt{C_\sigma T\beta_T\gamma_T},
\qquad C_\sigma=\frac{8}{\log(1+\sigma^{-2})}.
\]
Thus sublinear regret follows whenever \(\beta_T\gamma_T=o(T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a GP-sampled objective, calibrated GP-UCB has regret proportional to the square root of horizon, confidence scale, and maximum information gain.
knowledge_statements.title: Bayesian GP-UCB Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the Bayesian GP-UCB regime, but the exact constant and definition of maximum information gain require a source; the subset definition also needs a convention when repeated evaluations or T exceeding a finite domain size are allowed.
