knowledge_statements.statement_title: GP Sample Paths Are Not Automatically RKHS-Ball Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating fixed-function RKHS guarantees from Bayesian GP sample-path guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a nondegenerate infinite-rank Gaussian process \(F\sim\operatorname{GP}(0,k)\), correct covariance specification does not imply \(F\in\mathcal H_k\); in the standard infinite-rank setting, \(F\notin\mathcal H_k\) almost surely. Hence a theorem uniform over \(\{f:\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B\}\) cannot be applied to a GP draw solely because its covariance is \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A draw from an infinite-rank GP is generally outside that GP's RKHS, so Bayesian and fixed-function GP-UCB guarantees are not interchangeable.
assumptions_latex: The Gaussian process is nondegenerate and has infinite covariance rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Correct GP covariance specification alone does not establish \(\|F\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B\).
knowledge_statements.title: GP Sample Paths Are Not Automatically RKHS-Ball Functions

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-objective GP-UCB under explicitly normalized self-normalized confidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Use the notation and assumptions of Time-Uniform Self-Normalized RKHS Confidence, write \(w_{t-1}(x)=\|\phi(x)\|_{V_{t-1}^{-1}}\), and let \(\alpha_t=\sqrt\lambda B+R\sqrt{2\log(1/\delta)+\log\det(I+\lambda^{-1}K_{t-1})}\). Choose \(x_t\in\arg\max_x\{\widehat f_{t-1}(x)+\alpha_t w_{t-1}(x)\}\). On the confidence event, \[r_t\le2\alpha_t w_{t-1}(x_t),\qquad R_T\le2\alpha_T\sqrt{T\sum_{t=1}^T w_{t-1}^2(x_t)}.\] Hence, whenever \(\sum_{t=1}^T w_{t-1}^2(x_t)\le C_{\lambda,k}\gamma_T\), \[R_T\le2\alpha_T\sqrt{C_{\lambda,k}T\gamma_T}\] simultaneously for all \(T\), with probability at least \(1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed RKHS-bounded objective, self-normalized confidence plus posterior-width summation yields high-probability GP-UCB cumulative regret.
assumptions_latex: The fixed objective, predictable observations, and noise satisfy the self-normalized RKHS confidence theorem.
A maximizer of the objective and every acquisition maximizer exist.
\(\alpha_t\) is nondecreasing, and the stated width-summation inequality holds under the chosen normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_T\le2\alpha_T\sqrt{C_{\lambda,k}T\gamma_T}\) for every \(T\) on one event of probability at least \(1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.title: RKHS GP-UCB Confidence-to-Regret Theorem

assumptions_latex: The fixed objective satisfies \(f\in\mathcal H_k\) and \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B\), with \(k(x,x)\le1\).
Observation noise is conditionally \(R\)-sub-Gaussian and the kernel ridge regularization is \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With a self-normalized confidence radius \(b_t\), \(R_T=O(b_T\sqrt{T\gamma_T})\) with probability at least \(1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Frequentist GP-UCB bound for a fixed RKHS-bounded objective with sub-Gaussian observation noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\in\mathcal H_k\) satisfy \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le B\), and let the observation noise be conditionally \(R\)-sub-Gaussian. For regularization \(\lambda>0\), use an RKHS self-normalized radius of the form
\[
b_t=B+R\sqrt{2\bigl(\gamma_{t-1}+1+\log(1/\delta)\bigr)}
\]
and select \(x_t\in\arg\max_x\{\mu_{t-1}(x)+b_t\sigma_{t-1}(x)\}\). With probability at least \(1-\delta\), confidence-width summation gives
\[
R_T=O\!\left(b_T\sqrt{T\gamma_T}\right),
\]
where the hidden constant depends only on \(\lambda\) and the normalization of \(k\). This regime treats \(f\) as fixed, not as a GP draw.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed RKHS-bounded objective with sub-Gaussian noise, self-normalized confidence sets yield regret of order confidence radius times square-root information capacity.
knowledge_statements.title: RKHS GP-UCB Regime

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The frequentist RKHS regime is correctly distinguished from a GP draw, but the displayed radius is normalization-dependent and is not justified for arbitrary regularization lambda without a precise source.

children.title: GP-UCB Domain-Regime Specializations
children.top_down_role: Domain-specific forms of GP-UCB confidence and regret analysis.

children.title: Finite-Domain GP-UCB
children.top_down_role: GP-UCB confidence and regret analysis for finite action sets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bayesian GP-UCB on a fixed finite action set with Gaussian noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be finite with \(|D|=K\), let \(f\sim\operatorname{GP}(0,k)\), assume \(k(x,x)\le1\), and observe independent noise \(N(0,\sigma^2)\). Set \(\beta_t=2\log(K\pi^2t^2/(6\delta))\) and choose \(x_t\in\arg\max_{x\in D}\{\mu_{t-1}(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}\,s_{t-1}(x)\}\). Then, with probability at least \(1-\delta\), simultaneously for every \(T\ge1\), \[R_T\le\sqrt{C_\sigma T\beta_T\gamma_T},\qquad C_\sigma=\frac{8}{\log(1+\sigma^{-2})},\] where \(\gamma_T=\max_{(x_1,\ldots,x_T)\in D^T}\tfrac12\log\det(I+\sigma^{-2}K_T)\). Moreover, \[\gamma_T\le\frac K2\log\left(1+\frac{T}{K\sigma^2}\right).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-set Gaussian union-bound schedule gives an anytime GP-UCB regret bound, and repeated selections have information gain controlled by the action-set cardinality.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is fixed and finite, \(k(x,x)\le1\), and \(\sigma^2>0\).
The GP prior and independent Gaussian observation model are correctly specified.
Acquisition maximizers use a declared tie-breaking rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_T\le\sqrt{C_\sigma T\beta_T\gamma_T}\) for all \(T\) on one event of probability at least \(1-\delta\).

notation.meaning: Maximum information gain over length-T action sequences, allowing repetitions

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain GP-UCB Regret Bound

assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite, \(f\sim\operatorname{GP}(0,k)\), \(k(x,x)\le1\), and noise is independent \(N(0,\sigma^2)\).
GP-UCB uses \(\beta_t=2\log(|D|\pi^2t^2/(3\delta))\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-action Bayesian GP-UCB with confidence calibrated by a point-round union bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For finite \(D\), take
\[
\beta_t=2\log\!\left(\frac{|D|\pi^2t^2}{3\delta}\right)
\]
and choose \(x_t\in\arg\max_{x\in D}\{\mu_{t-1}(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}\sigma_{t-1}(x)\}\). Under the stated Gaussian-process and noise model, with probability at least \(1-\delta\),
\[
R_T\le\sqrt{C_\sigma T\beta_T\gamma_T},
\qquad C_\sigma=\frac{8}{\log(1+\sigma^{-2})}.
\]
Since \(\gamma_T\le\tfrac12\min\{T,|D|\}\log(1+T/\sigma^2)\) under unit diagonal normalization, this also provides a purely finite-domain capacity bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite action set, a union-bound confidence schedule yields the standard information-gain GP-UCB regret bound, with an additional cardinality-based capacity estimate.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain GP-UCB

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-domain specialization fits the leaf, but its exact constants and cardinality capacity estimate need a source. The information-gain maximization must also specify sequences or multisets when T exceeds the number of actions.

children.title: Continuous-Domain GP-UCB
children.top_down_role: GP-UCB confidence and regret analysis for continuous search spaces.

assumptions_latex: \(D\subset[0,r]^d\) is compact and admits finite grids \(D_t\) whose approximation errors are summable.
The GP sample paths satisfy a high-probability derivative or modulus-of-continuity bound, and observations have Gaussian noise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_T\le\sqrt{C_\sigma T\beta_T\gamma_T}+\sum_{t=1}^T\omega(\varepsilon_t)\) on the joint confidence and regularity event.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous-domain GP-UCB reduced to finite grids through a high-probability sample-path regularity event.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\subset[0,r]^d\) be compact. At round \(t\), optimize GP-UCB over an \(\varepsilon_t\)-net \(D_t\). Suppose that on an event of probability at least \(1-\delta_1\),
\[
|f(x)-f(x')|\le\omega(\|x-x'\|)
\]
for all \(x,x'\in D\), and calibrate confidence over the grids with failure probability \(\delta_2\). On the joint event, with \(\delta_1+\delta_2\le\delta\),
\[
R_T\le\sqrt{C_\sigma T\beta_T\gamma_T}+
\sum_{t=1}^T\omega(\varepsilon_t).
\]
Choosing the grids so that the final sum is bounded or subdominant transfers the finite-grid information-gain guarantee to the continuous domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuous-domain GP-UCB uses increasingly fine grids; regret equals the finite-grid information bound plus the accumulated continuity-controlled approximation error.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuous-Domain GP-UCB

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bound has the correct continuous-domain structure, but the sample-path regularity event, grid confidence calibration, and retained information-gain constant depend on a specific theorem that is not cited.

children.title: Domain-Discretization Interface
children.top_down_role: Transfer of finite-set control to continuous-domain analysis.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Mesh Refinement Without Regularity Can Fail
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample to transferring finite-grid regret to an uncountable domain using mesh refinement without objective regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be uncountable and let each \(D_t\subset D\) be finite. Put \(G=\bigcup_{t\ge1}D_t\), choose \(x^\star\in D\setminus G\), and define \(f(x)=\mathbf 1\{x=x^\star\}\). Then every sequence \(x_t\in D_t\) satisfies \[\sum_{t=1}^T\bigl(f(x^\star)-f(x_t)\bigr)=T,\] regardless of the mesh radii. Thus mesh refinement alone cannot transfer finite-grid regret without a continuity or other approximation condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrarily fine finite grids can miss a discontinuous unit spike forever, yielding linear continuous-domain regret.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is uncountable.
Each \(D_t\subset D\) is finite.

notation.meaning: Countable union of all round-dependent finite grids

knowledge_statements.title: Mesh Refinement Without Regularity Can Fail

assumptions_latex: Each \(D_t\) is an \(\varepsilon_t\)-net of a metric domain \(D\).
On a regularity event, \(|f(x)-f(x')|\le\omega(d(x,x'))\) for all \(x,x'\in D\).

notation.meaning: Nearest grid representative of x at round t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive decomposition connecting continuous-domain regret to finite-grid regret and approximation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each \(t\), let \(D_t\) be an \(\varepsilon_t\)-net of \(D\), and choose \([x^\star]_t\in D_t\) with \(d(x^\star,[x^\star]_t)\le\varepsilon_t\). If \(|f(x)-f(x')|\le\omega(d(x,x'))\), then every sequence \(x_t\in D_t\) satisfies
\[
\sum_{t=1}^T\bigl(f(x^\star)-f(x_t)\bigr)
=
\sum_{t=1}^T\bigl(f([x^\star]_t)-f(x_t)\bigr)
+
\sum_{t=1}^T\bigl(f(x^\star)-f([x^\star]_t)\bigr)
\]
and hence
\[
R_T(D)\le R_T(D_1,\ldots,D_T)+\sum_{t=1}^T\omega(\varepsilon_t).
\]
This identity isolates the exact interface term that domain discretization must control.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuous regret decomposes into regret against each finite grid plus a continuity-controlled approximation term determined by grid resolution.
knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Discretization Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The decomposition fits the domain-discretization interface, but the shorthand R_T(D_1,...,D_T) is not explicitly defined and no source supports the stated interface formulation.

children.title: Kernel-Specific GP-UCB Rates
children.top_down_role: Regret consequences of kernel-specific information-capacity bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regret consequence of finite-rank kernel information capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(k(x,x')=\langle\phi(x),\phi(x')\rangle\), \(\phi(x)\in\mathbb R^r\), and \(\|\phi(x)\|_2\le\kappa\). With Gaussian observation variance \(\sigma^2>0\), \[\gamma_T\le \frac r2\log\!\left(1+\frac{T\kappa^2}{r\sigma^2}\right).\] Therefore any applicable bound \(R_T\le C\sqrt{T\beta_T\gamma_T}\) implies \[R_T=O\!\left(\sqrt{rT\beta_T\log(1+T)}\right),\] with normalization-dependent constants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded rank-r kernel has information capacity at most logarithmic in the horizon up to a factor r, yielding the corresponding finite-rank GP-UCB regret rate.
assumptions_latex: \(k\) has a feature representation of dimension at most \(r\).
\(\|\phi(x)\|_2\le\kappa\) uniformly.
Observation variance satisfies \(\sigma^2>0\).
An applicable GP-UCB information-gain regret theorem is available.

notation.meaning: Maximum information gain from T noisy observations

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Rank Kernel GP-UCB Rate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Squared-Exponential and Matérn GP-UCB Rate Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical regret consequences of the dedicated kernel-capacity estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume an applicable GP-UCB theorem gives \(R_T=O(\sqrt{T\beta_T\gamma_T})\). If a squared-exponential kernel on a compact \(d\)-dimensional domain satisfies \(\gamma_T=O((\log T)^{d+1})\), then \[R_T=O\!\left(\sqrt{T\beta_T}(\log T)^{(d+1)/2}\right).\] If a Matérn kernel of smoothness \(\nu\) satisfies the classical estimate \(\gamma_T=O(T^a\log T)\), \(a=d(d+1)/(2\nu+d(d+1))\), then \[R_T=O\!\left(\sqrt{\beta_T\log T}\,T^{(1+a)/2}\right).\] These are substitutions into the stated capacity versions, not claims that the displayed capacity estimates are sharp.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical squared-exponential and Matérn information-capacity bounds transfer directly into their corresponding GP-UCB regret rates.
assumptions_latex: An applicable base theorem gives \(R_T=O(\sqrt{T\beta_T\gamma_T})\).
The relevant dedicated capacity estimate holds with its compact-domain, kernel, and noise assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed squared-exponential and Matérn regret rates follow from their respective capacity bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Squared-Exponential and Matérn GP-UCB Rate Transfer

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic transfer from capacity growth to GP-UCB regret growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(R_T\le C\sqrt{T\beta_T\gamma_T}\), \(\beta_T=O((\log T)^c)\), and \(\gamma_T=O(T^a(\log T)^b)\) with \(0\le a<1\), then \[R_T=O\!\left(T^{(1+a)/2}(\log T)^{(b+c)/2}\right)=o(T).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sublinear polynomial capacity exponent gives sublinear GP-UCB regret, with all logarithmic factors entering under the square root.
assumptions_latex: \(R_T\le C\sqrt{T\beta_T\gamma_T}\).
\(\beta_T=O((\log T)^c)\) and \(\gamma_T=O(T^a(\log T)^b)\), where \(a<1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Generic Information-Capacity Rate Transfer

assumptions_latex: \(D\subset\mathbb R^d\) is compact and the kernel is squared-exponential or Matérn with smoothness \(\nu>0\).
A GP-UCB regime supplies \(R_T=O(\sqrt{T\beta_T\gamma_T})\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Kernel-specific bounds on \(\gamma_T\) directly yield the displayed squared-exponential and Matérn regret rates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical information-capacity substitutions for squared-exponential and Matérn kernels on compact Euclidean domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume a GP-UCB bound \(R_T=O(\sqrt{T\beta_T\gamma_T})\). For the squared-exponential kernel on a compact subset of \(\mathbb R^d\), the classical capacity estimate
\[
\gamma_T=O((\log T)^{d+1})
\]
gives
\[
R_T=O\!\left(\sqrt{T\beta_T}\,(
\log T)^{(d+1)/2}\right).
\]
For a Matérn kernel of smoothness \(\nu\), the classical estimate
\[
\gamma_T=O\!\left(T^{\frac{d(d+1)}{2\nu+d(d+1)}}\log T\right)
\]
gives
\[
R_T=O\!\left(\sqrt{\beta_T\log T}\;T^{\frac12+\frac{d(d+1)}{2(2\nu+d(d+1))}}\right).
\]
All constants may depend on the kernel, domain, dimension, and noise level.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Substituting kernel-specific information-gain growth into GP-UCB's generic bound produces polylogarithmic capacity for squared-exponential kernels and polynomial capacity for Matérn kernels.
knowledge_statements.title: Kernel-Specific GP-UCB Rates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the leaf and the substitutions are algebraically consistent with the displayed classical information-gain estimates, but the Matérn exponent and logarithmic factors are version-dependent and require a precise source.

children.title: Posterior-Sampling Regret
children.top_down_role: Bayesian and frequentist regret families for Thompson-style kernel optimization.

children.title: GP Thompson-Sampling Bayesian Regret
children.top_down_role: Prior-averaged performance theory for posterior function sampling.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for interpreting GP Thompson-sampling regret as a prior-averaged guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact GP Thompson-sampling Bayesian-regret claim averages over the prior and observation law used to construct the posterior. If the data-generating objective or observation law differs from that model, posterior probability matching with the true optimizer need not hold, and the modeled Bayesian-regret bound does not imply a uniform frequentist guarantee for the fixed truth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: GP Thompson-sampling Bayesian regret requires the modeled prior-predictive law and does not automatically become a fixed-function guarantee under misspecification.
assumptions_latex: The claimed result is a prior-predictive Bayesian-regret guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Model misspecification blocks automatic transfer to true fixed-objective regret.
knowledge_statements.title: Bayesian-Regret Model-Correctness Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional distributional identity underlying exact GP Thompson sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\widetilde f_t\) is conditionally independent of \(f\) given \(H_{t-1}\) and has the same posterior law. If both optimizers exist and use the same measurable tie-breaking rule, then for every measurable action set \(B\), \[\mathbb P(x_t\in B\mid H_{t-1})=\mathbb P(x^*\in B\mid H_{t-1}),\] where \(x_t\in\arg\max_x\widetilde f_t(x)\) and \(x^*\in\arg\max_x f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact GP Thompson sampling chooses actions according to the posterior distribution of the optimizer.
assumptions_latex: The posterior function sample is exact and conditionally independent of the latent objective.
Optimizers exist and a common measurable tie-breaking rule is used.

notation.meaning: Independent draw from the current posterior function law

knowledge_statements.title: Posterior Probability Matching

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prior-averaged regret of exact posterior function sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) and the observations follow the GP model used by the posterior. At round \(t\), draw \(\widetilde f_t\) independently from the posterior given \(H_{t-1}\) and choose \(x_t\in\arg\max_x\widetilde f_t(x)\). Let \(x^*\) be the correspondingly tie-broken optimizer, \(\Delta_t=\mathbb E[f(x^*)-f(x_t)\mid H_{t-1}]\), and \(g_t=I(x^*;(x_t,Y_t)\mid H_{t-1})\). If \(\Delta_t^2\le\Gamma g_t\) almost surely, then \[\operatorname{BayesRegret}(T)\le\sqrt{\Gamma T I(x^*;H_T)}\le\sqrt{\Gamma T I(f;H_T)}\le\sqrt{\Gamma T\gamma_T},\] where \(\gamma_T\) upper-bounds information about \(f\) obtainable from every allowed adaptive length-T experiment under the stated observation model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact GP Thompson sampling inherits an information-ratio Bayesian regret bound, with optimizer information bounded by information about the latent GP.
assumptions_latex: The prior-predictive objective and observation laws are correctly specified.
Posterior samples are exact and conditionally independent of the latent objective.
Optimizers exist with common measurable tie-breaking.
A finite uniform information-ratio bound \(\Gamma\) holds.

notation.meaning: Adaptive information-capacity upper bound for the latent GP

knowledge_statements.title: GP Thompson-Sampling Information-Ratio Regret Bound
GP Thompson-Sampling Bayesian Regret
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-ratio Bayesian regret bound for posterior sampling from a Gaussian-process model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\) have a Gaussian-process prior on an action set \(\mathcal X\), let \(x^*\in\arg\max_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)\), and observe \(y_t=f(x_t)+\varepsilon_t\). At round \(t\), Thompson sampling draws \(\widetilde f_t\) from the posterior and selects \(x_t\in\arg\max_x\widetilde f_t(x)\). Given the history \(H_{t-1}\), define \(\Delta_t=\mathbb E[f(x^*)-f(x_t)\mid H_{t-1}]\) and \(g_t=I(x^*;(x_t,y_t)\mid H_{t-1})\). If \(\Delta_t^2\leq\Gamma g_t\) almost surely for every \(t\), then \[\operatorname{BayesRegret}(T)\leq\sqrt{\Gamma T I(x^*;H_T)}\leq\sqrt{\Gamma T\gamma_T},\] where \(\gamma_T\) bounds the information obtainable about \(f\) from \(T\) noisy observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform information-ratio bound converts the information gained by GP Thompson sampling into Bayesian cumulative regret of order the square root of horizon times information gain.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) follows the stated Gaussian-process prior and the observation model is the one used by the posterior.
Posterior samples are conditionally independent draws given \(H_{t-1}\).
\(\Delta_t^2/g_t\leq\Gamma\), with ratio zero when both quantities vanish.

notation.meaning: Conditional information gained about the optimal action.
Upper bound on maximum T-round information gain about the GP.

review_flags: Exact GP Thompson-sampling theorem and hypotheses require an authoritative source locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem fits the Bayesian-regret container, but no citation verifies the information-ratio hypothesis or the comparison between information about the optimizer and GP information gain.

children.title: Kernelized Thompson-Sampling Frequentist Regret
children.top_down_role: Fixed-objective performance theory for randomized kernel policies.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard proof conditions distinguishing fixed-objective kernelized Thompson analysis from Bayesian probability matching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A standard width-summation analysis for a fixed \(f\in\mathcal H_k\) combines: (i) a high-probability event \(|f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)|\le b_t s_{t-1}(x)\) over the relevant actions and rounds; (ii) conditional anti-concentration of the randomized score, providing a uniformly positive probability of optimism near an optimizer; and (iii) a bound on accumulated posterior widths. Width summability alone does not imply the policy-specific conditional regret-width inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard frequentist kernelized Thompson proof combines confidence, random-score optimism, and width summability; variance control alone is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: The objective is fixed in an RKHS ball.
The randomized score is measurable from the history and auxiliary randomness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Confidence, anti-concentration, and width summability are distinct interfaces in the standard regret argument.
knowledge_statements.title: Confidence and Anti-Concentration Proof Interface

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Under-Dispersion Breaks the Standard Optimism Argument
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the standard frequentist proof interface when randomized scores lack optimism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a randomized kernel score has no uniform positive conditional probability of exceeding its posterior mean by the confidence error at an unobserved optimizer, then its anti-concentration constant may be zero. The RKHS confidence event alone consequently does not imply a finite-constant inequality of the form \[\mathbb E[f(x^*)-f(x_t)\mid H_{t-1}]\le c b_T\mathbb E[s_{t-1}(x_t)\mid H_{t-1}].\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An under-dispersed randomized score can lack optimism at the true optimizer, so confidence alone cannot support the standard Thompson regret argument.
assumptions_latex: The randomized score lacks a uniform positive optimism probability at an optimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The standard conditional regret-width inequality does not follow from confidence alone.
knowledge_statements.title: Under-Dispersion Breaks the Standard Optimism Argument

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Randomized kernel-score family used in fixed-objective analyses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(H_{t-1}\), kernel-ridge mean \(\mu_{t-1}\), posterior covariance \(C_{t-1}\), candidate set \(D_t\), and inflation \(v_t>0\), draw \[G_t\mid H_{t-1}\sim\operatorname{GP}(\mu_{t-1},v_t^2C_{t-1})\] and choose \(x_t\in\arg\max_{x\in D_t}G_t(x)\) with declared measurable tie-breaking. The candidate sets, inflation schedule, regularization, and noise update are part of the algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-objective kernel Thompson policies maximize a randomized kernel score whose variance may be inflated to obtain optimism.
assumptions_latex: The conditional Gaussian score is well defined on \(D_t\).
A measurably tie-broken maximizer exists.
\(D_t\), \(v_t\), regularization, and the noise update are specified.

notation.meaning: Kernel posterior covariance used for scoring

knowledge_statements.title: Variance-Inflated Kernel Thompson Score
Kernelized Thompson-Sampling Frequentist Regret
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional frequentist regret calculus for a fixed RKHS objective and randomized posterior-like scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(f\in\mathcal H_k\) and noisy observations \(y_t=f(x_t)+\varepsilon_t\). Let \(s_{t-1}(x)\) be the kernel posterior standard deviation computed before round \(t\). Suppose a kernelized Thompson policy and its confidence event \(E\) satisfy \(\mathbb P(E)\geq1-\delta\) and, on \(E\), \(\mathbb E[f(x^*)-f(x_t)\mid H_{t-1}]\leq c\beta_T\mathbb E[s_{t-1}(x_t)\mid H_{t-1}]\). If every adaptive design obeys \(\sum_{t=1}^T s_{t-1}^2(x_t)\leq C_k\gamma_T\), then \[\mathbb E[R_T\mathbf1_E]\leq c\beta_T\sqrt{C_kT\gamma_T}.\] If instantaneous regret is at most \(L\), then \(\mathbb E R_T\leq c\beta_T\sqrt{C_kT\gamma_T}+\delta LT\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A kernelized Thompson policy has sublinear frequentist regret whenever its conditional regret is controlled by posterior width and accumulated squared widths are controlled by information gain.
assumptions_latex: \(f\in\mathcal H_k\) is fixed and the noise supports the stated confidence event.
The randomized policy satisfies the displayed conditional width bound on \(E\).
Instantaneous regret is bounded by \(L\) for the unconditional estimate.

notation.meaning: Reproducing-kernel Hilbert space of kernel k.
Cumulative regret against a maximizer of the fixed objective.

review_flags: Policy-specific confidence and anti-concentration constants require a kernelized Thompson-sampling source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The frequentist role and theorem kind fit, but a kernelized Thompson-sampling source is needed to justify the event-conditioned width inequality, its passage to expected regret, and the constants and confidence parameter.

children.title: Other Policy-Specific Regret Families
children.top_down_role: Regret analyses whose proof architecture differs from canonical GP-UCB.

children.title: Improvement-Based Regret
children.top_down_role: Cumulative-performance analysis for improvement policies, including noise-adjusted variants.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Adjusted Expected Improvement for Cumulative Regret Minimization in Noisy Bayesian Optimization
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Adjusted Expected Improvement for Cumulative Regret Minimization in Noisy Bayesian Optimization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Improvement policies formed by explicitly scaling posterior uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\omega_t>0\), define \(Z_t(x)\mid H_{t-1}\sim N(\mu_{t-1}(x),\omega_t^2s_{t-1}^2(x))\) and choose \[x_t\in\arg\max_{x\in\mathcal X}\mathbb E[(Z_t(x)-m_{t-1})_+\mid H_{t-1}].\] The choice \(\omega_t=1\) recovers the corresponding unscaled latent EI score. A regret claim for this family must specify \(m_{t-1}\), \(\omega_t\), and the observation-noise update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exploration-scaled EI inflates or contracts posterior uncertainty before computing improvement; its scale and noisy incumbent define the actual policy.
assumptions_latex: Posterior means and standard deviations are defined.
The incumbent and scale sequence are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy maximizes scaled posterior expected improvement.
knowledge_statements.title: Exploration-Scaled Expected-Improvement Family

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step latent improvement score and its noise-dependent incumbent convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For maximization, suppose \(F(x)\mid H_{t-1}\sim N(\mu_{t-1}(x),s_{t-1}^2(x))\), and declare an incumbent \(m_{t-1}\). Then \[\operatorname{EI}_t(x)=\mathbb E[(F(x)-m_{t-1})_+\mid H_{t-1}] =(\mu_{t-1}(x)-m_{t-1})\Phi(z_t(x))+s_{t-1}(x)\phi(z_t(x)),\] where \(z_t(x)=(\mu_{t-1}(x)-m_{t-1})/s_{t-1}(x)\) when \(s_{t-1}(x)>0\), and \(\operatorname{EI}_t(x)=(\mu_{t-1}(x)-m_{t-1})_+\) when \(s_{t-1}(x)=0\). Under observation noise, raw-observation and posterior-latent incumbent conventions define different policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected improvement is posterior expected positive latent gain over a declared incumbent; noisy incumbent conventions must be specified.
assumptions_latex: The one-point latent posterior is Gaussian.
The incumbent convention is explicitly declared.

notation.meaning: Standard normal distribution and density functions

knowledge_statements.title: Posterior Expected-Improvement Score

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear Regret from a Misspecified Noisy EI Surrogate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fully specified two-action failure of posterior-latent expected improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X=\{a,b\}\), with truth \(f(a)=0\), \(f(b)=\Delta>0\). The surrogate has independent coordinates, prior \(F(a)\sim N(0,\tau^2)\), deterministic \(F(b)=-1\), and observations at \(a\) have variance \(\sigma^2>0\). At every round let the incumbent be \(m_{t-1}=\mu_{t-1}(a)\), compute latent EI, break ties toward \(a\), and maximize EI. After any finite number of observations at \(a\), its latent posterior standard deviation is positive, so \(\operatorname{EI}_t(a)=s_{t-1}(a)/\sqrt{2\pi}>0\), while \(\operatorname{EI}_t(b)=0\). Thus \(x_t=a\) for every \(t\) and \(R_T=T\Delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coherent but misspecified noisy surrogate can remain uncertain at a suboptimal action and deterministically exclude the true optimum, causing linear EI regret.
assumptions_latex: The stated surrogate, noise model, posterior-latent incumbent, and tie-breaking rule define the policy.
The true objective need not be generated by the surrogate.

notation.meaning: Surrogate prior variance at a and observation-noise variance

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Regret from a Misspecified Noisy EI Surrogate
Improvement-Based Regret
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of unforced improvement maximization under a degenerate or misspecified noisy surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X=\{a,b\}\) with true values \(f(b)=f(a)+\Delta\) for \(\Delta>0\). Consider a noisy improvement policy whose surrogate assigns \(b\) a fixed mean below the incumbent and zero predictive variance, while repeated observations at \(a\) retain positive predictive noise variance. Then the surrogate expected improvement satisfies \(\operatorname{EI}_t(b)=0\) and \(\operatorname{EI}_t(a)>0\) at every round. Consequently the policy selects \(x_t=a\) for all \(t\), so \[R_T=\sum_{t=1}^T(f(b)-f(x_t))=T\Delta.\] Thus improvement maximization alone provides no sublinear-regret guarantee without calibrated uncertainty or an explicit exploration condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected improvement can incur linear regret when the surrogate is overconfident at the true optimum and noisy incumbent evaluations keep another point’s improvement positive.
assumptions_latex: The surrogate variance at \(b\) remains zero and its mean remains below the incumbent.
The noisy improvement calculation gives strictly positive improvement at \(a\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_T=T\Delta\), so the policy is not no-regret.

notation.meaning: Surrogate expected improvement at round t.
True optimality gap between b and a.

review_flags: A published noisy expected-improvement failure result or matching counterexample locator is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A failure boundary is suitable here, but the asserted noisy-EI behavior depends on an incompletely specified surrogate and incumbent convention. A published matching construction or authoritative locator is required.

children.title: Information-Directed Regret
children.top_down_role: Regret controlled through explicit loss–information tradeoffs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Action-distribution choice minimizing squared conditional regret per unit information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(H_{t-1}\), let \(q\) range over admissible distributions on actions, with \(A_t\sim q\) conditionally independent of the latent environment given the history. Define \(\Delta_t(q)=\mathbb E[f(A^*)-f(A_t)\mid H_{t-1}]\), \(g_t(q)=I(A^*;(A_t,Y_t)\mid H_{t-1})\), and \[\Psi_t(q)=\frac{\Delta_t(q)^2}{g_t(q)}.\] Set \(\Psi_t(q)=0\) when \(\Delta_t(q)=g_t(q)=0\), and \(\Psi_t(q)=+\infty\) when \(g_t(q)=0<\Delta_t(q)\). Information-directed sampling selects a minimizer of \(\Psi_t(q)\) and draws from it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Information-directed sampling chooses an action distribution minimizing squared conditional regret per unit information about the optimizer.
assumptions_latex: Conditional regret and mutual information are well defined.
The randomized action distribution depends only on the observed history.
knowledge_statements.title: Information-Directed Sampling Rule

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary at which finite information-ratio control is impossible.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If, on an event of positive probability, every admissible \(q\) has \(g_t(q)=0\) and \(\Delta_t(q)>0\), then \(\Psi_t(q)=+\infty\) for every admissible \(q\). Consequently no finite uniform information-ratio constant applies on that event.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every available experiment incurs positive conditional regret while revealing no information about the optimizer, the information ratio is infinite.
assumptions_latex: Every admissible action distribution has zero one-step information gain.
Every admissible action distribution has positive conditional regret.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Information Positive-Regret Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic chain-rule regret theorem for information-directed policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A^*\) be a prior-random optimal action, \(\Delta_t=\mathbb E[f(A^*)-f(A_t)\mid H_{t-1}]\), and \(g_t=I(A^*;(A_t,Y_t)\mid H_{t-1})\). If \(\Delta_t^2\le\Gamma g_t\) almost surely for every \(t\), then \[\operatorname{BayesRegret}(T)\le\sqrt{\Gamma T\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbb E g_t}=\sqrt{\Gamma T I(A^*;H_T)}\le\sqrt{\Gamma T H(A^*)}.\] The entropy bound applies when \(H(A^*)<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly controlling squared conditional regret per unit information bounds Bayesian cumulative regret by total optimizer information and, when finite, optimizer entropy.
assumptions_latex: Conditional regrets and mutual informations are finite.
\(\Delta_t^2\le\Gamma g_t\) almost surely for every round.
The entropy corollary requires discrete or otherwise entropy-defined \(A^*\) with finite entropy.

notation.meaning: Conditional one-round information about the optimizer

knowledge_statements.title: Information-Ratio Bayesian Regret Theorem
Information-Directed Regret
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic Bayesian regret theorem based on conditional squared loss per unit information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A^*\) be an optimal action under a prior, and let \(H_{t-1}\) be the history before action \(A_t\). Define the conditional expected regret \(\Delta_t=\mathbb E[f(A^*)-f(A_t)\mid H_{t-1}]\), information gain \(g_t=I(A^*;(A_t,Y_t)\mid H_{t-1})\), and information ratio \(\Psi_t=\Delta_t^2/g_t\), with \(\Psi_t=0\) when \(\Delta_t=g_t=0\). If an information-directed policy ensures \(\Psi_t\leq\Gamma\) almost surely, then \[\operatorname{BayesRegret}(T)\leq\sqrt{\Gamma T\sum_{t=1}^T\mathbb E g_t}=\sqrt{\Gamma T I(A^*;H_T)}.\] In particular, entropy finiteness gives \(\operatorname{BayesRegret}(T)\leq\sqrt{\Gamma T H(A^*)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Controlling squared conditional regret per unit information bounds Bayesian cumulative regret by the square root of horizon times total information about the optimal action.
assumptions_latex: Conditional regrets and mutual informations are finite.
The policy satisfies \(\Psi_t\leq\Gamma\) almost surely for every round.

notation.meaning: One-round conditional mutual information about the optimal action.

review_flags: The standard information-ratio theorem needs an exact authoritative theorem locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The information-ratio theorem is mathematically standard and matches the container, but the record has no source or inspectable theorem locator.

children.top_down_role: Algorithm-independent limitations for noisy kernel optimization.

children.title: Kernel-Smoothness Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Limitations indexed by the regularity of the kernel class.

knowledge_statements.title: Kernel-Smoothness Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Packing-based minimax lower-bound template whose packing radius is determined by kernel regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F_B=\{f\in\mathcal H_k:\lVert f\rVert_k\leq B\}\). Suppose \(\mathcal F_B\) contains functions \(f_1,\ldots,f_M\), each with a distinct maximizing region, such that playing outside the maximizing region of \(f_i\) loses at least \(\Delta\). Under Gaussian noise of variance \(\sigma^2\), assume every adaptive \(T\)-query experiment satisfies \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_i\Vert P_0)\leq\alpha\log M\) relative to a reference experiment, for a sufficiently small universal \(\alpha\). Then there is a universal \(c>0\) such that \[\inf_\pi\sup_{f\in\mathcal F_B}\mathbb E_f R_T(\pi)\geq cT\Delta.\] Kernel smoothness enters through the largest feasible packing size \(M=M_k(B,\Delta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If an RKHS ball contains many statistically indistinguishable separated peaks, every policy suffers cumulative regret proportional to horizon times their gap; kernel smoothness controls the packing size.
assumptions_latex: The stated separated-peak family lies in the radius-\(B\) RKHS ball.
Observation noise is Gaussian with variance \(\sigma^2\).
The adaptive experiment satisfies the displayed KL indistinguishability condition.

notation.meaning: Radius-B ball in the RKHS of k.
Law of the adaptive observations under objective f_i.

review_flags: Kernel-specific packing constructions and resulting exponents require authoritative lower-bound sources.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind is appropriate, but this is only a generic packing template: it does not identify a kernel regularity class, packing construction, or smoothness-dependent rate, and the stated KL condition needs authoritative support.

children.title: Dimension-Noise Lower-Bound Regimes
children.top_down_role: Limitations driven by search dimension and observation noise.

children.title: Dimension-Dependent Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Performance limitations driven by search-space dimension.

knowledge_statements.title: Dimension-Dependent Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension dependence obtained from an exponentially large family of separated alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a \(d\)-dimensional domain and a function class containing \(M\geq2^d\) alternatives with distinct optimal regions and loss at least \(\Delta\) outside the correct region. Suppose observations have Gaussian noise variance \(\sigma^2\), and the alternatives are constructed so that every adaptive \(T\)-query policy has pairwise information bounded by \(T\Delta^2/(2\sigma^2)\). If \(T\Delta^2/(2\sigma^2)\leq c_0d\) for a sufficiently small universal \(c_0\), then Fano-type testing yields \[\inf_\pi\sup_f\mathbb E_fR_T(\pi)\geq c_1T\Delta.\] Choosing \(\Delta=c_2\sigma\sqrt{d/T}\) gives \(\inf_\pi\sup_f\mathbb E_fR_T(\pi)\geq c_3\sigma\sqrt{dT}\), provided that gap is feasible in the function class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exponential-in-dimension packing of indistinguishable objectives forces minimax cumulative regret of order noise times the square root of dimension and horizon.
assumptions_latex: The function class contains the stated \(2^d\)-sized separated packing.
The selected gap \(\Delta\) is feasible within the class.
Observations have independent Gaussian noise of variance \(\sigma^2\).

notation.meaning: Loss outside the alternative’s optimal region.

review_flags: The applicable kernel class and dimension-dependent packing construction are unspecified.
Exact constants and effective-dimension interpretation require a source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed dimension-dependent rate cannot be reviewed reliably without the intended function or kernel class, a precise meaning of dimension, and a source for the adaptive packing and information bound.

children.title: Noise-Dependent Lower Bounds
children.top_down_role: Performance limitations driven by observation uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.title: Noise-Dependent Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-alternative lower bound isolating the effect of observation-noise scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a function class contain two objectives \(f_0,f_1\) whose optimal regions differ and for which choosing the wrong region incurs gap \(\Delta\). Assume independent Gaussian observation noise with variance \(\sigma^2\) and that, under any adaptive \(T\)-query policy, the induced laws satisfy \(D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P_0\Vert P_1)\leq T\Delta^2/(2\sigma^2)\). If \(T\Delta^2/(2\sigma^2)\leq c_0\), binary testing implies \[\inf_\pi\max_{i\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_iR_T(\pi)\geq c_1T\Delta.\] When the class permits \(\Delta=c_2\sigma/\sqrt T\), this becomes \(\inf_\pi\max_i\mathbb E_iR_T(\pi)\geq c_3\sigma\sqrt T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two objectives hidden by Gaussian noise force cumulative regret proportional to the noise standard deviation times the square root of the horizon.
assumptions_latex: The class contains two alternatives with different optimal regions and gap \(\Delta\).
The induced adaptive observation laws obey the displayed KL bound.
The gap \(c_2\sigma/\sqrt T\) is feasible in the class.

notation.meaning: Adaptive observation law under objective f_i.
Regret gap between the two optimal regions.

review_flags: A source is needed for the precise two-alternative construction within the intended kernel class.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lower-bound role and complexity-bound kind fit, but the two alternatives and their adaptive KL bound are not specified sufficiently to establish the claimed noise-dependent rate within the intended class.

children.title: Joint Dimension–Noise Regimes
children.top_down_role: Lower-bound behavior when dimensionality and feedback noise jointly constrain search.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Dimension–Noise Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Packing lower bound exhibiting the coupled dimension, noise, horizon, and amplitude regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a bounded function class contain at least \(M\geq2^d\) separated alternatives with attainable gap up to \(B\), and suppose observations have Gaussian noise variance \(\sigma^2\). If their adaptive observation laws have KL divergence at most \(T\Delta^2/(2\sigma^2)\), choose \(\Delta=c_0\min\{B,\sigma\sqrt{d/T}\}\). For sufficiently small universal \(c_0\), the testing error remains bounded away from zero, and hence \[\inf_\pi\sup_f\mathbb E_fR_T(\pi)\geq c_1T\min\{B,\sigma\sqrt{d/T}\}=c_1\min\{BT,\sigma\sqrt{dT}\}.\] The transition occurs near \(T\asymp\sigma^2d/B^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dimension-sized packing yields linear regret before noise permits identification and square-root dimension–noise regret afterward, with a transition set by amplitude.
assumptions_latex: The class contains the stated exponentially large packing with gaps through \(B\).
Adaptive KL divergence is bounded by \(T\Delta^2/(2\sigma^2)\).
Observation noise is independent Gaussian with variance \(\sigma^2\).
review_flags: The intended kernel-specific joint regime and packing feasibility require an authoritative source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The joint-regime form is plausible, but the exponential packing, attainable gaps through B, adaptive KL inequality, and transition rate all require a kernel-specific authoritative source.

children.title: Simple-Regret Guarantee
children.top_down_role: Canonical terminal-quality guarantee under alternative search and recommendation mechanisms.

children.title: Online-to-Simple-Regret Conversion
children.top_down_role: Terminal guarantees inherited from cumulative-regret control.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic conversion from cumulative regret to best latent queried-point regret.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(g_t=f(x^*)-f(x_t)\geq0\) and \(R_T=\sum_{t=1}^Tg_t\), let \(x_T^{\mathrm{best}}\in\arg\max_{1\leq t\leq T}f(x_t)\). Then \[f(x^*)-f(x_T^{\mathrm{best}})=\min_{1\leq t\leq T}g_t\leq\frac{R_T}{T}.\] More generally, if a terminal rule returns a queried point \(\widehat x_T\) satisfying \(f(x_T^{\mathrm{best}})-f(\widehat x_T)\leq\eta_T\), then \[f(x^*)-f(\widehat x_T)\leq R_T/T+\eta_T.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The best latent queried point has simple regret at most average cumulative regret; imperfect noisy selection adds its terminal-selection error.
assumptions_latex: All instantaneous regrets use the same fixed objective and comparator.

notation.meaning: Terminal error relative to the best queried point

knowledge_statements.title: Best-Queried-Point Conversion
Online-to-Simple-Regret Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected simple-regret conversion by recommending a uniformly sampled queried action.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\in\arg\max_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)\), and let an arbitrary adaptive policy query \(x_1,\ldots,x_T\). Define cumulative regret \(R_T=\sum_{t=1}^T(f(x^*)-f(x_t))\). Independently of the data, draw \(\tau\) uniformly from \(\{1,\ldots,T\}\) and recommend \(\widehat x_T=x_\tau\). Conditional on the queried sequence, \[\mathbb E[f(x^*)-f(\widehat x_T)\mid x_1,\ldots,x_T]=\frac{R_T}{T}.\] Therefore \(\mathbb E[f(x^*)-f(\widehat x_T)]=\mathbb E[R_T]/T\). In particular, any cumulative-regret bound \(\mathbb E R_T\leq B_T\) yields expected simple regret at most \(B_T/T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recommending a uniformly random queried point converts any expected cumulative-regret bound into an expected simple-regret bound divided by the horizon.
assumptions_latex: \(x^*\) maximizes the fixed objective \(f\) over \(\mathcal X\).
\(\tau\) is uniform on \(\{1,\ldots,T\}\) and independent of the observations and policy randomness.
\(\mathbb E[R_T]\) is finite.

notation.meaning: Cumulative regret of the queried sequence.
Upper bound on expected cumulative regret.
Uniformly sampled query index used for the recommendation.

review_flags: An authoritative source with a specific locator is required for the online-to-simple-regret conversion.

children.title: Direct Pure-Exploration Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Terminal guarantees designed without an online-reward objective.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Terminal certificate for a finite pure-exploration candidate set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be finite and suppose random intervals \([L_T(x),U_T(x)]\) satisfy \(\Pr\{f(x)\in[L_T(x),U_T(x)]\ \forall x\in C\}\geq1-\delta\). If \(\widehat x\in\arg\max_{x\in C}L_T(x)\), then, on that event, \[\max_{x\in C}f(x)-f(\widehat x)\leq \max_{x\in C}U_T(x)-\max_{x\in C}L_T(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneous confidence intervals turn their upper-versus-lower envelope gap into a high-probability finite-set simple-regret certificate.
assumptions_latex: The intervals cover every candidate simultaneously with probability at least \(1-\delta\).
The displayed maxima exist.

notation.meaning: Simple regret relative to the best member of C

knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous-Band Simple-Regret Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of finite-set regret certification from merely pointwise confidence intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Bounds satisfying \(\Pr\{f(x)\in[L_T(x),U_T(x)]\}\geq1-\delta\) separately for each \(x\in C\) need not cover all candidates on one event. After selecting or maximizing over \(C\), the simultaneous-band regret certificate is therefore unavailable unless multiplicity, selection, and any adaptive stopping are included in the coverage guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pointwise confidence intervals do not by themselves certify regret after selection across multiple candidates.
assumptions_latex: Only marginal pointwise coverage, rather than joint simultaneous coverage, has been established.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise-Coverage Selection Boundary
Direct Pure-Exploration Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-budget uniform exploration guarantee for finitely many sub-Gaussian alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X=\{1,\ldots,K\}\), and suppose each evaluation of action \(i\) has mean \(f(i)\) and independent \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian noise. Allocate \(n=\lfloor T/K\rfloor\geq1\) evaluations to every action, let \(\overline Y_i\) be its empirical mean, and recommend \(\widehat i\in\arg\max_i\overline Y_i\). Then, with probability at least \(1-\delta\), \[f(i^*)-f(\widehat i)\leq2\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2\log(2K/\delta)}{n}},\] where \(i^*\in\arg\max_i f(i)\). Consequently simple regret at most \(\varepsilon\) is ensured by \(T\geq K\lceil8\sigma^2\varepsilon^{-2}\log(2K/\delta)\rceil\), up to unused remainder evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly replicating every finite action and selecting the largest sample mean achieves epsilon simple regret with order K noise-variance over epsilon-squared evaluations.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) contains exactly \(K\) actions.
Noise variables are independent, centered, and \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian.
Each action receives at least \(n=\lfloor T/K\rfloor\) evaluations.

notation.meaning: Mean of the n evaluations of action i.

review_flags: A finite-arm pure-exploration concentration reference with constants is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-action pure-exploration guarantee and complexity-bound kind fit the leaf, but the high-probability constants and sample-complexity statement lack a specific source locator.

children.title: Posterior-Recommendation Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Terminal guarantees for recommendations chosen from posterior summaries.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional posterior guarantee for a posterior-mean terminal recommendation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given history \(H_T\), suppose \[\Pr\{|f(x)-\mu_T(x)|\leq w_T(x)\ \forall x\in\mathcal X\mid H_T\}\geq1-\delta.\] If \(\widehat x_T\in\arg\max_x\mu_T(x)\), then, conditionally on \(H_T\), with probability at least \(1-\delta\), \[\sup_x f(x)-f(\widehat x_T)\leq 2\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}w_T(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simultaneous posterior band converts a posterior-mean recommendation into a high-posterior-probability simple-regret bound.
assumptions_latex: The simultaneous posterior band is valid conditionally on \(H_T\).
The posterior-mean maximizer exists; objective maxima may equivalently be interpreted using suprema.

notation.meaning: Posterior law after the terminal history

knowledge_statements.title: Posterior Uniform-Band Regret Certificate
Posterior-Recommendation Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bayes-optimal terminal recommendation under posterior expected simple loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given terminal history \(H_T\), let \(f\) have posterior distribution \(\Pi_T\), posterior mean \(\mu_T(x)=\mathbb E[f(x)\mid H_T]\), and posterior simple loss \(L(a,f)=\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)-f(a)\). Whenever the conditional expectations and maximizers exist, every posterior Bayes recommendation satisfies \[\widehat x_T\in\arg\min_{a\in\mathcal X}\mathbb E[L(a,f)\mid H_T]=\arg\max_{a\in\mathcal X}\mu_T(a).\] Its conditional Bayes simple regret is \[\mathbb E[L(\widehat x_T,f)\mid H_T]=\mathbb E[\sup_x f(x)\mid H_T]-\sup_x\mu_T(x).\] Thus any bound on this posterior optimality gap is directly a terminal Bayes-regret guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximizing the posterior mean is Bayes-optimal for simple regret, and its conditional regret equals expected posterior maximum minus maximum posterior mean.
assumptions_latex: The posterior expectations of \(f(a)\) and \(\sup_x f(x)\) are finite.
The displayed minimizing and maximizing actions exist.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x_T\in\arg\max_a\mu_T(a)\) and \(\mathbb E[L(\widehat x_T,f)\mid H_T]=\mathbb E[\sup_xf(x)\mid H_T]-\sup_x\mu_T(x)\).

notation.meaning: Posterior distribution of the objective after T observations.

review_flags: A Bayesian decision-theory or Bayesian-optimization source locator is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property correctly expresses the posterior Bayes action for simple loss and fits the terminal container, but no decision-theory or Bayesian-optimization source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Validation-Aware Terminal Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Terminal guarantees incorporating confirmation evaluations or replication.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validation guarantee using simultaneous intervals under unequal or adaptively stopped replication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a search stage produce a finite set \(C\), and let validation intervals \([L_x,U_x]\), possibly based on unequal and adaptively stopped replication counts, satisfy \[\Pr\{f(x)\in[L_x,U_x]\ \forall x\in C\mid C\}\geq1-\delta.\] If \(\widehat x\in\arg\max_{x\in C}L_x\), then with probability at least \(1-\delta\), \[\sup_{z\in\mathcal X}f(z)-f(\widehat x)\leq r_C+\max_{x\in C}U_x-\max_{x\in C}L_x,\] where \(r_C=\sup_zf(z)-\max_{x\in C}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneously valid validation intervals separate global regret into candidate-generation error and a reportable validation gap, including under unequal adaptive replication.
assumptions_latex: Conditional simultaneous coverage remains valid under the validation allocation and stopping rule.
The candidate set is fixed before the validation streams used for the certificate, or the coverage guarantee accounts for its adaptivity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r(\widehat x)\leq r_C+\max_xU_x-\max_xL_x\) with probability at least \(1-\delta\).

notation.meaning: Final simultaneously valid validation interval for candidate x

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive-Replication Validation Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of naive holdout concentration after data-dependent candidate construction or stopping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the same validation observations are used to construct \(C\), select among candidates, or choose replication stopping times, fixed-sample pointwise intervals need not satisfy \(\Pr\{f(x)\in[L_x,U_x]\ \forall x\in C\}\geq1-\delta\). Consequently the validation gap is not a valid terminal-regret certificate unless independence, simultaneous selective inference, or anytime-valid confidence sequences restore the required coverage event.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive reuse of validation data invalidates naive fixed-sample guarantees unless inference accounts for selection and stopping.
assumptions_latex: The nominal intervals are justified only for fixed candidates and fixed sample sizes.
Candidate selection or stopping depends on the same observations.
knowledge_statements.title: Validation Reuse Boundary
Validation-Aware Terminal Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Replicated validation of a finite candidate set with a separate candidate-generation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a search stage produce a finite candidate set \(C\) of size \(m\), independently of subsequent validation noise. Evaluate each \(x\in C\) exactly \(n\) times with independent centered \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian validation noise, let \(\overline Y(x)\) be its validation mean, and output \(\widehat x\in\arg\max_{x\in C}\overline Y(x)\). With probability at least \(1-\delta\), \[\max_{x\in C}f(x)-f(\widehat x)\leq2\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2\log(2m/\delta)}{n}}.\] Hence, writing \(r_C=\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)-\max_{x\in C}f(x)\), the global terminal regret is at most \(r_C+2\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2m/\delta)/n}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent replicated validation separates terminal regret into candidate-generation error and a finite-sample selection error controlled by noise, replications, and candidate-set size.
assumptions_latex: The candidate set is fixed before the independent validation samples are drawn.
Validation noise is centered, independent, and \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian.
Every candidate receives exactly \(n\) validation evaluations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_xf(x)-f(\widehat x)\leq r_C+2\sigma\sqrt{2\log(2m/\delta)/n}\) with probability at least \(1-\delta\).

notation.meaning: Finite set produced by the search stage.
Approximation error of the best candidate in C.
Mean of the independent validation evaluations at x.

knowledge_statements.title: Expected-Improvement Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional noiseless EI rate obtained from geometric coverage and Hölder regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) be compact, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be \(\alpha\)-Hölder with constant \(L\), and let \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) be points selected by noiseless expected improvement. Define \(h_n=\sup_{x\in X}\min_{1\le i\le n}\lVert x-x_i\rVert\) and \(r_n=\min_{1\le i\le n}f(x_i)-\min_{x\in X}f(x)\). If the EI design satisfies \(h_n\le Cn^{-1/d}\), then \[r_n\le Lh_n^\alpha\le LC^\alpha n^{-\alpha/d}.\] Thus the evaluation budget sufficient for \(r_n\le\varepsilon\) is at most \(\lceil(LC^\alpha/\varepsilon)^{d/\alpha}\rceil\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An EI design with fill distance of order n^{-1/d} has simple regret of order n^{-α/d} on α-Hölder objectives.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) is compact.
\(|f(x)-f(y)|\le L\lVert x-y\rVert^\alpha\) for all \(x,y\in X\).

notation.meaning: fill distance of the first n evaluation points
best-sample simple regret after n evaluations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional Hölder/coverage calculation is coherent and the complexity_bound kind fits the terminal rate container, but no source verifies that noiseless expected improvement satisfies the assumed fill-distance rate. Without that result, this is only a generic space-filling-design bound rather than a supported EI rate.

children.title: Smoothness Dependence

assumptions_latex: \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) is compact and \(d\ge 1\).
\(0<\alpha\le 1\) and \(|f(x)-f(y)|\le L\lVert x-y\rVert^\alpha\) for all \(x,y\in X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_n\le LC^\alpha n^{-\alpha/d}\), so the polynomial decay exponent is \(\alpha/d\).

notation.meaning: fill distance of the first n design points

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of a noiseless coverage-based regret exponent on the ordinary Hölder exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subset\mathbb R^d\) be compact, let \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\in X\), and define \(h_n=\sup_{x\in X}\min_{1\le i\le n}\lVert x-x_i\rVert\) and \(r_n=\min_{1\le i\le n}f(x_i)-\min_{x\in X}f(x)\). Fix \(d\ge1\). If \(0<\alpha\le1\), \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) satisfies \(|f(x)-f(y)|\le L\lVert x-y\rVert^\alpha\), and \(h_n\le Cn^{-1/d}\), then \[r_n\le Lh_n^\alpha\le LC^\alpha n^{-\alpha/d}.\] Thus, across Hölder classes for which the same coverage hypothesis is available, increasing \(\alpha\) increases the polynomial decay exponent \(\alpha/d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For ordinary Hölder objectives and fixed dimension, the coverage-based simple-regret exponent is α/d, so greater Hölder smoothness gives a larger polynomial exponent.
knowledge_statements.title: Smoothness Dependence

children.title: Dimension Dependence
children.top_down_role: Variation of terminal rates with search-space dimension.

assumptions_latex: \(X_d\subset\mathbb R^d\) is compact and \(d\ge1\).
\(0<\alpha\le1\) and \(f_d\) is \(\alpha\)-Hölder with constant \(L_d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_{n,d}le L_dC_d^\alpha n^{-\alpha/d}\), and \(n\ge(L_dC_d^\alpha/\varepsilon)^{d/\alpha}\) is sufficient for \(r_{n,d}\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: best-sample simple regret in dimension d

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dimension dependence of noiseless Hölder optimization under a dimension-indexed coverage bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each integer \(d\ge1\), let \(X_d\subset\mathbb R^d\) be compact and let \(x_{1,d},\ldots,x_{n,d}\in X_d\). Define \(h_{n,d}=\sup_{x\in X_d}\min_{1\le i\le n}\lVert x-x_{i,d}\rVert\) and \(r_{n,d}=\min_{1\le i\le n}f_d(x_{i,d})-inf_{x\in X_d}f_d(x)\). Fix \(0<\alpha\le1\). If \(f_d:X_d\to\mathbb R\) is \(\alpha\)-Hölder with constant \(L_d\) and \(h_{n,d}\le C_dn^{-1/d}\), then \[r_{n,d}\le L_dC_d^\alpha n^{-\alpha/d}.\] Hence the polynomial exponent \(\alpha/d\) decreases with \(d\); for each fixed \(d\), the stated bound guarantees \(r_{n,d}\le\varepsilon\) whenever \(n\ge(L_dC_d^\alpha/\varepsilon)^{d/\alpha}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With Hölder smoothness fixed, the coverage-based polynomial exponent is α/d and therefore decreases with dimension; the sufficient budget has ε-exponent d/α, with dimension-dependent constants retained.
knowledge_statements.title: Dimension Dependence

children.title: Smoothness–Dimension Interaction
children.top_down_role: Combined influence of regularity and dimensionality on terminal complexity.

assumptions_latex: \(0<\alpha_j\le1\) and \(d_j\in\mathbb N\) for \(j\in\{1,2\}\).
For each \(j\), the applicable simple-regret bound has polynomial exponent \(\alpha_j/d_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exponents are equal if and only if \(\alpha_1/d_1=\alpha_2/d_2\).

notation.meaning: Hölder exponent for comparison case j
ambient dimension for comparison case j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic interaction of smoothness and dimension in a coverage-based noiseless regret exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose two coverage-based noiseless optimization bounds have polynomial factors \(n^{-\alpha_1/d_1}\) and \(n^{-\alpha_2/d_2}\), where \(0<\alpha_j\le1\) and \(d_j\in\mathbb N\) for \(j\in\{1,2\}\). Their polynomial decay exponents are equal exactly when \[\frac{\alpha_1}{d_1}=\frac{\alpha_2}{d_2}.\] In particular, replacing \((\alpha,d)\) by \((q\alpha,qd)\) preserves the exponent whenever \(q>0\), \(qd\in\mathbb N\), and \(q\alpha\le1\). This compares polynomial exponents only; multiplicative constants may differ between the two problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coverage-based polynomial exponents depend on the ratio α/d. Proportional changes preserve that exponent when the resulting dimension and Hölder exponent remain admissible, although constants may change.
knowledge_statements.title: Smoothness–Dimension Interaction

children.title: Fixed-Budget Simple Regret
children.top_down_role: Recommendation quality after a prescribed number or cost of evaluations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-Budget Rates Require a Declared Problem Class
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary excluding model-free numerical simple-regret rates from the fixed-budget protocol alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_n(\mathcal F,\mathcal P)=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi_n}\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_{f,\mathcal P}[f(\widehat x_n)-\inf_x f(x)]\), where \(\mathcal P\) specifies the observation laws and \(\Pi_n\) the admissible fixed-budget policies and recommendation rules. A rate stated only as a function of \(n\) is not determined by the budget protocol: changing \(\mathcal F\), \(\mathcal P\), or \(\Pi_n\) can change the rate or make the risk infinite. Every fixed-budget rate must therefore declare these ingredients and its guarantee mode.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A budget alone does not determine a simple-regret rate; the objective class, observation model, admissible policies, recommendation rule, and guarantee mode must be specified.
assumptions_latex: Policies in \(\Pi_n\) obey the declared at-most or exactly \(n\) charged-observation protocol.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_n\text{ is determined by }(\mathcal F,\mathcal P,\Pi_n),\text{ not by }n\text{ alone}.\)

notation.meaning: Admissible fixed-budget policy and recommendation class.
Minimax fixed-budget simple-regret risk for the declared policy class.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Budget Rates Require a Declared Problem Class

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Recommendation and Best-Sampled Regret Need Not Coincide
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes terminal recommendation quality from the quality of the best queried design.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After queries \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), define \(r_n^{\mathrm{sample}}=\min_{1\le t\le n}f(x_t)-f^\star\) and \(r_n^{\mathrm{rec}}=f(\widehat x_n)-f^\star\), where \(f^\star=\inf_x f(x)\). If \(\widehat x_n\in\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\), then \(r_n^{\mathrm{rec}}\ge r_n^{\mathrm{sample}}\), with equality exactly when the recommendation is a latent-best sampled point. If unsampled recommendations are allowed, neither regret generally bounds the other.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The returned recommendation's regret differs from best-sampled regret, and their ordering depends on whether the recommendation must be a queried point.
assumptions_latex: \(f^\star=\inf_x f(x)>-\infty\).

notation.meaning: Latent regret of the best queried point.
Latent regret of the terminal recommendation.

knowledge_statements.title: Recommendation and Best-Sampled Regret Need Not Coincide

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform-Sampling Fixed-Budget Bound on a Finite Domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representative high-probability simple-regret upper bound under independent sub-Gaussian noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\{1,\ldots,K\}\). Suppose observations at arm \(i\) are independent with mean \(f(i)\) and \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian noise. For minimization and \(n\ge K\), sample every arm \(m=\lfloor n/K\rfloor\) times and recommend an empirical-mean minimizer \(\widehat i_n\). Then, for every \(\delta\in(0,1)\),
\[P\!\left(f(\widehat i_n)-\min_i f(i)\le2\sigma\sqrt{\frac{2\log(2K/\delta)}{m}}\right)\ge1-\delta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform allocation over K alternatives followed by empirical-mean selection has high-probability simple regret of order square root of K log(K/delta) over n.
assumptions_latex: \(K\ge2\) and \(n\ge K\).
Noise variables are independent and \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian about their arm means.
The recommendation minimizes the empirical mean using a measurable tie rule.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform-Sampling Fixed-Budget Bound on a Finite Domain

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotonicity of At-Most-Budget Minimax Simple Regret
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural monotonicity induced by nested admissible policy classes as the evaluation budget grows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Pi_{\le n}\) be the class of policies using at most \(n\) charged observations and returning a measurable recommendation, and define
\[R_n^*=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi_{\le n}}\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_f[r(\pi)].\]
Because \(\Pi_{\le n}\subseteq\Pi_{\le n+1}\), one has \(R_{n+1}^*\le R_n^*\). The same conclusion for an exactly-\(n\) protocol requires that a policy may take and ignore an additional observation without changing its recommendation or admissibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal minimax simple-regret risk cannot increase with an at-most evaluation budget; exact-budget monotonicity additionally requires admissible padding by an ignored observation.
assumptions_latex: The objective class and observation model are fixed across budgets.
Policies using fewer than the allowed observations remain admissible under the at-most-budget protocol.

notation.meaning: admissible policies using at most n charged observations
optimal minimax expected simple-regret risk at budget n

knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity of At-Most-Budget Minimax Simple Regret
Fixed-Budget Simple Regret
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Terminal recommendation loss after a prescribed noisy-evaluation budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) have minimizer \(x^*\), and let a policy receive \(n\) noisy observations before returning a measurable recommendation \(\widehat x_n\in X\). Its fixed-budget simple regret is \[r_n=f(\widehat x_n)-f(x^*).\] Its expected simple regret is \(\mathbb E_f[r_n]\), where expectation covers observation noise and policy randomization. For a function class \(\mathcal F\), its worst-case fixed-budget risk is \(R_n=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_f[r_n]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-budget simple regret is the objective gap of the recommendation returned after exactly n noisy evaluations.
assumptions_latex: \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)\).
\(\widehat x_n\) is measurable with respect to the first \(n\) observations and policy randomness.

u)\le C\sqrt{\frac{k}{n}}.\]

children.title: Fixed-Confidence Identification
children.top_down_role: Evaluation complexity for attaining a prescribed terminal confidence or tolerance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantile alternative to expected fixed-confidence evaluation complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-correct policy \(\pi\) with stopping time \(\tau_\pi\), define its worst-case \((1-\eta)\)-quantile complexity by \[N^{\mathrm q}_{\mathcal F}(\pi;\varepsilon,\delta,\eta)=\inf\left\{n\in\mathbb N:\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb P_f(\tau_\pi>n)\le\eta\right\}.\] This differs from \(\sup_f\mathbb E_f[\tau_\pi]\). If the latter is at most \(M<\infty\), Markov's inequality yields \(N^{\mathrm q}_{\mathcal F}(\pi;\varepsilon,\delta,\eta)\le\lceil M/\eta\rceil\). A quantile bound at one fixed \(\eta\) does not by itself bound the expectation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-confidence runtime may be measured by expected stopping time or by a uniform stopping-time quantile; an expectation bound gives a quantile bound, but not conversely at one fixed quantile.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi\) is \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-correct on \(\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_f[\tau_\pi]\le M\Longrightarrow N^{\mathrm q}_{\mathcal F}(\pi;\varepsilon,\delta,\eta)\le\lceil M/\eta\rceil.\)

notation.meaning: Allowed probability of exceeding the declared evaluation count.

knowledge_statements.title: High-Probability Stopping-Time Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic identifiability boundary for uniform epsilon-correctness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_0,f_1\in\mathcal F\) induce the same distribution for the complete adaptive observation transcript and terminal recommendation under a policy, and suppose \(X_\varepsilon^\star(f_0)\cap X_\varepsilon^\star(f_1)=\varnothing\). Then the policy cannot be \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-correct for both functions when \(\delta<1/2\): the common recommendation distribution cannot assign probability at least \(1-\delta\) to each of two disjoint sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If observationally indistinguishable objectives have disjoint epsilon-optimal sets, no policy can identify an epsilon-optimal point for both with confidence greater than one half.
assumptions_latex: The complete adaptive transcript and recommendation have the same law under \(f_0\) and \(f_1\).
\(X_\varepsilon^\star(f_0)\cap X_\varepsilon^\star(f_1)=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Indistinguishability Obstructs Fixed-Confidence Identification

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic-stopping uniform-sampling guarantee for epsilon-optimal identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\{1,\ldots,K\}\), and suppose observations at arm \(i\) are independent with mean \(f(i)\) and \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian noise. For minimization, sample each arm
\[m=\left\lceil\frac{8\sigma^2}{\varepsilon^2}\log\frac{2K}{\delta}\right\rceil\]
times, stop at \(\tau=Km\), and recommend an empirical-mean minimizer \(\widehat i\). Then
\[\inf_fP_f\!\left(f(\widehat i)-\min_jf(j)\le\varepsilon\right)\ge1-\delta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform sampling identifies an epsilon-optimal member of a finite set with confidence one minus delta using order K sigma-squared epsilon-to-minus-two log(K/delta) observations.
assumptions_latex: \(K\ge2\), \(\varepsilon>0\), and \(0<\delta<1\).
Observations are independent and \(\sigma\)-sub-Gaussian about their arm means.
The terminal tie rule is measurable.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain Sub-Gaussian Fixed-Confidence Upper Bound

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Accuracy-Confidence Monotonicity of Optimal Identification Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order relation between fixed-confidence parameters and minimax expected stopping complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(0<\varepsilon_1\le\varepsilon_2\) and \(0<\delta_1\le\delta_2<1\), every policy that is \((\varepsilon_1,\delta_1)\)-correct on \(\mathcal F\) is also \((\varepsilon_2,\delta_2)\)-correct. Hence
\[\Pi_{\varepsilon_1,\delta_1}\subseteq\Pi_{\varepsilon_2,\delta_2}\quad\text{and}\quad N_{\mathcal F}^*(\varepsilon_1,\delta_1)\ge N_{\mathcal F}^*(\varepsilon_2,\delta_2).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Demanding smaller value error or smaller failure probability cannot reduce optimal fixed-confidence evaluation complexity.
assumptions_latex: The objective class, observation laws, admissible policy family, and runtime criterion are fixed.
\(0<\varepsilon_1\le\varepsilon_2\).
\(0<\delta_1\le\delta_2<1\).

notation.meaning: policies correct at tolerance epsilon and failure level delta

knowledge_statements.title: Accuracy-Confidence Monotonicity of Optimal Identification Complexity

assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(\delta\in(0,1)\).
Each \(\pijin\Pi_{\varepsilon,\bdelta}\) uses a stopping time \(\tau_\pi\) and an \(\mathcal F_{\tau_\pi}\)-measurable recommendation \(\widehat x_{\tau_\pi}\).

notation.meaning: stopping time used by policy pi
class of policies correct at tolerance epsilon and confidence 1-delta
optimal worst-case expected fixed-confidence evaluation complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal stopping-time complexity for an accurate terminal recommendation with prescribed confidence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a search space, let \(\mathcal F\) be a class of functions \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), and let \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(\delta\in(0,1)\). A sequential policy \(\pi\) with stopping time \(\tau_\pi\) and terminal recommendation \(\widehat x_{\tau_\pi}\) is \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-correct on \(\mathcal F\) if \[\inf_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb P_f\!\left(f(\widehat x_{\tau_\pi})-inf_{x\in X}f(x)\le\varepsilon\right)\bge1-\bdelta.\] Let \(\Pi_{\varepsilon,\bdelta}\) denote the class of such policies. The policy-specific worst-case expected complexity is \(N_{\mathcal F}(\bpi;\bvarepsilon,\bdelta)=\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_f[\tau_\pi]\), and the optimal fixed-confidence complexity is \[N_{\mathcal F}^*(\varepsilon,\bdelta)=inf_{\pijin\Pi_{\varepsilon,\bdelta}}N_{\mathcal F}(\bpi;\bvarepsilon,\bdelta),\] with \(+\infty\) allowed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A policy is fixed-confidence correct if it returns an ε-optimal point with probability at least 1−δ uniformly over the function class. Optimal fixed-confidence complexity is the infimum, over all such policies, of their worst-case expected stopping times.
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Confidence Identification
