knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimax expected simple-regret lower bound for a fully specified Hölder class under Gaussian observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0<\alpha\leq1\), \(X=[0,1]^d\), and \(\mathcal H^\alpha(L)=\{f:|f(x)-f(y)|\leq L\|x-y\|_2^\alpha\}\). Under adaptive observations \(Y_t=f(x_t)+\xi_t\) with independent \(\xi_t\sim N(0,\sigma^2)\), there is \(c=c(d,\alpha)>0\) such that every policy returning \(\widehat x_n\) satisfies \[\sup_{f\in\mathcal H^\alpha(L)}\mathbb E_f\!\left[f(\widehat x_n)-\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\right]\geq c\min\!\left\{L,\;L^{d/(2\alpha+d)}\left(\frac{\sigma^2}{n}\right)^{\alpha/(2\alpha+d)}\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: No adaptive policy uniformly improves on the noisy Hölder simple-regret order n^{-α/(2α+d)} in the nontrivial regime.
assumptions_latex: The recommendation may be any measurable function of the adaptive Gaussian observation transcript.

notation.meaning: Hölder class with exponent α and seminorm at most L

knowledge_statements.title: Noisy Hölder Simple-Regret Lower Rate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-theoretic lower-bound template for noisy terminal recommendations under adaptive sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f_0,f_1\) induce transcript laws \(P_0,P_1\) for an arbitrary adaptive \(n\)-evaluation policy. Suppose disjoint sets \(G_0,G_1\subseteq\mathcal X\) satisfy \(f_i(x)-\inf_z f_i(z)\geq\Delta\) whenever \(x\notin G_i\). Then every terminal recommendation \(\widehat x_n\) satisfies \[\max_{i\in\{0,1\}}\mathbb E_i[r_n]\geq \frac{\Delta}{4}\exp\{-\mathrm{KL}(P_0\|P_1)\}.\] For conditionally independent observations, \[\mathrm{KL}(P_0\|P_1)=\sum_{t=1}^n\mathbb E_0\!\left[\mathrm{KL}\bigl(Q_{0,x_t}\|Q_{1,x_t}\bigr)\right].\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two objectives with separated optimal regions but statistically similar adaptive transcripts force nonzero worst-case expected simple regret.
assumptions_latex: \(G_0\cap G_1=\varnothing\).
Leaving \(G_i\) incurs simple regret at least \(\Delta>0\) under instance \(i\).

notation.meaning: Law of the complete adaptive transcript under objective i
Observation law at location x under objective i
Low-regret recommendation region for objective i

Noisy Simple-Regret Lower Bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimax lower-rate template for Gaussian-noise optimization over Hölder classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[0,1]^d\), observe \(Y_t=f(x_t)+\xi_t\) with adaptive \(x_t\) and independent \(\xi_t\sim N(0,\sigma^2)\), and let \(\mathcal H^\alpha(L)\) be an \(\alpha\)-Hölder class rich enough to contain localized bumps. There exists \(c>0\), depending only on \(d,\alpha,L\), such that every policy returning \(\widehat x_n\) after \(n\) observations satisfies \[\sup_{f\in\mathcal H^\alpha(L)}\mathbb E_f\!\left[f(\widehat x_n)-\min_{x\in X}f(x)\right]\ge c\left(\frac{\sigma^2}{n}\right)^{\alpha/(2\alpha+d)}\] in the nontrivial small-regret regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Gaussian noise, no adaptive policy uniformly beats the Hölder minimax simple-regret order n^{-α/(2α+d)}.
assumptions_latex: \(X=[0,1]^d\) and \(f\in\mathcal H^\alpha(L)\).
\(Y_t=f(x_t)+\xi_t\) with independent \(\xi_t\sim N(0,\sigma^2)\).
\(x_t\) may depend on observations before time \(t\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity_bound kind is correct for this leaf, but the exact minimax exponent and scaling cannot be accepted from a class described only as 'rich enough to contain localized bumps.' Boundary conditions, the precise Hölder ball, parameter regime, and dependence of the constant require an authoritative lower-bound source.

children.title: Minimax Efficiency
children.top_down_role: Exact rate matching between policy performance and lower bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Upper-and-lower-bound sandwich certifying constant-factor minimax efficiency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_n^*=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi}\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_f[r_n(\pi)]\). If, for every \(n\geq n_0\), \[R_n^*\geq c a_n\quad\text{and}\quad \sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_f[r_n(\widehat\pi)]\leq C a_n\] for constants \(0<c\leq C<\infty\), then \[\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_f[r_n(\widehat\pi)]\leq (C/c)R_n^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching a minimax lower bound and a policy upper bound at the same benchmark rate certifies constant-factor minimax efficiency.
assumptions_latex: The bounds use the same function class, admissible policy class, loss, noise model, budget convention, and guarantee mode.
\(a_n>0\) for \(n\geq n_0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Matching-Rate Minimax Certificate
Minimax Efficiency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact constant-factor matching of a policy risk to minimax risk.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a function class \(\mathcal F\), loss \(r_n\), and policies \(\Pi\), define the minimax risk \[R_n^*=\inf_{\pi\in\Pi}\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_f[r_n(\pi)].\] A policy \(\widehat\pi\) is minimax efficient over \(\mathcal F\) if there exist constants \(C<\infty\) and \(n_0\) such that, for every \(n\ge n_0\), \[\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_f[r_n(\widehat\pi)]\le C R_n^*.\] Thus its worst-case risk matches the optimal achievable rate without an asymptotically growing multiplicative loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A policy is minimax efficient when its worst-case risk stays within a constant factor of the minimax risk.
assumptions_latex: \(0<R_n^*<\infty\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the rate-optimality leaf and the constant-factor comparison is internally coherent with the stated role. An inspectable source is still needed because 'minimax efficient' can denote stronger asymptotic-constant efficiency in some literature.

children.title: Near-Minimax Efficiency
children.top_down_role: Rate comparison allowing secondary or logarithmic losses.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate for rate matching up to an explicitly declared secondary factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(R_n^*\geq c a_n>0\) and \(\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_f[r_n(\widehat\pi)]\leq Cg(n)a_n\), where \(g(n)\geq1\). Then \[\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_f[r_n(\widehat\pi)]\leq \frac{C}{c}g(n)R_n^*.\] The factor \(g\) and the common statistical regime must be declared in any near-minimax claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A lower bound and policy upper bound certify near-minimaxity when their mismatch is no larger than the stated secondary factor.
assumptions_latex: Both bounds concern the same class, loss, policy restrictions, noise model, budget convention, and guarantee mode.
\(g(n)\geq1\) is specified independently of the unknown objective.
knowledge_statements.title: Near-Minimax Rate Sandwich
Near-Minimax Efficiency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimax rate matching up to a specified slowly varying factor.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_n^*\) be the minimax risk over \(\mathcal F\). Given a factor \(g(n)\ge1\), a policy \(\widehat\pi\) is \(g\)-near-minimax efficient if there exist \(C<\infty\) and \(n_0\) such that \[\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\mathbb E_f[r_n(\widehat\pi)]\le Cg(n)R_n^*\qquad(n\ge n_0).\] The usual polylogarithmic notion takes \(g(n)=(\log n)^q\) for some fixed \(q\ge0\); near-minimaxity must state the permitted factor explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near-minimax efficiency allows a declared secondary factor, commonly polylogarithmic, above the minimax risk.
assumptions_latex: \(0<R_n^*<\infty\) for all sufficiently large \(n\).
\(g(n)\ge1\) is specified independently of \(f\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits and the permitted factor is explicitly parameterized, avoiding an overclaim that all near-minimax results allow the same loss. The convention nevertheless has no cited source or locator.

children.title: Design-Coverage Consistency
children.top_down_role: Global convergence obtained through persistent coverage of the search domain.

children.title: Dense-Sampling Consistency
children.top_down_role: Global-consistency route based on density of evaluation locations.

assumptions_latex: The sample range is a dense subset of \((0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{1\le i\le n}f(x_i)=1\) for every \(n\), although \(\min_{x\in X}f(x)=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp objective-regularity boundary for dense-sampling consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[0,1]\), let \((x_n)\) enumerate a subset of \((0,1]\) dense in \(X\), and define \(f(0)=0\) and \(f(x)=1\) for \(x>0\). Then the sample range is dense, but the best sampled value is always \(1\) while the global minimum is \(0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense design can miss an isolated downward discontinuity forever, so objective regularity is essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Density Alone Fails for Discontinuous Objectives
knowledge_statements.title: Density Alone Fails for Discontinuous Objectives

assumptions_latex: \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is continuous.
\(f^\star=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)>-\infty\).
\(\{x_n:n\ge1\}\) is dense in \(X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-only dense-sampling consistency without compactness or attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a topological space, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be continuous with \(f^\star=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)>-\infty\), and let the range of \((x_n)\) be dense in \(X\). Then \(\min_{1\le i\le n}f(x_i)\downarrow f^\star\). Compactness and attainment are unnecessary for value convergence but are needed for the seed's accumulation-point conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuity and a dense sampling range suffice for convergence of best sampled values to a finite infimum without compactness; compactness is needed for optimizer accumulation statements.
knowledge_statements.title: Dense-Sampling Value Consistency Without Compactness

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a compact metric space.
\(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is continuous.
\(\{x_n:n\ge1\}\) is dense in \(X\).
\(\widehat x_n\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\le i\le n}f(x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\widehat x_n)\to\min_{x\in X}f(x)\), and every accumulation point of \((\widehat x_n)\) is a global minimizer.

notation.meaning: best point among the first n exact evaluations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic global consistency obtained from density of exact evaluation locations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a compact metric space, let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be continuous, and let \((x_n)_{n\ge1}\) be a sequence whose range is dense in \(X\). For each \(n\ge1\), choose \(\widehat x_n\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\le i\le n}f(x_i)\). Then \[f(\widehat x_n)\longrightarrow\min_{x\in X}f(x).\] Every accumulation point of \((\widehat x_n)\) belongs to \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuous objective on a compact metric space, dense exact sampling makes the best sampled value converge to the global minimum, and every accumulation point of the best sampled points is a global minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Dense-Sampling Consistency

children.title: Fill-Distance Consistency
children.top_down_role: Geometric consistency expressed through shrinking uncovered regions.

assumptions_latex: The fill-distance setting of the immutable seed holds.
\(|f(x)-f(y)|\le L\rho(x,y)^\alpha\) for some \(L>0\) and \(0<\alpha\le1\).
For the displayed sample-size rate, \(h_n\le Cn^{-1/d}\).

notation.meaning: Exponent governing the assumed fill-distance decay.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularity-based rate specialization of the seed's modulus bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the seed's assumptions, if \(|f(x)-f(y)|\le L\rho(x,y)^\alpha\), then \(0\le f(\widehat x_n)-f^\star\le Lh_n^\alpha\). In particular, if \(h_n\le Cn^{-1/d}\), then the simple regret is at most \(LC^\alpha n^{-\alpha/d}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hölder regularity converts fill distance directly into a simple-regret rate.
knowledge_statements.title: Hölder Fill-Distance Regret Bound

assumptions_latex: \((X,\rho)\) is a compact metric space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h_n\to0\) if and only if \(\{x_n:n\ge1\}\) is dense in \(X\).

notation.meaning: Distance from x to the finite design.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric equivalence for nested finite designs on compact metric spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,\rho)\) be compact, let \(D_n=\{x_1,\ldots,x_n\}\), and let \(h_n=\sup_{x\in X}\rho(x,D_n)\). Then \(h_n\to0\) if and only if \(\overline{\bigcup_{n\ge1}D_n}=X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For nested finite designs on a compact metric space, vanishing fill distance is equivalent to density of the infinite design.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Vanishing Fill Distance Characterizes Dense Nested Designs
knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Fill Distance Characterizes Dense Nested Designs

assumptions_latex: \((X,\brho)\) is a compact metric space.
\(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is continuous.
\(\widehat x_n\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\le i\le n}f(x_i)\).

notation.meaning: fill distance of the first n evaluation locations
modulus of continuity of f with respect to rho
best point among the first n exact evaluations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric global consistency from vanishing fill distance on a compact metric space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,\brho)\) be a compact metric space, let \(x_1,x_2,\bldots\in X\), and define \(h_n=\sup_{x\in X}\min_{1\le i\le n}\rho(x,x_i)\). Let \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) be continuous, define \(\omega_f(t)=\sup\{|f(x)-f(y)|:x,y\in X,\b \rho(x,y)\le t\}\), and choose \(\widehat x_n\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\le i\le n}f(x_i)\). If \(h_n\to0\), then \[0\le f(\widehat x_n)-min_{x\in X}f(x)\le\omega_f(h_n)\longrightarrow0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing fill distance guarantees best-sample consistency for a continuous objective on a compact metric space, with simple regret bounded by the objective's modulus of continuity.
knowledge_statements.title: Fill-Distance Consistency

children.title: Persistent-Exploration Mechanisms
children.top_down_role: Policy-level mechanisms that prevent permanent exclusion of relevant regions.

assumptions_latex: For each \(k\), \(G_k\) is a finite \(\delta_k\)-net of \(X\).
\(\delta_k\to0\).
Every point of every \(G_k\) is evaluated after a finite time.

notation.meaning: Finite exploration net at resolution delta_k.
Covering radius of the kth net.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric mechanism directly enforcing vanishing fill distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\delta_k\downarrow0\), and for each \(k\) let \(G_k\subset X\) be a finite \(\delta_k\)-net. A policy that eventually evaluates every point of every \(G_k\), while inserting arbitrary exploitation evaluations between them, has fill distance \(h_n\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluating successively finer finite nets forces fill distance to zero even when arbitrary exploitation steps are interleaved.
knowledge_statements.title: Shrinking-Net Exploration

assumptions_latex: \((z_k)\) is dense in \(X\).
The exploration times \((n_k)\) form an infinite strictly increasing sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\overline{\{x_n:n\ge1\}}=X\); recurrent visitation by \((z_k)\) additionally gives persistent exploration.

notation.meaning: Time of the kth forced exploratory evaluation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Policy-independent deterministic mechanism guaranteeing coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((z_k)_{k\ge1}\) be dense in \(X\), and let \(1\le n_1<n_2<\cdots\). Define a policy with \(x_{n_k}=z_k\) and any admissible exploitation rule at other times. Then the evaluation range is dense in \(X\). If every nonempty open set contains \(z_k\) for infinitely many indices \(k\), the policy persistently explores \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interleaving any exploitation policy with a prescribed dense subsequence guarantees density; a recurrent exploration schedule guarantees persistent exploration.
knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Dense-Subsequence Exploration

assumptions_latex: \((E_n)\) are independent Bernoulli variables with probabilities \(\varepsilon_n\).
\(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\varepsilon_n<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(E_n=1\text{ infinitely often})=0\); density and persistent exploration are therefore not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp probability boundary for the seed's randomized mixture mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the independent mixture mechanism of the seed, if \(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\varepsilon_n<\infty\), then only finitely many indicators satisfy \(E_n=1\) almost surely. Consequently, full support of \(\mu\) alone cannot guarantee density or persistent exploration; the exploitation rule may permanently exclude an open set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full-support exploratory draws do not guarantee asymptotic coverage when exploration probabilities are summable, because only finitely many exploration steps occur almost surely.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Summable Exploration Does Not Guarantee Coverage
knowledge_statements.title: Summable Exploration Does Not Guarantee Coverage

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a second-countable compact metric space.
\(E_n\) are independent Bernoulli variables with \(\mathbb P(E_n=1)=\varepsilon_n\).
Conditional on \(E_n=1\), the exploratory draws are independent with common law \(\mu\), and \(\mu(U)>0\) for every nonempty open \(U\subset X\).
\(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\varepsilon_n=\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With probability one, every nonempty open \(U\subset X\) contains infinitely many evaluation locations; hence \(\{x_n:n\ge1\}\) is dense in \(X\).

notation.meaning: indicator that time n uses the exploration mechanism
nonempty open subset of the search space

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent randomized exploration condition ensuring that every open region is revisited indefinitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a second-countable compact metric space and let \(\mu\) be a probability measure satisfying \(\mu(U)>0\) for every nonempty open \(U\subset X\). For each \(n\ge1\), let \(E_n\) be an independent Bernoulli variable with \(\mathbb P(E_n=1)=\varepsilon_n\). Conditional on \(E_n=1\), let the policy set \(x_n=Z_n\), where the exploratory draws \((Z_n)_{n\ge1}\) are independent with common law \(\mu\) and are independent of \((E_n)_{n\ge1}\). If \[\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\varepsilon_n=infty,\] then, with probability one, every nonempty open set \(U\subset X\) contains \(x_n\) for infinitely many \(n\). Consequently, \(\{x_n:n\ge1\}\) is almost surely dense in \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent full-support exploration with nonsummable exploration probabilities samples every open region infinitely often almost surely and therefore produces a dense design.
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent-Exploration Mechanisms

children.top_down_role: Global-convergence family for classical and adaptively fitted efficient global optimization.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Convergence Properties of the Expected Improvement Algorithm with Fixed Mean and Covariance Functions

children.title: Fixed-Prior Expected-Improvement Consistency
children.top_down_role: Classical convergence theory with fixed covariance and mean structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A design-level implication, not a theorem that fixed-prior EI necessarily generates a dense design.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(X\) is compact, \(f\in C(X)\), and \(\{x_n:n\ge1\}\) is dense in \(X\), then \[\min_{1\le i\le n}f(x_i)\longrightarrow\min_{x\in X}f(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dense evaluation sequence is sufficient for convergence of the best sampled value for every continuous objective on a compact domain.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact.
\(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is continuous.
The sampled locations are dense in \(X\).
knowledge_statements.title: Dense-Design Sufficiency for Best-Sampled-Value Consistency

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A finite-domain example showing that fixing a prior does not alone guarantee EI consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{a,b\}\), with true objective \(f(a)=0\) and \(f(b)=-1\). Suppose a noise-free fixed Gaussian specification assigns the deterministic values \(f(a)=0\) and \(f(b)=1\). After observing \(a\), minimization EI is zero at both points. An admissible tie rule that always selects \(a\) gives \[f_n^{\min}=0\quad\text{for every }n,\qquad f^\star=-1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degenerate misspecified fixed prior can assign zero improvement to the true optimum, allowing an EI tie rule to sample an inferior point forever.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\{a,b\}\) and observations are noise-free.
The fixed prior has zero marginal variance and means zero at \(a\) and one at \(b\).
The tie rule selects \(a\) whenever both EI values are zero.
knowledge_statements.title: Degenerate Fixed-Prior Exploration Failure

assumptions_latex: \(M_n=\sup_{x\in X}\operatorname{EI}_n(x)>0\) on the stages where the ratio is used.
The selected point satisfies additive acquisition error \(\eta_n\ge0\).
The underlying fixed-prior consistency theorem remains valid under asymptotically exact relative EI maximization.

notation.meaning: Maximum expected improvement at stage n.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acquisition-optimization condition for EI theorems permitting asymptotically exact relative maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_n=\sup_{x\in X}\operatorname{EI}_n(x)\). If \(\operatorname{EI}_n(x_{n+1})\ge M_n-\eta_n\) and \(\eta_n/M_n\to0\) along every subsequence on which \(M_n>0\), then \(\operatorname{EI}_n(x_{n+1})/M_n\to1\). Thus a fixed-prior EI theorem that explicitly permits asymptotically exact relative maximization also permits this additive-error schedule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate EI optimization is asymptotically relatively exact when its additive error is negligible compared with the current maximum EI.
knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Relative EI-Maximization Error

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite.
Observations are noise-free.
The fixed Gaussian prior covariance matrix on \(X\) is positive definite.
Minimization EI is maximized exactly relative to the best observed value.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-domain convergence result for fixed-prior noiseless expected improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be finite and observations be exact. Suppose the fixed Gaussian prior covariance matrix on \(X\) is positive definite. Conditional on any proper subset of locations having been observed, every unobserved location has positive conditional variance and hence strictly positive minimization EI, whereas every observed location has zero EI. Exact EI maximization therefore selects a previously unobserved point until all of \(X\) has been evaluated, and \(f_n^{\min}=f^\star\) after at most \(|X|\) distinct evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nondegenerate fixed Gaussian prior makes exact noiseless EI exhaust a finite domain and attain the optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain Nondegenerate Fixed-Prior EI Theorem
Fixed-Prior Expected-Improvement Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines latent-value consistency of expected improvement when the GP prior specification and noise parameters are not refitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A fixed-prior expected-improvement policy is consistent for \(f\) if \[\mathbb{P}\!\left(\lim_{n\to\infty} f_n^{\min}=f^\star\right)=1.\] The prior mean function, covariance family and hyperparameters, and noise parameters used by expected improvement are fixed across stages, while the posterior is updated by conditioning on accumulated observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-prior expected improvement is consistent when the best sampled latent objective value converges almost surely to the global minimum while the prior and noise parameters are not refitted.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a compact metric space and \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous.
Observations satisfy \(Y_n=f(x_n)+\varepsilon_n\) under a specified noise model.
The policy selects \(x_{n+1}\) by maximizing posterior expected improvement computed from a fixed prior specification.

notation.meaning: Global minimum of the latent objective.
Best sampled latent objective value through stage n.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: almost-sure convergence of best sampled latent value defines value consistency

children.title: Estimated-Prior Expected-Improvement Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency and failure boundaries when covariance parameters are fitted sequentially.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates fitted-parameter convergence from the acquisition stability required to transfer a fixed-prior EI theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The implication \[\widehat\theta_n\to\theta_\infty\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \sup_{x\in X}|\operatorname{EI}_n(x;\widehat\theta_n)-\operatorname{EI}_n(x;\theta_\infty)|\to0\] need not hold without uniform-in-stage continuity and covariance nondegeneracy along the data-dependent posterior sequence. Consequently, parameter convergence alone does not establish estimated-prior EI consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convergent fitted parameters need not make the fitted EI acquisitions uniformly approach a fixed-prior acquisition, so parameter convergence alone is not a consistency certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat\theta_n\to\theta_\infty\) in a declared parameter topology.
No uniform-in-stage acquisition-continuity or covariance-nondegeneracy condition is imposed.

notation.meaning: Limit of the fitted parameter sequence.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Convergence Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: An abstract sufficient transfer result; it does not show that a particular hyperparameter estimator satisfies the uniform approximation assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_n(\cdot;\widehat\theta_n)\) be fitted EI and \(a_n^\circ\) a fixed-prior oracle acquisition. If \[\delta_n:=\sup_{x\in X}|a_n(x;\widehat\theta_n)-a_n^\circ(x)|\to0\] almost surely and \[a_n(x_{n+1};\widehat\theta_n)\ge\sup_{x\in X}a_n(x;\widehat\theta_n)-\eta_n,\qquad\eta_n\to0,\] then \[a_n^\circ(x_{n+1})\ge\sup_{x\in X}a_n^\circ(x)-\eta_n-2\delta_n.\] Hence consistency transfers whenever the oracle theorem covers maximizers with vanishing acquisition error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform approximation to a consistent fixed-prior EI acquisition transfers consistency when acquisition-optimization error also vanishes.
assumptions_latex: The fitted and oracle acquisitions are finite on the common domain \(X\).
\(\delta_n\to0\) and \(\eta_n\to0\) almost surely.
The fixed-prior oracle consistency theorem permits vanishing acquisition-maximization error.

notation.meaning: Fixed-prior oracle acquisition at stage n.

knowledge_statements.title: Plug-In Acquisition Stability Transfer

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is a compact metric space with a countable dense sequence \((z_j)_{j\ge1}\).
\(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is continuous.
Every scheduled exploration stage is executed.
Performance is measured by best sampled latent value.

notation.meaning: Infinite deterministic set of forced-exploration stages.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency-preserving plug-in EI variant whose guarantee does not require the fitted parameters to remain exploratory.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a compact metric space, \(f\in C(X)\), and \((z_j)_{j\ge1}\) a dense sequence in \(X\). Choose infinite stages \(E=\{e_1<e_2<\cdots\}\). At stage \(e_j\), query \(z_j\); at every other stage, maximize \(\operatorname{EI}_n(\cdot;\widehat\theta_n)\). Then the evaluation sequence contains a dense subsequence, irrespective of the fitted parameters, and \(f_n^{\min}\to f^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interleaving fitted EI with a dense exploration schedule guarantees best-sampled-value consistency even when hyperparameter fitting becomes degenerate.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Forced-Exploration Safeguard for Fitted Expected Improvement
knowledge_statements.title: Forced-Exploration Safeguard for Fitted Expected Improvement

assumptions_latex: \(X=\{a,b\}\), observations are exact, and \(f(a)=0\), \(f(b)=-1\).
The fitting rule permits a zero-covariance boundary estimate and fitted means \(m(a)=0\), \(m(b)=1\).
Acquisition ties select the previously evaluated point \(a\).
No independent exploration safeguard is imposed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete two-point failure caused by fitted covariance collapse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{a,b\}\), observations be exact, and \(f(a)=0\), \(f(b)=-1\). After observing \(a\), suppose the sequential fitting rule selects a plug-in model with zero covariance and fitted means \(m(a)=0\), \(m(b)=1\). EI is then zero at both points. A tie rule selecting \(a\) forever yields \(f_n^{\min}=0\) for all \(n\), although \(f^\star=-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fitted covariance that collapses to zero can erase every EI incentive to evaluate the true optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Plug-In Variance Collapse Can Suppress the Optimum
knowledge_statements.title: Plug-In Variance Collapse Can Suppress the Optimum

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite and observations are exact.
At every stage the fitted model is a proper data-measurable Gaussian predictive model with finite predictive means.
Every unevaluated point has strictly positive fitted conditional variance.
EI is computed against the best observed latent value and maximized exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_n^{\min}=f^\star\text{ after at most }|X|\text{ distinct evaluations}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain consistency for sequential fitting rules whose predictive covariance does not degenerate at unevaluated points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be finite and observations exact. At every stage fit a data-measurable Gaussian predictive model with finite means such that, conditional on the observations, every unevaluated point has strictly positive predictive variance. Define EI relative to the best observed value and maximize it exactly. Evaluated points have zero EI, whereas every unevaluated point has strictly positive EI; therefore the plug-in policy samples a new point at every stage until \(X\) is exhausted and attains \(f^\star\) after at most \(|X|\) distinct evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite noiseless domain, sequential refitting preserves EI consistency whenever it cannot collapse predictive variance at unevaluated points.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Domain Uniformly Nondegenerate Plug-In EI Consistency
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain Uniformly Nondegenerate Plug-In EI Consistency

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Corrected finite-domain result requiring every sequentially fitted predictive model to interpolate exact observations and remain nondegenerate elsewhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be finite and observations exact. At every stage let the fitted Gaussian predictive model have finite means, interpolate every evaluated value with zero latent predictive variance there, and assign strictly positive conditional variance to every unevaluated point. If EI is computed relative to the best observed value and maximized exactly, then evaluated points have zero EI and every unevaluated point has strictly positive EI. Consequently the policy evaluates a new point at each stage until \(X\) is exhausted and attains \(f^\star\) after at most \(|X|\) distinct evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite-domain plug-in EI exhausts the domain when every fitted model interpolates exact observations and retains positive variance at every unevaluated point.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite and observations are exact.
Each fitted predictive model has finite means and is measurable with respect to the accumulated data.
At evaluated points, the fitted latent posterior mean equals the observed value and its latent variance is zero.
Every unevaluated point has strictly positive fitted conditional variance.
EI uses the best observed value and is maximized exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_n^{\min}=f^\star\text{ after at most }|X|\text{ distinct evaluations}.
review_flags: corrects_prior_version: predictive nondegeneracy alone did not ensure zero EI at evaluated points
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain Interpolating Plug-In EI Consistency
Estimated-Prior Expected-Improvement Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines latent-value consistency of plug-in expected improvement; it does not claim that unrestricted hyperparameter fitting guarantees consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An estimated-prior expected-improvement policy is consistent for \(f\) if its decisions \[x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in X}\operatorname{EI}_n(x;\widehat\theta_n)\] satisfy \[\mathbb{P}\!\left(\lim_{n\to\infty}f_n^{\min}=f^\star\right)=1.\] Here \(\widehat\theta_n\) may depend on the data accumulated through stage \(n\); convergence of \(\widehat\theta_n\) alone is not the stated consistency property.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Estimated-prior expected improvement is consistent when sequentially refitting its model parameters still yields almost-sure convergence of the best sampled latent value to the optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact and \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous.
At stage \(n\), the fitted parameter \(\widehat\theta_n\) is measurable with respect to the accumulated information.
The expected-improvement acquisition \(\operatorname{EI}_n(\cdot;\widehat\theta_n)\) is well defined.

notation.meaning: Sequentially fitted model and noise parameters.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the definition distinguishes data-dependent fitting from a fixed prior

children.title: Posterior Learning Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency of latent-function and optimizer learning under adaptive sequential designs.

children.title: Posterior Prediction Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency of latent prediction in optimization-relevant regions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Prediction Does Not Imply Uniform Prediction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates pointwise posterior-mean consistency from the uniform criterion owned by this leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(D=[0,1]\), let \(f\equiv0\), and let \(m_n\) be a continuous triangular spike of height one supported on \((0,2/n)\) with peak at \(1/n\). Then \(m_n(x)\to0\) for every fixed \(x\in D\), but \[\sup_{x\in D}|m_n(x)-f(x)|=1\quad\text{for every }n.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Moving prediction-error spikes can give pointwise consistency everywhere without uniform consistency.
assumptions_latex: \(m_n\) is the stated continuous moving triangular spike.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Prediction Does Not Imply Uniform Prediction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uncertainty Contraction Does Not Ensure Prediction Accuracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates posterior concentration from correctness under misspecification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a fitted posterior is degenerate at a deterministic function \(g\ne f\), then for every \(n\) and \(x\), \[s_n(x)=0,\qquad m_n(x)=g(x).\] Hence \(\sup_{x\in D}s_n(x)=0\) while \[\sup_{x\in D}|m_n(x)-f(x)|=\|g-f\|_{\infty,D}>0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A misspecified posterior can be completely certain while predicting the latent objective incorrectly.
assumptions_latex: The fitted posterior is a point mass at \(g\).
\(g\ne f\) on the prediction region \(D\).

notation.meaning: Incorrect deterministic function selected by the fitted posterior.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncertainty Contraction Does Not Ensure Prediction Accuracy
Posterior Prediction Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines uniform consistency of the latent posterior mean on a designated optimization-relevant region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a declared convergence mode \(\mathsf M\), posterior prediction is uniformly consistent on \(D\) if \[\sup_{x\in D}|m_n(x)-f(x)|\longrightarrow0\quad\text{in mode }\mathsf M.\] The prediction target is the latent response \(f\), not a future noisy observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Posterior prediction is uniformly consistent when the latent posterior mean converges uniformly to the true objective on the relevant region in the declared mode.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq X\) is the designated prediction region.
\(m_n(x)=\mathbb{E}[f(x)\mid\mathcal F_n]\) is the latent posterior mean.
\(\mathsf M\) is a specified mode such as almost-sure convergence or convergence in probability.

notation.meaning: Latent posterior mean after n observations.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: uniform posterior-mean convergence is a standard prediction-consistency predicate

children.title: Posterior-Uncertainty Contraction
children.top_down_role: Reduction of epistemic uncertainty along the sequential design.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates contraction by conditioning under one model from changes caused by replacing the covariance model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The ordering \(s_{n+1}^2(x)\le s_n^2(x)\) follows from Gaussian conditioning within a fixed joint model. If stage \(n+1\) replaces covariance or noise parameters by \(\widehat\theta_{n+1}\), then \(s_{n+1}^2(x;\widehat\theta_{n+1})\) and \(s_n^2(x;\widehat\theta_n)\) are computed under different fitted laws, and neither ordering is guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Posterior variance is monotone under fixed-model Gaussian conditioning, but sequential hyperparameter refitting can make reported uncertainty increase.
assumptions_latex: The fitted parameter may change from \(\widehat\theta_n\) to \(\widehat\theta_{n+1}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Refitting Can Break Variance Monotonicity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: An isolated scalar Gaussian-update formula for repeated independent observations at one location.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f(x)\) has prior variance \(s_0^2(x)>0\) and the only data are \(r\) conditionally independent observations at \(x\), each with noise variance \(\tau^2(x)>0\), then \[s_r^2(x)=\left(s_0^{-2}(x)+r\tau^{-2}(x)\right)^{-1}\to0.\] The predictive variance of a new observation satisfies \[s_r^2(x)+\tau^2(x)\to\tau^2(x),\] not zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent replication drives latent uncertainty at the replicated site to zero at order one over the replicate count, while future-observation noise remains.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)\) has a scalar Gaussian prior with variance \(s_0^2(x)>0\).
The data consist of \(r\) conditionally independent Gaussian replicates at \(x\) with common variance \(\tau^2(x)>0\).

notation.meaning: Number of independent replicates at x.

knowledge_statements.title: Replicated-Site Latent Variance Contraction

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotonicity of Fixed-Model Gaussian Posterior Variance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Applies when the covariance and observation model remain fixed; sequential refitting can destroy the ordering.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed Gaussian model, after adding a scalar observation at \(z\) with conditionally independent noise variance \(\tau^2(z)\), \[s_{n+1}^2(x)=s_n^2(x)-\frac{c_n(x,z)^2}{s_n^2(z)+\tau^2(z)}\le s_n^2(x),\] whenever the denominator is positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a fixed Gaussian model, conditioning on one additional observation cannot increase latent posterior variance.
assumptions_latex: Conditional on \(\mathcal F_n\), the latent field and new observation are jointly Gaussian.
The covariance and noise model are not refitted between stages.

notation.meaning: Variance of the new independent observation noise.

knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity of Fixed-Model Gaussian Posterior Variance
Posterior-Uncertainty Contraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines uniform contraction of epistemic uncertainty about the latent objective; irreducible observation noise is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a declared convergence mode \(\mathsf M\), posterior uncertainty contracts uniformly on \(D\) if \[\sup_{x\in D}s_n(x)\longrightarrow0\quad\text{in mode }\mathsf M,\] where \(s_n^2(x)=\operatorname{Var}(f(x)\mid\mathcal F_n)\). This condition concerns latent epistemic uncertainty, not the predictive variance of a new noisy observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Posterior uncertainty contracts uniformly when the largest latent posterior standard deviation on the relevant region tends to zero in the declared mode.
assumptions_latex: \(D\subseteq X\) is the designated contraction region.
\(s_n^2(x)=\operatorname{Var}(f(x)\mid\mathcal F_n)\) exists for \(x\in D\).
\(\mathsf M\) is a specified mode of convergence.

notation.meaning: Region on which contraction is required.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: vanishing latent posterior standard deviation is the standard contraction predicate

children.title: Optimizer-Value Consistency Pair
children.top_down_role: Consistency of posterior conclusions about the optimum and optimizer set.

children.title: Optimizer-Set Consistency
children.top_down_role: Posterior conclusions concerning the location or set of global optimizers.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decomposes Hausdorff consistency into outer exclusion and inner recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty compact \(\widehat S_n,S^\star\), \[d_H(\widehat S_n,S^\star)\to0\] is equivalent to \[\sup_{x\in\widehat S_n}\operatorname{dist}(x,S^\star)\to0\quad\text{and}\quad\sup_{x\in S^\star}\operatorname{dist}(x,\widehat S_n)\to0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hausdorff optimizer-set consistency requires both exclusion of false minimizers and approximation of every true minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat S_n\) and \(S^\star\) are nonempty compact subsets of a metric space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: d_H(\widehat S_n,S^\star)\to0\iff\text{both directed distances tend to zero}.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Set-Recovery Condition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that uniform objective convergence supplies only outer argmin consistency without an additional inner-recovery condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[-1,1]\), \(f(x)=0\), and \(m_n(x)=x/n\). Then \(\|m_n-f\|_\infty=1/n\to0\), but \(S^\star=X\) and \(\widehat S_n=\{-1\}\). Therefore \[\sup_{x\in\widehat S_n}\operatorname{dist}(x,S^\star)=0,\qquad d_H(\widehat S_n,S^\star)=2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A vanishing perturbation can select only one member of a continuum of true minimizers, so uniform prediction does not guarantee two-sided Hausdorff recovery.
assumptions_latex: \(f\equiv0\) and \(m_n(x)=x/n\).
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Sided Hausdorff Recovery Failure

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Argmin Outer Consistency under Uniform Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ensures that estimated minimizers approach the true optimizer set; it does not ensure recovery of every true minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be compact, let \(f,m_n\in C(X)\), and suppose \(\|m_n-f\|_\infty\to0\). If \(\widehat S_n=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_Xm_n\) and \(S^\star=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_Xf\), then \[\sup_{x\in\widehat S_n}\operatorname{dist}(x,S^\star)\to0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform convergence of continuous objectives on a compact domain forces every estimated minimizer toward the true optimizer set.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact.
\(f,m_n\in C(X)\).
\(\|m_n-f\|_\infty\to0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Argmin Outer Consistency under Uniform Convergence
Optimizer-Set Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses two-sided Hausdorff convergence for nonempty compact estimated and true optimizer sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Optimizer-set consistency in a declared convergence mode \(\mathsf M\) holds when \[d_H(\widehat S_n,S^\star)\longrightarrow0\quad\text{in mode }\mathsf M,\] where \[d_H(A,B)=\max\!\left\{\sup_{a\in A}\inf_{b\in B}d(a,b),\ \sup_{b\in B}\inf_{a\in A}d(a,b)\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimizer-set consistency means that the estimated optimizer sets converge to the true optimizer set in Hausdorff distance in the declared mode.
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is a metric space.
\(S^\star=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in X}f(x)\) is nonempty and compact.
Each \(\widehat S_n\subseteq X\) is nonempty and compact.
\(\mathsf M\) is a specified mode of convergence.

notation.meaning: Estimated optimizer set at stage n.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Hausdorff convergence is a standard two-sided compact-set consistency notion

children.title: Optimal-Value Consistency
children.top_down_role: Posterior conclusions concerning the global optimum value.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Value Consistency Does Not Identify Optimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates scalar optimal-value estimation from optimizer localization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=[0,1]\), \(f(x)=x\), and \(\widehat v_n=0\) for every \(n\). Then \(\widehat v_n=f^\star\), while the unrelated optimizer estimate \(\widehat x_n=1\) satisfies \[f(\widehat x_n)-f^\star=1,\qquad\operatorname{dist}(\widehat x_n,S^\star)=1\] for every \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even an exact optimum-value estimate gives no optimizer-location guarantee unless the value and optimizer estimators are structurally linked.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat v_n=0\) and \(\widehat x_n=1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Value Consistency Does Not Identify Optimizers

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfers uniform latent-prediction consistency to consistency of the induced minimum value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For real functions \(g,f\) on a nonempty set \(X\) with finite infima and finite \(\|g-f\|_\infty\), \[\left|\inf_{x\in X}g(x)-\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\right|\le\sup_{x\in X}|g(x)-f(x)|.\] Hence, if \(\widehat v_n=\inf_Xm_n\) and \(\|m_n-f\|_\infty\to0\) in mode \(\mathsf M\), then \(\widehat v_n\to f^\star\) in the same mode.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniformly accurate latent predictions yield an equally accurate plug-in estimate of the optimum value.
assumptions_latex: \(X\ne\varnothing\).
\(f\) and \(m_n\) have finite infima.
\(\|m_n-f\|_\infty\to0\) in mode \(\mathsf M\).

notation.meaning: Plug-in estimate of the optimal value.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimal-Value Stability under Uniform Prediction
Optimal-Value Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines convergence of an estimated latent optimal value separately from optimizer-set or point convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a declared convergence mode \(\mathsf M\), an estimator \(\widehat v_n\) is optimal-value consistent if \[\widehat v_n\longrightarrow f^\star\quad\text{in mode }\mathsf M,\] where \(f^\star=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\) is finite. This property does not require convergence of an optimizer estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal-value consistency means that the estimated latent optimum converges to the true finite optimal value in the declared mode.
assumptions_latex: \(f^\star=\inf_{x\in X}f(x)\) is finite.
\(\widehat v_n\) is the stage-n estimator of the latent optimal value.
\(\mathsf M\) is a specified mode of convergence.

notation.meaning: Estimated latent optimal value after n stages.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: convergence of the estimated extremal value is the standard value-consistency predicate

children.title: Nonunique-Optimum Regimes
children.top_down_role: Consistency interpretation when multiple global optimizers exist.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The equivalence concerns distance to the entire optimizer set, not convergence to a selected optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((X,d)\) be compact, let \(f\in C(X)\), and let \(S^\star=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in X}f(x)\). For every sequence \(x_n\in X\), \[f(x_n)\to f^\star\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{dist}(x_n,S^\star)\to0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuous objective on a compact domain, value convergence is equivalent to convergence in distance to the full optimizer set, even when minimizers are nonunique.
assumptions_latex: \((X,d)\) is compact.
\(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is continuous.
knowledge_statements.title: Value–Distance Equivalence for Point Recommendations
Nonunique-Optimum Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concrete nonunique-minimum example separating value and distance-to-set consistency from convergence to a particular optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \[X=[-1,1],\qquad f(x)=(|x|-1)^2.\] Then \(S^\star=\{-1,1\}\) and \(f^\star=0\). For \(\widehat x_n=(-1)^n\), \[f(\widehat x_n)=f^\star,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(\widehat x_n,S^\star)=0\quad\text{for every }n,\] but \((\widehat x_n)\) does not converge in \(X\). Thus value consistency and distance-to-set consistency do not imply convergence to a particular optimizer when the optimum is nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternating between two exact minimizers gives perfect value and distance-to-set consistency but no convergence to a particular optimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(\widehat x_n=(-1)^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(\widehat x_n)=f^\star\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(\widehat x_n,S^\star)=0\) for every \(n\), while \((\widehat x_n)\) has no limit.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the displayed elementary counterexample is directly checkable
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A general compactness boundary rather than a phenomenon specific to nonunique optima.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=\mathbb R\), let \(f(x)=x^2/(1+x^4)\). Then \(S^\star=\{0\}\) and \(f^\star=0\), but for \(x_n=n\), \[f(x_n)\to0=f^\star,\qquad\operatorname{dist}(x_n,S^\star)=n\to\infty.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a noncompact domain, values can approach the optimum along a sequence escaping far from every optimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\mathbb R\).
review_flags: deferred_canonical_home: boundary is not specific to nonunique optima and belongs with general argmin/value stability
knowledge_statements.title: Compactness Boundary for Value-to-Set Consistency

intermediate_metadata.reason: This leaf owns consistency interpretation when minimizers are nonunique: value and distance-to-set convergence may hold without convergence to one optimizer. General scalar-value and Hausdorff-set definitions remain in their sibling leaves. The proposed noncompact counterexample was deferred because its canonical home is general argmin/value stability, not the nonunique regime.

children.title: Acquisition-Policy Consistency
children.top_down_role: Global-consistency families organized by acquisition-policy construction.

children.title: Optimistic-Policy Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency of confidence-bound and elimination-style policies.

assumptions_latex: Only fixed-index pointwise confidence statements are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A simultaneous confidence event cannot be inferred without additional uniform or time-uniform control over indices and locations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifier boundary for confidence-bound consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Bounds of the form \(\mathbb P(|f(x)-m_n(x)|\le w_n(x))\ge1-\delta\) for each fixed \((n,x)\) do not imply \(\mathbb P(\forall n,\forall x,\ |f(x)-m_n(x)|\le w_n(x))\ge1-\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate pointwise confidence statements are insufficient for an adaptive optimistic policy; the regret argument needs a simultaneous event or a valid time-uniform adaptive substitute.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Confidence Does Not Justify Adaptive Optimism
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Confidence Does Not Justify Adaptive Optimism

assumptions_latex: \(f^\star=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) exists.
The simultaneous envelope \(|f(x)-m_n(x)|\le w_n(x)\) holds for every \(x\in X\).
The selected point minimizes the lower confidence bound within \(\eta_n\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le f(x_{n+1})-f^\star\le2w_n(x_{n+1})+\eta_n\), which tends to zero if both terms vanish.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acquisition-optimization-error variant of lower-confidence-bound consistency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(w_n(x)=\sqrt{\beta_n}s_n(x)\) and suppose \(|f(x)-m_n(x)|\le w_n(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). If \(m_n(x_{n+1})-w_n(x_{n+1})\le\inf_{x\in X}\{m_n(x)-w_n(x)\}+\eta_n\), then \(0\le f(x_{n+1})-f^\star\le2w_n(x_{n+1})+\eta_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate LCB optimization remains consistent when both the selected confidence width and acquisition-optimization error vanish.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Lower-Confidence-Bound Consistency

assumptions_latex: On an event \(E\), \(L_n(x)\le f(x)\le U_n(x)\) for every \(x\in X\) and every \(n\).
\(S^\star=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in X}f(x)\) is nonempty.
The recommendation satisfies \(\widehat x_n\in A_n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le f(\widehat x_n)-f^\star\le[U_n(\widehat x_n)-L_n(\widehat x_n)]+\sup_{x\in S^\star}[U_n(x)-L_n(x)]\), and the regret tends to zero when both width terms vanish.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency theorem for minimization policies that eliminate points using valid lower and upper confidence bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On an event \(E\), suppose \(L_n(x)\le f(x)\le U_n(x)\) for every \(x\in X\) and every \(n\). Define \(A_n=\{x:L_n(x)\le\inf_{z\in X}U_n(z)\}\), and let \(\widehat x_n\in A_n\). Every global minimizer belongs to \(A_n\), and \[0\le f(\widehat x_n)-f^\star\le[U_n(\widehat x_n)-L_n(\widehat x_n)]+\sup_{x\in S^\star}[U_n(x)-L_n(x)].\] Therefore \(f(\widehat x_n)\to f^\star\) on \(E\) whenever both displayed width terms vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid confidence elimination preserves every optimizer, and surviving recommendations are consistent when uncertainty contracts at both the recommendation and optimizer set.
knowledge_statements.title: Confidence-Set Elimination Consistency
Optimistic-Policy Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional value consistency for lower-confidence-bound minimization; model-specific results must establish the confidence and contraction hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose that, with probability at least \(1-\delta\), \[|f(x)-m_n(x)|\le \sqrt{\beta_n}s_n(x)\quad\text{for every }x\in X\text{ and every }n,\] where \(\beta_n\ge0\). If \[x_{n+1}\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in X}\bigl[m_n(x)-\sqrt{\beta_n}s_n(x)\bigr]\] and \(\sqrt{\beta_n}s_n(x_{n+1})\to0\), then on that simultaneous confidence event \[0\le f(x_{n+1})-f^\star\le2\sqrt{\beta_n}s_n(x_{n+1})\longrightarrow0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a valid simultaneous confidence event, lower-confidence-bound selections are value-consistent when their selected confidence widths vanish.
assumptions_latex: \(f^\star=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\) exists.
\(\beta_n\ge0\) and the stated simultaneous confidence envelope holds with probability at least \(1-\delta\).
The policy minimizes the lower confidence bound.
\(\sqrt{\beta_n}s_n(x_{n+1})\to0\).

notation.meaning: Posterior mean and standard deviation after n stages.
Global minimum of the latent objective.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the confidence-envelope inequality directly yields the displayed regret bound

children.title: Improvement-Policy Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency of expected- and probability-of-improvement policies.

assumptions_latex: \(Y_i=f(x)+\varepsilon_i\).
\(\varepsilon_i\) are independent \(N(0,\sigma^2)\) variables with \(\sigma>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{1\le i\le n}Y_i\to-\infty\) almost surely, so raw observed improvement does not certify latent-value consistency.

notation.meaning: Noisy observation at the repeatedly evaluated point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noise boundary for improvement policies using uncorrected observed incumbents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a fixed point \(x\) is evaluated repeatedly and \(Y_i=f(x)+\varepsilon_i\), where \(\varepsilon_i\) are independent \(N(0,\sigma^2)\) variables with \(\sigma>0\). Then \(\min_{1\le i\le n}Y_i\to-\infty\) almost surely although \(f(x)\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With unbounded observation noise, the smallest raw observation diverges downward even at one fixed design, so noisy improvement policies require a noise-aware incumbent and recommendation analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Raw Noisy Incumbents Need Not Be Consistent
knowledge_statements.title: Raw Noisy Incumbents Need Not Be Consistent

assumptions_latex: The PI target is fixed at \(\tau=1\).
Observations are exact.
Repeated evaluation of an already known point is admissible.
The posterior at the unevaluated point remains nondegenerate and assigns probability strictly below one to improvement below \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: PI-specific failure caused by a fixed target that already classifies an evaluated suboptimal point as improving.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{a,b\}\), with exact observations, \(f(a)=0\), and \(f(b)=-1\). For minimization PI with fixed target \(\tau=1\), after evaluating \(a\) the posterior at \(a\) is degenerate and \(\operatorname{PI}_n(a)=1\). If the nondegenerate posterior at \(b\) gives \(\operatorname{PI}_n(b)<1\), exact PI maximization repeatedly selects \(a\), so \(f_n^{\min}=0\ne-1=f^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Probability of improvement with an unsuitable fixed target can repeatedly select a known suboptimal point and never evaluate the optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-Target Probability of Improvement Can Exploit Forever
knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Target Probability of Improvement Can Exploit Forever

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite and the initial evaluated set is nonempty.
Observations are noise-free.
The fixed Gaussian covariance matrix on \(X\) is positive definite.
PI uses the strict incumbent target \(b_n\) and is maximized exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_n^{\min}=f^\star\text{ after at most }|X|\text{ distinct evaluations}.

notation.meaning: Best observed latent value through stage n.
Posterior probability of strict improvement below the incumbent.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noiseless finite-domain PI theorem with the target equal to the current incumbent and a nondegenerate fixed Gaussian prior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be finite, observations be exact, and the fixed Gaussian prior covariance matrix on \((f(x))_{x\in X}\) be positive definite. At stage \(n\), let \(b_n=\min_{i\le n}f(x_i)\) and select an exact maximizer of \(\operatorname{PI}_n(x)=\Pr(f(x)<b_n\mid D_n)\). Every evaluated point has PI zero, while every unevaluated point has positive conditional variance and therefore strictly positive PI. Thus PI selects an unevaluated point until all points have been sampled, and \(f_n^{\min}=f^\star\) after at most \(|X|\) distinct evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With exact observations and a positive-definite fixed Gaussian prior, incumbent-target PI exhausts a finite domain and reaches the optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain Probability-of-Improvement Consistency

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common latent best-sampled-value criterion for expected- and probability-of-improvement policies; recommendation consistency and cumulative regret are separate properties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_1,x_2,\ldots\) be the evaluations generated by an expected- or probability-of-improvement policy on \(X\), let \(f_n^{\min}=\min_{1\le i\le n}f(x_i)\), and let \(f^\star=\min_{x\in X}f(x)\). The policy is value-consistent in a declared convergence mode if \[f_n^{\min}\longrightarrow f^\star\] in that mode. Under observation noise, this criterion uses latent values rather than the minimum raw observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An EI or PI policy is value-consistent when its best sampled latent value converges to the global optimum in the stated convergence mode; raw noisy observations are not substitutes for latent values.
assumptions_latex: The global minimum value \(f^\star\) is attained.
The convergence mode—deterministic, almost sure, in probability, or in expectation—is declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f_n^{\min}\to f^\star\text{ in the declared convergence mode}.

notation.meaning: Best sampled latent objective value through stage n.

knowledge_statements.title: Improvement-Policy Value Consistency
Improvement-Policy Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A sufficient recurrent-sampling theorem for improvement policies; acquisition-specific assumptions must separately establish recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be compact, let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuous, and let \(S^\star=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in X}f(x)\). If the evaluation sequence of an improvement policy visits every open set \(U\subseteq X\) with \(U\cap S^\star\ne\varnothing\) infinitely often, then \[f_n^{\min}=\min_{1\le i\le n}f(x_i)\longrightarrow f^\star=\min_{x\in X}f(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An improvement policy whose evaluations repeatedly enter every open neighborhood intersecting the optimizer set is consistent in best sampled latent value.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact and \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous.

Starting from a nonempty evaluated set, exact minimization-EI maximization relative to the best observed value selects an unevaluated point until all points have been evaluated; hence \(f_n^{\min}=f^\star\) after at most \(|X|\) distinct queries.

Randomized-Policy Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A conditional Borel–Cantelli consistency criterion for randomized exploration on a compact metric space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((X,d)\) be compact and let \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuous. Suppose \(x_{n+1}\) has conditional law \(Q_n(\cdot\mid\mathcal F_n)\) and, for every nonempty open \(U\subseteq X\), \[\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}Q_n(U\mid\mathcal F_n)=\infty\quad\text{almost surely}.\] Under the conditional Borel–Cantelli conditions for these adapted events, \[f_n^{\min}=\min_{1\le i\le n}f(x_i)\longrightarrow f^\star=
\min_{x\in X}f(x)\quad\text{almost surely}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A randomized policy is value-consistent when conditional Borel–Cantelli applies and the cumulative conditional probability of every nonempty open region diverges.

assumptions_latex: \(Z\sim N(0,1)\) is independent of the objective ordering.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure boundary when the information utility targets a latent quantity insufficient for locating the objective minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{a,b\}\), \(f(a)=0\), and \(f(b)=-1\). Let \(Z\sim N(0,1)\) be independent of the objective ordering. Each query at \(a\) observes \(Z+\xi_n\), where \(\xi_n\sim N(0,1)\) are independent, while a query at \(b\) provides no information about \(Z\). Every finite history leaves positive mutual information in another observation at \(a\), so a policy maximizing information about \(Z\) selects \(a\) at every stage. If recommendations are restricted to evaluated points, then \(f(\widehat x_n)-f^\star=1\) for every \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximizing information about a latent target unrelated to the optimizer can gather information forever while never evaluating the optimum.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be finite and \(Y_n=f(x_n)+\varepsilon_n\), where the \(\varepsilon_n\) are independent \(N(0,\sigma^2)\) variables with \(\sigma^2>0\). Then every \(x\in X\) is sampled infinitely often, \(s_n^2(x)\to0\), and \(m_n(x)\to f(x)\) almost surely for every \(x\). Consequently, any recommendation satisfying \(m_n(\widehat x_n)-\min_xm_n(x)\to0\) obeys \(f(\widehat x_n)-\min_xf(x)\to0\) almost surely.

children.title: Bayesian Calibration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the scope of Bayesian calibration without duplicating the sibling frequentist-calibration definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The identity \(\mathbb P\{f\in C_\alpha(D)\}=1-\alpha\) averages over \(f\sim\Pi\) and data generated from the assumed likelihood. It does not imply \[P_{f_0}\{f_0\in C_\alpha(D)\}=1-\alpha\] for every fixed \(f_0\), and it need not persist under a data-generating law outside the posited joint model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prior-predictive Bayesian coverage is neither uniform fixed-objective coverage nor protection against prior or likelihood misspecification.
assumptions_latex: The credible set is calibrated only under the assumed Bayesian joint law.

If \[\Pi\{f\in C_\alpha(H_\tau)\mid H_\tau\}=1-\alpha\quad\text{almost surely},\] then under the correctly specified adaptive joint model, \[\mathbb P\{f\in C_\alpha(H_\tau)\}=1-\alpha.\]

Bayesian Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Prior-predictive calibration of Bayesian credible sets for the latent objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\sim\Pi\), let \(D\mid f\sim P_f\), and let \(C_\alpha(D)\) be measurable with \(\Pi(C_\alpha(D)\mid D)=1-\alpha\) almost surely. Under the joint prior-predictive law, \[\mathbb P\{f\in C_\alpha(D)\}=\mathbb E[\mathbb P\{f\in C_\alpha(D)\mid D\}]=1-\alpha.\] Thus exact posterior credibility entails exact average coverage when both the latent function and observations are generated from the assumed Bayesian model.

children.title: Frequentist Calibration
children.top_down_role: Uncertainty reliability interpreted for fixed objectives across observation randomness.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform asymptotic repeated-sampling calibration over a fixed objective class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A sequence \(C_{n,\alpha}(D_n)\) is uniformly asymptotically frequentist calibrated at level \(1-\alpha\) over \(\mathcal F\) if \[\sup_{f\in\mathcal F}\left|P_f^{(n)}\{f\in C_{n,\alpha}(D_n)\}-(1-\alpha)\right|\to0.\] It is uniformly asymptotically honest if \[\liminf_{n\to\infty}\inf_{f\in\mathcal F}P_f^{(n)}\{f\in C_{n,\alpha}(D_n)\}\ge1-\alpha.\] Pointwise convergence for every fixed \(f\) need not imply either uniform condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform asymptotic calibration makes worst-case fixed-objective coverage error vanish; honesty requires uniformly nondeficient limiting coverage. Pointwise convergence is weaker.
assumptions_latex: For every \(f\in\mathcal F\), \(D_n\) has sampling law \(P_f^{(n)}\).
The coverage events are measurable.

notation.meaning: sample-size-n law for fixed objective f

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F\) be a class of fixed objective functions and let \(D\sim P_f\) for \(f\in\mathcal F\). A random set \(C_\alpha(D)\) is pointwise frequentist calibrated at level \(1-\alpha\) on \(\mathcal F\) if \[P_f\{f\in C_\alpha(D)\}=1-\alpha\qquad\text{for every }f\in\mathcal F.\] It is conservative if the equality is replaced by \(\ge 1-\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A confidence set is frequentist calibrated when its repeated-data coverage is nominal for every fixed objective in the stated class.

children.title: Calibration-Interpretation Gap
children.top_down_role: Boundaries between prior-average reliability and fixed-objective coverage.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact averaging relation between prior-predictive and fixed-objective coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the joint model \(\Theta\sim\Pi\) and \(D\mid\Theta=\theta\sim P_\theta\), every measurable random set \(C(D)\) satisfies \[P\{\Theta\in C(D)\}=\int P_\theta\{\theta\in C(D)\}\,\Pi(d\theta).\] Consequently, fixed-objective coverage \(P_\theta\{\theta\in C(D)\}=1-\alpha\) for \(\Pi\)-almost every \(\theta\) implies prior-predictive coverage \(1-\alpha\). The converse fixes only the prior average of the coverage function and need not make that function constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bayesian coverage is the prior average of fixed-objective coverage. Constant frequentist coverage implies Bayesian coverage, but nominal average coverage does not imply constant fixed-objective coverage.
assumptions_latex: \(\Theta\sim\Pi\) and \(D\mid\Theta=\theta\sim P_\theta\) define a joint law.
\(C(D)\) has a measurable coverage event.

notation.meaning: prior law of the latent parameter or objective
sampling law conditional on fixed value theta

knowledge_statements.title: Coverage-Averaging Identity
Calibration-Interpretation Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bayesian average coverage need not imply fixed-parameter frequentist coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\theta\sim N(0,\tau^2)\), observe \(Y\mid\theta\sim N(\theta,\sigma^2)\), and form the central \((1-\alpha)\)-posterior interval. Writing \(a=\tau^2/(\tau^2+\sigma^2)\), its center is \(aY\) and half-width is \(z_{1-\alpha/2}\sigma\tau/\sqrt{\tau^2+\sigma^2}\). Its prior-predictive coverage is \(1-\alpha\), but at fixed \(\theta\) its coverage equals \[\Phi\!\left(\frac{h-(1-a)\theta}{a\sigma}\right)-\Phi\!\left(\frac{-h-(1-a)\theta}{a\sigma}\right),\] which depends on \(\theta\) and tends to zero as \(|\theta|\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conjugate Bayesian credible interval is calibrated on average under its prior, yet its fixed-parameter coverage varies and vanishes for extreme means.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\tau,\sigma<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Bayesian prior-predictive calibration does not imply uniform frequentist calibration over \(\theta\in\mathbb R\).

notation.meaning: q-quantile of the standard normal law

knowledge_statements.title: Latent-Function Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior epistemic uncertainty about the noise-free objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a latent objective \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) and data \(D\), latent-function uncertainty at \(x\in\mathcal X\) is the posterior conditional distribution \(\mathcal L(f(x)\mid D)\). When its second moment exists, its scalar variance summary is \[v_f(x)=\operatorname{Var}(f(x)\mid D).\] In a Gaussian-process model this conditional law is Gaussian with posterior mean \(m_D(x)\) and variance \(v_f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Latent-function uncertainty is posterior uncertainty about the noise-free objective value, summarized by its posterior variance when finite.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is a random latent function under the fitted Bayesian model.
\(\mathbb E[f(x)^2\mid D]<\infty\) when variance is used.

children.title: Observation Uncertainty
children.top_down_role: Variability associated with noisy feedback at evaluated inputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Observation Uncertainty
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional variability introduced by the observation channel at a proposed evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a future observation satisfies \(Y(x)=f(x)+\varepsilon(x)\), where \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon(x)\mid f(x),D]=0\). Observation uncertainty at \(x\) is the conditional law \(\mathcal L(Y(x)\mid f(x),D)\), which is determined by translating the conditional noise law \(\mathcal L(\varepsilon(x)\mid f(x),D)\) by \(f(x)\). When finite, its variance is \[v_\varepsilon(x,f)=\operatorname{Var}(Y(x)\mid f(x),D).\] Under additive, conditionally independent homoscedastic noise, this variance equals the constant \(\sigma^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Observation uncertainty is variability in a measured response conditional on the latent objective; its law is the noise law shifted by the latent value, and under homoscedastic additive noise its variance is constant.
assumptions_latex: \(Y(x)=f(x)+\varepsilon(x)\).
\(\mathbb E[\varepsilon(x)\mid f(x),D]=0\).

children.title: Uncertainty Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Separation of epistemic uncertainty from feedback variability in optimization decisions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional covariance decomposition, including correlated observation noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite tuple \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\), let \(Y_X=f_X+\varepsilon_X\), assume finite conditional second moments, and suppose \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_X\mid f_X,D]=0\). Then \[\operatorname{Cov}(Y_X\mid D)=\operatorname{Cov}(f_X\mid D)+\mathbb E[\operatorname{Cov}(\varepsilon_X\mid f_X,D)\mid D].\] If the errors are conditionally independent with variances \(\sigma_i^2\), the second term is \(\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_1^2,\ldots,\sigma_m^2)\); correlated errors contribute their full conditional covariance matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint predictive covariance is latent posterior covariance plus expected conditional noise covariance. Independent noise adds diagonal variance, while correlated noise adds cross-covariances.
assumptions_latex: \(Y_X=f_X+\varepsilon_X\) has finite conditional second moments given \(D\).
\(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_X\mid f_X,D]=0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior predictive variance split into latent and observation components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Y(x)=f(x)+\varepsilon(x)\) with finite conditional second moments and \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon(x)\mid f(x),D]=0\), the conditional law of total variance gives \[\operatorname{Var}(Y(x)\mid D)=\operatorname{Var}(f(x)\mid D)+\mathbb E[\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon(x)\mid f(x),D)\mid D].\] If the noise is conditionally independent of \(f(x)\) and homoscedastic with variance \(\sigma^2\), then \(\operatorname{Var}(Y(x)\mid D)=v_f(x)+\sigma^2\).

knowledge_statements.title: Local Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise predictive calibration at each fixed design location.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_{n,x}\) be a data-dependent predictive distribution function for a future response \(Y(x)\), and let \(P\) denote the data-generating law. The predictor is asymptotically locally calibrated at \(x\in\mathcal X\) if, for every \(u\in(0,1)\) at which the relevant distribution is continuous, \[P\{Y(x)\le F_{n,x}^{-1}(u)\}\longrightarrow u\qquad(n\to\infty).\] Local calibration on \(S\subseteq\mathcal X\) requires this convergence separately for every fixed \(x\in S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local calibration requires nominal predictive coverage at each fixed design point, without requiring convergence uniform over the design space.
assumptions_latex: The target response distribution is continuous at the stated quantile.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\{Y(x)\le F_{n,x}^{-1}(u)\}\to u\) for each fixed \(x\) and \(u\).

notation.meaning: predictive distribution after n observations at location x
subset on which pointwise calibration is required
