children.title: Global Calibration
children.top_down_role: Uncertainty reliability across the full search domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform predictive calibration over locations and quantile levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_{n,x}\) predict a future response \(Y(x)\) for \(x\in\mathcal X\). For \(U\subset(0,1)\), the predictor is globally calibrated on \(\mathcal X\times U\) if \[\sup_{x\in\mathcal X,\,u\in U}\left|P\{Y(x)\le F_{n,x}^{-1}(u)\}-u\right|\longrightarrow0\qquad(n\to\infty).\] When \(U=[\delta,1-\delta]\), this definition excludes unstable extreme quantiles while requiring uniform spatial calibration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global calibration requires the worst predictive coverage error across all locations and specified quantile levels to vanish.
assumptions_latex: The displayed probabilities are measurable in \((x,u)\).

notation.meaning: quantile levels subject to uniform calibration

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The uniform calibration condition is mathematically coherent and contrasts correctly with the local definition, but calling this global calibration requires an authoritative source and locator.

children.title: Local-to-Global Calibration Gap
children.top_down_role: Limits on extending neighborhood-level reliability to domain-wide conclusions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid predictive-distribution realization of a moving local calibration defect.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y(x)\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) for every \(x\in[0,1]\), fix \(0<c<1/4\), and set \[e_n(x)=\max\{1-n|x-1/n|,0\},\qquad Q_{n,x}(u)=u+4c e_n(x)u(1-u),\quad0\le u\le1.\] Because \(\partial Q_{n,x}(u)/\partial u=1+4c e_n(x)(1-2u)>0\), \(Q_{n,x}\) is a valid predictive quantile function. Its calibration error is \[E_n(x,u)=P\{Y(x)\le Q_{n,x}(u)\}-u=4c e_n(x)u(1-u).\] For every fixed \((x,u)\), \(E_n(x,u)\to0\), whereas \(\sup_{x,u}|E_n(x,u)|=E_n(1/n,1/2)=c\) for every \(n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valid predictive distributions can carry a defect that moves through the domain: every fixed location and quantile becomes calibrated while worst-case error stays constant.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X=[0,1]\) and \(Y(x)\sim\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\) for every \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_n(x,u)\to0\) for every fixed \((x,u)\), but \(\sup_{x,u}|E_n(x,u)|=c\) for every \(n\).
knowledge_statements.title: Moving Predictive-Calibration Defect

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A joint regularity condition promoting pointwise location-and-quantile calibration to uniform calibration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal X,d)\) be compact, let \(U\subset(0,1)\) be compact, and let \(E_n:\mathcal X\times U\to\mathbb R\) be uniformly equicontinuous on the product metric space. If \(E_n(x,u)\to0\) for every fixed \((x,u)\in\mathcal X\times U\), then \[\sup_{x\in\mathcal X,\,u\in U}|E_n(x,u)|\to0.\] Thus pointwise local calibration promotes to global calibration when the calibration errors have a common joint location-and-quantile modulus on a compact index set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On compact location and quantile sets, pointwise calibration plus a common joint continuity modulus implies uniform global calibration.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal X,d)\) and \(U\subset(0,1)\) are compact.
\(E_n\) is uniformly equicontinuous jointly in \((x,u)\).
\(E_n(x,u)\to0\) for every fixed \((x,u)\).

notation.meaning: calibration error at location x and quantile level u

review_flags: builder_record_revised: joint equicontinuity over location and quantile is required for the stated global criterion
knowledge_statements.title: Equicontinuous Local-to-Global Promotion
Local-to-Global Calibration Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise vanishing calibration error does not imply uniform calibration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X=[0,1]\) and define calibration-error functions \(e_n(x)=\max\{1-n|x-1/n|,0\}\). For every fixed \(x\in[0,1]\), \(e_n(x)\to0\): at \(x=0\) the value is always zero, and for \(x>0\) the moving support eventually misses \(x\). Nevertheless, \[\sup_{x\in[0,1]}e_n(x)=e_n(1/n)=1\qquad\text{for every }n.\] Hence pointwise local calibration errors can vanish while the global worst-case error remains maximal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A calibration defect can move through the domain, disappearing at every fixed point while its worst-case magnitude never decreases.
assumptions_latex: Calibration error is measured pointwise by a nonnegative function \(e_n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pointwise convergence \(e_n(x)\to0\) does not imply \(\sup_x e_n(x)\to0\).

notation.meaning: absolute calibration error after n observations at x

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The moving-spike construction correctly separates pointwise from uniform convergence, but it is stated only for abstract error functions and does not show that these functions arise from valid predictive distributions and coverage probabilities. A source or explicit realization is needed before accepting it as a calibration counterexample.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Replication Equivalence under Known Homoscedastic Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient reduction of repeated observations at one site under a known common Gaussian variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Y_j=f(x)+\varepsilon_j\) for \(j=1,\ldots,r\), with conditionally independent \(\varepsilon_j\sim N(0,\sigma^2)\) and known \(\sigma^2\), then \[\bar Y_r\mid f(x)\sim N\!\left(f(x),\frac{\sigma^2}{r}\right).\] The replicated likelihood factors into a term depending on \(f(x)\) only through \(\bar Y_r\) and a factor independent of \(f(x)\); therefore the replications are equivalent for inference about \(f(x)\) to one averaged observation with variance \(\sigma^2/r\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With known independent constant Gaussian noise, repeated observations reduce to their mean with effective variance sigma squared divided by the replication count.
assumptions_latex: The common variance \(\sigma^2>0\) is known.
Replicate errors are conditionally independent Gaussian variables.
The latent value is unchanged across replications.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar Y_r\mid f(x)\sim N(f(x),\sigma^2/r)\), and \(\bar Y_r\) is sufficient for \(f(x)\) in the replicated likelihood.

notation.meaning: Mean of the r replicated observations.

knowledge_statements.title: Replication Equivalence under Known Homoscedastic Noise
Known Homoscedastic Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian observation model with a fixed, externally known noise variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A noisy objective has known homoscedastic Gaussian noise when observations satisfy \[Y_i=f(x_i)+\varepsilon_i,\qquad \varepsilon_i\mid x_i,f\mathrel{\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}}N(0,\sigma^2),\] where the same constant \(\sigma^2>0\) applies at every design point and is supplied to the inference and acquisition procedures rather than estimated from \(D_n=\{(x_i,Y_i)\}_{i=1}^n\). Conditional on \(f\) and the design, the observation covariance is \(\sigma^2 I_n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Known homoscedastic noise means independent Gaussian errors share one fixed variance that is given to the Bayesian optimization procedure.
assumptions_latex: \(\sigma^2>0\) is known.
Errors are conditionally independent given the latent function and design.

u=\sum_i(r_i-1)\), and \[\widehat\sigma^2_{\mathrm{pool}}= rac{\sum_i(r_i-1)S_i^2}{
u}.\] Then \(\mathbb E[\widehat\sigma^2_{\mathrm{pool}}]=\sigma^2\) and \(
u\widehat\sigma^2_{\mathrm{pool}}/\sigma^2\sim\chi^2_
u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within-site replication gives an unbiased pooled estimator of a common Gaussian noise variance and an exact chi-square sampling law.
assumptions_latex: Every included site has at least two independent replications.
Errors are independent Gaussian variables with the same variance at all sites.

knowledge_statements.title: Pooled Replication Estimator of a Common Noise Variance
Estimated Homoscedastic Noise
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Plug-in or joint Bayesian inference for an unknown constant noise variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(Y_i=f(x_i)+\varepsilon_i\) with \(\varepsilon_i\mid f,x_i,\sigma^2\mathrel{\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}}N(0,\sigma^2)\), but \(\sigma^2\) is unknown. An estimated-homoscedastic-noise model obtains \(\widehat\sigma_n^2=T(D_n)\) and uses the plug-in posterior \(\Pi(df\mid D_n,\widehat\sigma_n^2)\), or assigns a prior \(p(d\sigma^2)\) and uses the marginal posterior \[\Pi(df\mid D_n)=\int\Pi(df\mid D_n,\sigma^2)\,p(d\sigma^2\mid D_n).\] The variance remains spatially constant in either formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The common noise variance is unknown and is either plugged in from data or integrated out under a joint Bayesian posterior.
assumptions_latex: Observation errors are conditionally independent Gaussian with one common variance.
\(\widehat\sigma_n^2\) is measurable with respect to \(D_n\) in the plug-in formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Inference uses either \(\Pi(df\mid D_n,\widehat\sigma_n^2)\) or the posterior mixture over \(\sigma^2\).

notation.meaning: posterior distribution of the common variance

knowledge_statements.title: Studentized Correction for Independently Estimated Gaussian Scale
Noise-Scale Estimation Risk
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predictive undercoverage caused by treating an independently estimated, underestimated noise scale as known.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y-\mu\sim N(0,\sigma^2)\), and let \(\widehat\sigma>0\) be fixed or estimated from data conditionally independent of the future response \(Y\). Construct the nominal \((1-\alpha)\) interval \([\mu-z_{1-\alpha/2}\widehat\sigma,\mu+z_{1-\alpha/2}\widehat\sigma]\). Conditional on \(\widehat\sigma\), its true coverage is \[2\Phi\!\left(z_{1-\alpha/2}\frac{\widehat\sigma}{\sigma}\right)-1.\] This is below \(1-\alpha\) whenever \(\widehat\sigma<\sigma\), and it tends to zero as \(\widehat\sigma/\sigma\to0\). Thus guarantees derived for known noise require estimation-error control, an appropriate treatment of dependence, or posterior integration when the noise scale is estimated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a future Gaussian response independent of the scale-estimation data, plugging in an underestimated noise scale makes the interval too narrow, and its conditional coverage approaches zero as the estimated-to-true scale ratio vanishes.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\alpha<1\) and \(0<\widehat\sigma,\sigma<\infty\).
Conditional on \(\widehat\sigma\), \(Y-\mu\sim N(0,\sigma^2)\); in particular, the future response is independent of the data used to estimate \(\widehat\sigma\).
The plug-in interval ignores uncertainty in \(\widehat\sigma\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Replication Requirement for Sitewise Variance Estimation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of the usual within-site plug-in variance in stochastic kriging.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The within-site estimator \[S_i^2=\frac{1}{r_i-1}\sum_{j=1}^{r_i}(Y_{ij}-\bar Y_i)^2\] is defined as an unbiased sample variance only when \(r_i\ge2\). With \(r_i=1\), the site supplies no within-site residual degree of freedom, so \(\tau^2(x_i)\) cannot be estimated by this sitewise formula and must instead be known, pooled, regularized, or modeled across sites.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A singly sampled site cannot provide its own unbiased within-site noise-variance estimate; stochastic kriging must obtain that variance elsewhere.
assumptions_latex: The sitewise noise variance is to be estimated solely from independent replications at that site.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_i=1\) provides zero within-site residual degrees of freedom and does not define \(S_i^2\).
knowledge_statements.title: Replication Requirement for Sitewise Variance Estimation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of increased replication when site variances and covariance parameters are fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be the latent covariance matrix at sampled sites and \(R(r)=\operatorname{diag}(\tau^2(x_i)/r_i)\). For prediction sites, define \[V_\star(r)=K_{\star\star}-K_{\star X}(K+R(r))^{-1}K_{X\star}.\] If \(r'_i\ge r_i\) at every site, then \(R(r')\preceq R(r)\) and \(V_\star(r')\preceq V_\star(r)\). Thus additional independent replication cannot increase latent posterior covariance when site variances and model parameters are held fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasing independent replication lowers effective site-mean noise and cannot increase fixed-parameter stochastic-kriging posterior covariance.
assumptions_latex: \(K+R(r)\) and \(K+R(r')\) are positive definite.
Sitewise replication errors are independent with known variances \(\tau^2(x_i)\).
Latent covariance and noise-variance parameters are held fixed.

notation.meaning: Effective covariance matrix of replicated site means.
Posterior latent covariance at the prediction sites.

knowledge_statements.title: Replication Monotonicity of Stochastic-Kriging Uncertainty

assumptions_latex: At each design site \(x_i\in\mathcal X\), replications satisfy \(Y_{ij}=f(x_i)+\varepsilon_{ij}\) for \(j=1,\ldots,r_i\).
Conditional on the sites, the errors are centered, independent across replications and sites, and have finite site-dependent variances \(\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_{ij}\mid x_i)=\tau^2(x_i)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting covariance separates latent-process uncertainty from replication-estimated simulation noise.

notation.meaning: Latent mean response modeled by a Gaussian process.
Sample mean and unbiased sample variance at site \(x_i\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical stochastic-kriging representation with independent, input-dependent simulation noise estimated from replications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\sim\operatorname{GP}(m,k)\), and define \(\bar Y_i=r_i^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{r_i}Y_{ij}\) and \(S_i^2=(r_i-1)^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{r_i}(Y_{ij}-\bar Y_i)^2\). Then \(\bar Y_i=f(x_i)+\bar\varepsilon_i\), with \(\operatorname{Var}(\bar\varepsilon_i\mid x_i)=\tau^2(x_i)/r_i\). Stochastic kriging uses the observation covariance \[\operatorname{Cov}(\bar Y_i,\bar Y_\ell\mid X)=k(x_i,x_\ell)+\mathbf 1_{\{i=\ell\}}\frac{\tau^2(x_i)}{r_i},\] commonly replacing \(\tau^2(x_i)\) by \(S_i^2\). Thus replication counts and within-site variances determine the diagonal simulation-noise matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stochastic kriging combines a Gaussian-process covariance for the latent mean with site-specific noise variances estimated from replicated simulation outputs.
knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic-Kriging Noise Models

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inference boundary for an exponentiated Gaussian-process observation variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(y_i\mid f_i,g_i\sim N(f_i,\exp(g_i))\), the likelihood contribution as a function of \(g_i\) is proportional to \[\exp\!\left[-\frac12g_i-\frac12(y_i-f_i)^2e^{-g_i}\right].\] It is not Gaussian in \(g_i\). Consequently, a Gaussian-process prior for \(g\) is nonconjugate and the exact finite-dimensional posterior of \(g\) is generally non-Gaussian.

The observations use the stated Gaussian log-variance likelihood.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior predictive uncertainty for a centered observation residual with random local variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under \(Y_\star=f_\star+\varepsilon_\star\), with \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_\star\mid f_\star,g_\star,\mathcal D]=0\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_\star\mid f_\star,g_\star,\mathcal D)=\exp(g_\star)\), \[\mathbb E[Y_\star\mid\mathcal D]=\mathbb E[f_\star\mid\mathcal D],\qquad \operatorname{Var}(Y_\star\mid\mathcal D)=\operatorname{Var}(f_\star\mid\mathcal D)+\mathbb E[\exp(g_\star)\mid\mathcal D].\]

assumptions_latex: The conditional residual is centered and has variance \(\exp(g_\star)\).
The displayed posterior moments are finite.

assumptions_latex: Observations satisfy \(Y_i=f(x_i)+\varepsilon_i\) on an input domain \(\mathcal X\).
Conditional on latent functions, \(\varepsilon_i\) are independent Gaussian variables with variances determined by a positive link.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent Gaussian-process priors for mean and log-variance; other links and coupled priors are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\sim\operatorname{GP}(m_f,k_f)\) and \(g\sim\operatorname{GP}(m_g,k_g)\) be independent latent processes on \(\mathcal X\). A latent variance-process surrogate is specified by \[Y_i\mid f,g,x_i\sim\mathcal N\!\left(f(x_i),\exp(g(x_i))\right),\qquad i=1,\ldots,n.\] The exponential link guarantees \(\exp(g(x))>0\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\). Its posterior predictive distribution at a new input is obtained by integrating both latent quantities: \[p(y_\star\mid x_\star,\mathcal D)=\int p(y_\star\mid f_\star,g_\star)\,p(f_\star,g_\star\mid\mathcal D)\,d(f_\star,g_\star).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A latent variance-process model places separate process priors on the response mean and log noise variance, then integrates uncertainty in both surfaces.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robustness is represented through the observation likelihood, not through a robust acquisition rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A robust noise model replaces the Gaussian likelihood by a residual law tolerant of extreme observations. One standard specification is \[Y_i\mid f,s,x_i\sim t_\nu\!\left(f(x_i),s(x_i)\right),\qquad \nu>0,\quad s(x_i)>0.\] A contamination alternative is \[Y_i\mid f,x_i\sim(1-\epsilon)\mathcal N\!\left(f(x_i),\sigma^2(x_i)\right)+\epsilon Q_{x_i},\qquad 0\leq\epsilon<1,\] where \(Q_{x_i}\) is an outlier distribution. Both models retain a latent location \(f(x_i)\) while allowing observations inconsistent with a single Gaussian noise law; posterior inference and acquisition values must use the selected non-Gaussian likelihood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robust noise models use heavy-tailed or contaminated likelihoods so isolated outliers need not dominate inference about the latent objective.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of dependent simulation noise on a pairwise design contrast.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_a=f(x_a)+\varepsilon_a\) and \(Y_b=f(x_b)+\varepsilon_b\), with \(\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_a)=v_a\), \(\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_b)=v_b\), and \(\operatorname{Cov}(\varepsilon_a,\varepsilon_b)=c_{ab}\). Then \[\operatorname{Var}\!\left((Y_a-Y_b)-(f(x_a)-f(x_b))\right)=v_a+v_b-2c_{ab}.\] Thus the coupling reduces this contrast's variance exactly when \(c_{ab}>0\), increases it when \(c_{ab}<0\), and leaves it unchanged when \(c_{ab}=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Correlated simulation errors change pairwise comparison precision through their covariance; common random numbers help a contrast only when they induce positive covariance.

Here \(\mathcal H\) may encode shared random-number streams, replication blocks, or simulator state. If \(f_X\) has covariance \(K_X\) and is conditionally independent of \(\varepsilon\), then \[\operatorname{Cov}(Y\mid X,\mathcal H)=K_X+\Sigma_\varepsilon(X,\mathcal H).\] Off-diagonal entries of \(\Sigma_\varepsilon\) represent dependent simulation errors and cannot generally be replaced by a diagonal nugget without changing posterior means, posterior variances, and noise-aware acquisition values.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected improvement conditional on a latent incumbent value; distinct from constrained expected improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization, given a latent incumbent value \(B=b\), define \[\operatorname{CEI}(x;b)=\mathbb E[(b-F_x)_+\mid\mathcal D,B=b].\] If \(F_x\mid\mathcal D,B=b\sim\mathcal N(\mu_{x\mid b},s_{x\mid b}^2)\) and \(s_{x\mid b}>0\), then \[\operatorname{CEI}(x;b)=(b-\mu_{x\mid b})\Phi(z)+s_{x\mid b}\phi(z),\qquad z=\frac{b-\mu_{x\mid b}}{s_{x\mid b}}.\] For \(s_{x\mid b}=0\), the value is \((b-\mu_{x\mid b})_+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional expected improvement is the expected latent reduction below a fixed latent incumbent, with the usual Gaussian closed form.

If \(F\sim\mathcal N(\mu,s^2)\), \(s>0\), then \[h'(c)=\Phi((c-\mu)/s),\qquad h''(c)=s^{-1}\phi((c-\mu)/s).\] This statement cannot be applied by varying the conditioning value \(b\) in \(F_x\mid B=b\) unless that conditional law is otherwise held fixed.

children.title: Noisy Expected Improvement

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Family showing why an observed noisy response cannot be used as an exact latent incumbent in NEI.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an existing latent value and a proposed latent value both equal zero almost surely, while the existing observation is \(Y_0=\varepsilon\) with \(\varepsilon\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)\), \(\sigma>0\). Correct latent improvement is zero, but using \(Y_0\) as the incumbent gives \[\mathbb E[(Y_0-0)_+]=\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{2\pi}}>0.\] Hence observation noise alone can create spurious apparent improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Treating a noisy response as an exact incumbent can report positive expected improvement even when both latent values are identical.
assumptions_latex: \(F_{x_0}=F_x=0\) almost surely.
The existing observation has centered Gaussian noise with \(\sigma>0\).

notation.meaning: Noisy observation at the existing design.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-candidate noisy expected improvement using the best latent value at previously sampled designs as the random incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), \(F_X=(F_{x_1},\ldots,F_{x_n})\), and \(B(F_X)=\min_iF_{x_i}\). For minimization, \[\operatorname{NEI}(x)=\mathbb E\!\left[(B(F_X)-F_x)_+\mid\mathcal D\right] =\mathbb E_{F_X\mid\mathcal D}\!\left[\mathbb E[(B(F_X)-F_x)_+\mid\mathcal D,F_X]\right].\] Thus noisy responses are not substituted as exact latent incumbent values; the joint posterior dependence between old and proposed latent values is retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noisy expected improvement averages latent improvement over posterior uncertainty in sampled latent values and the proposed candidate.
assumptions_latex: The problem is minimization.
The joint posterior of old and proposed latent values is proper.
The positive-part payoff is integrable.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proposed batch \(X_q=(x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(q)})\), define \[\operatorname{qNEI}(X_q)=\mathbb E\!\left[\left(B(F_X)-\min_{1\le j\le q}F_{x^{(j)}}\right)_+\middle|\mathcal D\right],\] with expectation over the joint posterior of existing and proposed latent values. For \(q=1\), this reduces to \(\operatorname{NEI}(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Batch noisy expected improvement integrates the best latent improvement in a proposed batch over all relevant posterior uncertainty.
assumptions_latex: The joint posterior is proper.
The batch positive-part payoff is integrable.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), let \(F_X=(F_{x_1},\ldots,F_{x_n})\), and define the random latent incumbent \(B(F_X)=\min_{1\leq i\leq n}F_{x_i}\). Noisy expected improvement is the posterior average \[\operatorname{NEI}(x)=\mathbb E_{F_X\mid\mathcal D}\!\left[\mathbb E\!\left[(B(F_X)-F_x)_+\mid\mathcal D,F_X\right]\right].\] Equivalently, \[\operatorname{NEI}(x)=\int \operatorname{CEI}\!\left(x;B(f_X)\mid F_X=f_X\right)p(f_X\mid\mathcal D)\,df_X.\] Thus observed noisy responses are not treated as exact incumbent values; their corresponding latent values are integrated under the posterior.

children.title: Incumbent-Uncertainty Effects

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dependence Can Reverse the Jensen Ordering
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete posterior family showing that the independent-incumbent ordering fails under dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Condition on \(\mathcal D\), and let \(B=F_x\) take values \(0\) and \(2\), each with probability \(1/2\). Then \[\mathbb E[(B-F_x)_+\mid\mathcal D]=0,\] while \(\mathbb E[B\mid\mathcal D]=1\) and \[\mathbb E[(1-F_x)_+\mid\mathcal D]=\tfrac12.\] Thus integrating the dependent incumbent can give strictly less improvement than plugging in its mean.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perfect dependence between incumbent and candidate values can reverse the ordering valid under independence.
assumptions_latex: The conditional joint distribution is the stated two-point distribution.
knowledge_statements.title: Dependence Can Reverse the Jensen Ordering

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of integrating rather than replacing a posterior-random latent incumbent in minimization improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For integrable \((B-F_x)_+\), \[\mathbb E[(B-F_x)_+\mid\mathcal D]=\mathbb E_{B\mid\mathcal D}\!\left[\mathbb E[(B-F_x)_+\mid\mathcal D,B]\right].\] This generally differs from \(\mathbb E[(\widehat b-F_x)_+\mid\mathcal D]\). If \(B\) and \(F_x\) are conditionally independent and \(\bar b=\mathbb E[B\mid\mathcal D]\), convexity gives \[\mathbb E[(B-F_x)_+\mid\mathcal D]\ge\mathbb E[(\bar b-F_x)_+\mid\mathcal D].\] Under arbitrary posterior dependence, no such universal ordering holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integrating incumbent uncertainty generally differs from plugging in a point estimate; independence gives a Jensen ordering, while dependence removes it.
assumptions_latex: The problem is minimization and the positive-part payoffs are integrable.
The directional inequality additionally assumes conditional independence of \(B\) and \(F_x\).

notation.meaning: A point summary of the incumbent posterior.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of integrating, rather than plugging in, a noisy latent incumbent in minimization EI.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The improvement value with an uncertain incumbent is \[\mathbb E\!\left[(B-F_x)_+\mid\mathcal D\right]=\mathbb E_{B\mid\mathcal D}\!\left[\mathbb E\!\left[(B-F_x)_+\mid\mathcal D,B\right]\right].\] A plug-in rule instead evaluates \(\mathbb E[(\hat b-F_x)_+\mid\mathcal D]\) for a summary \(\hat b\), such as \(\mathbb E[B\mid\mathcal D]\). In general, \[\mathbb E[(B-F_x)_+\mid\mathcal D]\neq\mathbb E[(\hat b-F_x)_+\mid\mathcal D],\] because the positive-part map is nonlinear and the joint dependence between \(B\) and \(F_x\) matters. Equality requires special degeneracy or distributional structure and is not implied by \(\hat b=\mathbb E[B\mid\mathcal D]\).

source_refs.locator: 7.4 The Knowledge Gradient Algorithm for Discrete Alternatives p. 262
source_refs.source_title: Approximate Dynamic Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For maximization, define \(V_n=\max_{a\in\mathcal A}\mu_n(a)\), where \(\mu_n(a)=\mathbb E[f(a)\mid\mathcal D_n]\). For each admissible measurement \(x\in\mathcal M\), define \[\operatorname{KG}_n(x)=\mathbb E_{Y\mid x,\mathcal D_n}\!\left[\max_{a\in\mathcal A}\mu_{n+1}(a;Y,x)\right]-V_n.\] Starting from prior data \(\mathcal D_0\), at stage \(n\) choose \(x_{n+1}\in\arg\max_{x\in\mathcal M}\operatorname{KG}_n(x)\), observe the noisy response \(Y_{n+1}\), and update the posterior. After the measurement budget \(N\), return any \(a_N\in\arg\max_{a\in\mathcal A}\mu_N(a)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For finite alternatives, noisy knowledge gradient measures where one additional noisy observation is expected to increase the best terminal posterior-mean value most, samples a maximizing measurement, and finally recommends an alternative with maximal posterior mean.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonnegativity and One-Step Interpretation of Noisy Knowledge Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural property of the accepted finite-alternative noisy knowledge-gradient seed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\mathbb E[\mu_{n+1}(a;Y,x)\mid\mathcal D_n,x]=\mu_n(a)\) for every terminal alternative \(a\). Then \[\operatorname{KG}_n(x)=\mathbb E\!\left[\max_a\mu_{n+1}(a;Y,x)\mid\mathcal D_n,x\right]-\max_a\mu_n(a)\ge0.\] Hence \(\max_x\operatorname{KG}_n(x)=0\) certifies zero expected improvement from one additional admissible measurement in the specified terminal posterior-mean value; it does not certify zero multistep value or global identification of the true optimizer.

children.title: Noise-Aware Confidence Policies
children.top_down_role: Optimistic policies whose uncertainty assessments incorporate stochastic feedback.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic upper-confidence policy for maximizing a latent objective under modeled noisy feedback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At round \(t\), form \[U_t(x)=\mu_{t-1}(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}\,s_{t-1}(x),\] select \(x_t\in\arg\max_{x\in\mathcal X}U_t(x)\), observe a noisy response, and update the posterior using its observation likelihood. If \[|f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)|\le\sqrt{\beta_t}s_{t-1}(x)\] simultaneously over the points and rounds required by the analysis, then \(U_t\) is optimistic there. The sequence \(\beta_t\) is not universal and must be chosen for the stated domain, model class, noise assumptions, horizon, and confidence level.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A noise-aware confidence policy maximizes a posterior upper bound whose uncertainty comes from conditioning on noisy feedback.
assumptions_latex: Posterior means and latent standard deviations are defined after each noisy update.
A measurable maximizer or declared approximate-maximizer rule is available.
Any claimed guarantee uses a confidence schedule valid for its stated assumptions.
review_flags: Replaces the deferred seed without asserting an unsupported universal calibration schedule.
knowledge_statements.title: Noise-Aware Upper-Confidence Policy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kernel-independent pathwise consequence of exact UCB maximization on a valid confidence event.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^\star\in\arg\max_x f(x)\). If the confidence inequality holds at \(x^\star\) and \(x_t\), and \(x_t\) maximizes \(U_t\), then \[r_t=f(x^\star)-f(x_t)\le2\sqrt{\beta_t}\,s_{t-1}(x_t).\] Consequently, on a simultaneous confidence event, \[R_T=\sum_{t=1}^T r_t\le2\sum_{t=1}^T\sqrt{\beta_t}\,s_{t-1}(x_t).\] Converting this reduction into a numerical rate requires an additional bound on accumulated posterior widths.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On the valid confidence event, UCB regret is bounded by twice the selected confidence radius; a numerical rate additionally needs a model-specific width bound.
assumptions_latex: A global maximizer exists.
The stated confidence inequalities hold at the optimizer and selected point.
The acquisition is maximized exactly.
knowledge_statements.title: Confidence-Width Regret Reduction

assumptions_latex: For every round \(t\), the surrogate supplies posterior mean \(\mu_{t-1}\) and standard deviation \(s_{t-1}\) on \(\mathcal X\).
A sequence \((\beta_t)_{t\geq1}\) is chosen so the simultaneous confidence event has the desired coverage.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On the confidence event, maximizing the upper confidence bound is optimistic for the unknown objective at every round.

notation.meaning: Posterior standard deviation incorporating noisy feedback.

review_flags: No supplied locator states a noise-aware confidence-policy theorem or calibration schedule.
Requires source specifying assumptions under which the simultaneous confidence event holds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic noisy upper-confidence policy; no particular kernel, domain, or regret schedule is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For maximization, initialize a probabilistic surrogate with its observation-noise model. At round \(t\), form \[U_t(x)=\mu_{t-1}(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}\,s_{t-1}(x),\] choose \(x_t\in\arg\max_{x\in\mathcal X}U_t(x)\), observe a noisy response, and update both posterior moments using the likelihood. The policy is calibrated at level \(1-\delta\) when \[\mathbb P\!\left(\forall t\geq1,\ \forall x\in\mathcal X:\ |f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)|\leq\sqrt{\beta_t}\,s_{t-1}(x)\right)\geq1-\delta.\] Stop at the prescribed budget and return the specified posterior recommendation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A noise-aware confidence policy maximizes a posterior upper bound whose width is calibrated using uncertainty after conditioning on noisy feedback.
knowledge_statements.title: Noise-Aware Confidence Policies

children.title: Noise-Aware Posterior-Sampling Policies

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Function-level posterior sampling with a common measurable optimizer selector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\tau\) be a measurable rule selecting one maximizer, or a declared approximate maximizer, from each admissible function. At round \(t\), draw \(\widetilde f_t\sim p(f\mid\mathcal D_{t-1})\), choose \(x_t=\tau(\widetilde f_t)\), observe \(Y_t\) through the stated noise likelihood, and update the posterior. If \(X^\star=\tau(f)\) uses the same selector, then for every measurable \(A\subseteq\mathcal X\), \[\mathbb P(x_t\in A\mid\mathcal D_{t-1})=\mathbb P(X^\star\in A\mid\mathcal D_{t-1}).\] Without a common measurable tie rule, this optimizer-distribution identity is not well-defined when maximizers are nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Posterior sampling draws a latent objective from the noise-aware posterior and evaluates its measurably selected optimizer, thereby matching the posterior optimizer distribution.
assumptions_latex: The posterior incorporates the observation-noise likelihood.
The function and action spaces support the stated conditional distribution and measurable selector.
The same tie or approximation rule defines sampled and posterior optimizers.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Function-level posterior sampling for maximization under an explicitly modeled noisy likelihood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a prior on \(f\) and a likelihood for noisy observations. At round \(t\), sample \[\tilde f_t\sim p(f\mid\mathcal D_{t-1}),\] choose \[x_t\in\arg\max_{x\in\mathcal X}\tilde f_t(x),\] observe \(Y_t\sim p(\,\cdot\mid f(x_t))\), and update \(p(f\mid\mathcal D_t)\) using \(\mathcal D_t=\mathcal D_{t-1}\cup\{(x_t,Y_t)\}\). After a fixed budget, output the prescribed posterior recommendation. For any measurable \(A\subseteq\mathcal X\), exact maximizer selection satisfies \[\mathbb P(x_t\in A\mid\mathcal D_{t-1})=\mathbb P(\arg\max_x f(x)\in A\mid\mathcal D_{t-1}).\]

children.title: Feedback-Calibration Requirements
children.top_down_role: Calibration conditions supporting confidence-based or randomized policy guarantees.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Calibration needed to transfer confidence-event arguments to policies using noisy adaptive feedback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\) contain the actions and observations available before round \(t\). A noise-aware surrogate is calibrated for a stated policy guarantee when its update uses the conditional observation law given \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\), its candidate set \(\mathcal X_t\) is \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable, and, for the required horizon \(T\), \[\mathbb P\!\left(\forall t\le T,\ \forall x\in\mathcal X_t:\ |f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)|\le c_t s_{t-1}(x)\right)\ge1-\delta.\] The scale \(s_{t-1}\) and width \(c_t\) must reflect the stated noise likelihood or covariance. Pointwise marginal coverage alone does not establish this adaptive simultaneous event.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Guarantee transfer requires likelihood-correct updating and simultaneous coverage over the adaptively used times and candidate points, not merely pointwise intervals.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X_t\), \(\mu_{t-1}\), \(s_{t-1}\), and \(c_t\) are predictable from \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\).
The required conditional observation model and displayed probabilities are well-defined.

notation.meaning: Predictable surrogate center and latent-error scale.

review_flags: Replaces the deferred seed with an explicit horizon- and candidate-set-relative condition; no universal confidence width is asserted.
knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Feedback-Calibration Requirement

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Coverage Does Not Imply Simultaneous Calibration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiple-round counterexample to substituting marginal coverage for an adaptive simultaneous guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E_1,\ldots,E_T\) be independent coverage events with \(\mathbb P(E_t)=1-\alpha\). Then every round has pointwise coverage \(1-\alpha\), but \[\mathbb P\!\left(\bigcap_{t=1}^T E_t\right)=(1-\alpha)^T,\] which can be far below \(1-\alpha\). Thus even nonadaptive pointwise validity does not yield the simultaneous event required by a multi-round guarantee; adaptive selection introduces an additional requirement rather than repairing the failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Individually valid intervals can have rapidly deteriorating joint coverage across rounds, so pointwise validity cannot certify an adaptive policy guarantee.
assumptions_latex: \(T\ge2\) and \(0<\alpha<1\).
The coverage events are independent.
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Coverage Does Not Imply Simultaneous Calibration

assumptions_latex: The data filtration \((\mathcal F_t)_{t\geq0}\) contains all past actions and noisy observations.
The surrogate produces predictable means \(\mu_{t-1}\), scales \(s_{t-1}\), and widths \(c_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A valid feedback calibration controls adaptive prediction errors uniformly over the decisions and times required by the policy guarantee.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly gives feedback-calibration conditions for noisy optimism or posterior sampling.
Requires source relating adaptive coverage, likelihood correctness, and guarantee transfer.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: High-probability adaptive calibration condition for surrogate-based policies receiving noisy feedback.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For confidence level \(1-\delta\), a feedback model is calibrated for a policy when its updates use the conditional law of observations given \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\) and the event \[\mathcal E_\delta=\left\{\forall t\leq T,\ \forall x\in\mathcal X_t:\ |f(x)-\mu_{t-1}(x)|\leq c_t s_{t-1}(x)\right\}\] satisfies \(\mathbb P(\mathcal E_\delta)\geq1-\delta\). Here each candidate set \(\mathcal X_t\) and each selected action must be \(\mathcal F_{t-1}\)-measurable. The scale must include uncertainty induced by the stated noise covariance or likelihood. A guarantee proved only on \(\mathcal E_\delta\) requires this adaptive, simultaneous coverage rather than merely pointwise marginal intervals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feedback calibration requires noise-aware posterior updates and simultaneous prediction-error coverage along adaptively selected actions, not merely pointwise intervals.
knowledge_statements.title: Feedback-Calibration Requirements

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition content kind fits the requirements leaf, and the record clearly distinguishes simultaneous adaptive coverage from pointwise coverage. An authoritative source is nevertheless required for the claimed guarantee-transfer requirement and for the measurability and likelihood-correctness conditions.

children.title: Noisy Information Search
children.top_down_role: Entropy- and information-seeking policies incorporating observation uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic mutual-information search targeting a posterior-random optimizer or optimal value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given data \(\mathcal D_n\), a posterior-random optimization target \(Z\), and the prospective noisy observation \(Y_x\), define \[\alpha_n(x)=I(Z;Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n)=H(Z\mid\mathcal D_n)-\mathbb E\!\left[H(Z\mid\mathcal D_n,x,Y_x)\mid\mathcal D_n\right].\] Select a maximizer of \(\alpha_n\), observe through the stated likelihood, and update the posterior. Choosing \(Z\) as a measurably selected optimizer gives optimizer-targeted search; choosing \(Z\) as the latent optimum value gives value-targeted search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noisy information search samples where the prospective noisy observation has greatest mutual information with a chosen optimization target.
assumptions_latex: The target and predictive observation possess well-defined finite information quantities.
The predictive law of \(Y_x\) incorporates observation noise.
A measurable acquisition maximizer or approximation rule is specified.
review_flags: Replaces the deferred seed; differential-entropy expressions require the usual finiteness conditions, while mutual information is the primary definition.
knowledge_statements.title: Noisy Targeted Information Search

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information loss from observing a noisy channel of a latent evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Condition on \(\mathcal D_n\). Let \(F_x=f(x)\), and suppose \(Z-F_x-Y_x\) is a conditional Markov chain. Then \[I(Z;Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n)\le I(Z;F_x\mid\mathcal D_n).\] Equality holds exactly when \(I(Z;F_x\mid Y_x,\mathcal D_n)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A noisy observation cannot contain more information about the target than the latent evaluation that generates it.
assumptions_latex: The displayed conditional mutual informations are well-defined.
\(Y_x\) is conditionally independent of \(Z\) given \(F_x\) and \(\mathcal D_n\).
knowledge_statements.title: Observation-Noise Information Contraction

assumptions_latex: The posterior defines a random optimization target \(Z\), such as the latent maximizer or optimal value.
For every candidate \(x\), the noisy predictive observation \(Y_x\) and the required entropies or divergences are well-defined and finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Noisy information search selects evaluations by their expected information about the optimization target, automatically discounting information destroyed by observation noise.

notation.meaning: Random optimization target under the posterior.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports entropy-based noisy Bayesian optimization.
Requires source for information search targeting an optimizer or optimal value under noisy observations.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic mutual-information policy encompassing optimizer- and optimal-value-targeted noisy information search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given data \(\mathcal D_n\), define the acquisition \[\alpha_n(x)=I(Z;Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n)=H(Z\mid\mathcal D_n)-\mathbb E_{Y_x\mid\mathcal D_n}\!\left[H(Z\mid\mathcal D_n,x,Y_x)\right].\] Initialize a posterior over the latent objective and the target \(Z\). At round \(n+1\), choose \(x_{n+1}\in\arg\max_{x\in\mathcal X}\alpha_n(x)\), observe \(Y_{x_{n+1}}\) through the stated noise model, and update the posterior. Continue until the evaluation budget is exhausted, then report a posterior decision for \(Z\). The likelihood of \(Y_x\) must include observation uncertainty when computing both predictive and conditional entropies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noisy information search evaluates where a noisy observation is expected to reduce posterior uncertainty about the optimizer or optimal value most.
knowledge_statements.title: Noisy Information Search

children.title: Fixed Replication Designs
children.top_down_role: Predetermined replication structures supporting noise estimation and stable inference.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed Replication Designs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predetermined equal or unequal replication at a fixed set of design sites.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given sites \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\in\mathcal X\), predetermined integers \(r_i\ge 2\), and budget \(N=\sum_{i=1}^m r_i\), observe \(Y_{ij}=f(x_i)+\varepsilon_{ij}\) for \(j=1,\ldots,r_i\). Compute \(\bar Y_i=r_i^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{r_i}Y_{ij}\) and \(S_i^2=(r_i-1)^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{r_i}(Y_{ij}-\bar Y_i)^2\). The sites and replication counts are fixed before any response is observed. Return \(\{(x_i,\bar Y_i,S_i^2,r_i)\}_{i=1}^m\) for surrogate inference or selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose all sites and replication counts in advance, then return each site's sample mean, sample variance, and replication count.
assumptions_latex: For each \(i\), the errors \(\varepsilon_{i1},\ldots,\varepsilon_{ir_i}\) are conditionally independent and identically distributed given \(x_i\).
For each \(i\), \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_{ij}\mid x_i]=0\) and \(\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_{ij}\mid x_i)=\sigma_i^2<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(i\), \(\mathbb E[\bar Y_i\mid x_i]=f(x_i)\) and \(\mathbb E[S_i^2\mid x_i]=\sigma_i^2\).

notation.meaning: predetermined number of observations at site i
conditional observation-noise variance at site i

source_refs.source_title: Simulation-Based Optimization: Parametric Optimization Techniques and Reinforcement Learning

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of inverse-count precision under correlated replications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If site-i errors have variance \(\sigma_i^2\) and common pairwise correlation \(\rho_i\), then \[\operatorname{Var}(\bar Y_i)=\sigma_i^2\left(\rho_i+\frac{1-\rho_i}{r_i}\right).\] Thus the usual \(\sigma_i^2/r_i\) law requires \(\rho_i=0\); for fixed \(\rho_i>0\), averaging has variance floor \(\rho_i\sigma_i^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive within-site correlation creates a nonvanishing variance floor for a fixed replication design.
assumptions_latex: Errors at the site are exchangeable with common variance and pairwise correlation.
The exchangeable covariance matrix is positive semidefinite.
knowledge_statements.title: Dependence Boundary for Replicate Means

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle unequal allocation for a separable precision objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(w_i,\sigma_i>0\), the unique minimizer over real \(r_i>0\) with \(\sum_i r_i=N\) of \[\sum_{i=1}^m\frac{w_i\sigma_i^2}{r_i}\] is \[r_i^*=N\frac{\sigma_i\sqrt{w_i}}{\sum_j\sigma_j\sqrt{w_j}},\] with minimum \(N^{-1}(\sum_i\sigma_i\sqrt{w_i})^2\). Integer or minimum-count restrictions require a separate feasible discrete allocation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For weighted site-mean variance, the continuous oracle allocation is proportional to noise standard deviation times square-root weight.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation permits positive real counts.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Optimal Fixed Replication Allocation

children.title: Adaptive Replication Allocation
children.top_down_role: Sequential allocation of repeated observations using current uncertainty or decision value.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Replication Allocation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequential replication driven by a measurable uncertainty or decision-value score.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with at least one observation at each site in a finite set \(C\subset\mathcal X\). At stage \(t\), form the data filtration \(\mathcal F_t\) and compute an \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable replication score \(a_t(x)\) for every \(x\in C\), such as posterior variance reduction or expected decision-value gain. Select \(x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in C}a_t(x)\), obtain an independent response there, and update the posterior and noise estimates. Stop at budget \(N\) and return the prescribed posterior recommendation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly allocate the next observation to the current site with greatest measurable replication value, updating inference after every response.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite and every score \(a_t(x)\) is measurable with respect to \(\mathcal F_t\).
Conditional on its selected site, the new observation follows the stated noise model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{x\in C}n_N(x)=N\), with allocations determined sequentially from observed information.

notation.meaning: current value of another replication at x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Score-based fixed-site replication with nonstarving forced sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) be finite and assign each \(x\in C\) an infinite set of forced stages \(S_x\subset\mathbb N\), with the sets pairwise disjoint. At stage \(t\in S_x\), sample \(x\); at every other stage, choose a maximizer of the measurable score \(a_t\). Then \(n_T(x)\ge |S_x\cap\{1,\ldots,T\}|\to\infty\) for every \(x\in C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reserve infinitely many stages for every site and use the adaptive score at all remaining stages; no site can then be starved.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite.
Each \(S_x\) is infinite and the forced-stage sets are pairwise disjoint.
Nonforced choices are measurable with respect to the current information.

notation.meaning: forced sampling stages for site x
observations allocated to x through stage T

knowledge_statements.title: Forced-Schedule Adaptive Replication

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of unrestricted greedy allocation on a fixed candidate set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(C=\{x_1,x_2\}\), let \(a_t(x_1)=1\) and \(a_t(x_2)=0\) at every stage. Every greedy maximizer samples \(x_1\), so \(n_T(x_2)\) remains bounded. Thus score greediness alone does not imply infinite sampling of every site.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A greedy score can permanently starve a site unless the score itself or an explicit schedule forces revisits.
assumptions_latex: The rule always maximizes the current score and has no forced-sampling condition.

children.title: Explore-versus-Replicate Decisions
children.top_down_role: Decision-theoretic comparison between new locations and variance reduction at existing locations.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

knowledge_statements.title: Explore-versus-Replicate Decisions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step decision rule comparing a new site with another observation at an existing site.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At stage \(t\), let \(D_t\) be the observed data and \(C_t\) the distinct sampled sites. For each action \(u\) in \(\mathcal A_t=\{\operatorname{new}(x):x\in\mathcal X\}\cup\{\operatorname{rep}(x):x\in C_t\}\), define \(V_t(u)=\mathbb E[U(D_t\cup\{Y_u\})-U(D_t)\mid D_t,u]-c(u)\). Choose any \(u_t\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{u\in\mathcal A_t}V_t(u)\), observe \(Y_{u_t}\), and update \(D_{t+1}\). Thus exploration and replication are compared in the same posterior-utility units.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose between a new location and an existing location by maximizing expected posterior utility gain minus evaluation cost.
assumptions_latex: The conditional predictive law of \(Y_u\) given \(D_t\) is defined for every admissible action.
The expected utility increments exist, and an action maximizing \(V_t\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u_t\) has maximal one-step net expected value among the admissible exploration and replication actions.

notation.meaning: terminal or information utility of data D

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limit of one-step exploration-versus-replication comparisons.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With at least two evaluations remaining, maximizing the one-step value \(V_t(u)\) need not maximize expected terminal utility: an action with smaller immediate gain can reveal information that changes the profitable next action. Equivalence requires a one-step horizon or additional structure establishing greedy optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The greatest immediate exploration-or-replication value need not identify the best first action over a multistep horizon.
assumptions_latex: At least two evaluations remain.
Later actions may depend on the current observation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\arg\max_u V_t(u)\) need not maximize multistep expected terminal utility.

notation.meaning: one-step net value of action u

knowledge_statements.title: Myopic Action-Value Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-observation variance reduction for either a new site or a replicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given latent posterior covariance \(k_t\) and independent observation noise variance \(\tau^2(x)>0\), observing \(x\) changes the marginal variance at \(z\) to \[k_{t+1}(z,z)=k_t(z,z)-\frac{k_t(z,x)^2}{k_t(x,x)+\tau^2(x)}.\] Hence \[\Delta_t(x)=\int\frac{k_t(z,x)^2}{k_t(x,x)+\tau^2(x)}\,\mu(dz)\] is the integrated variance reduction, with the same formula for new and previously sampled \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: New-site and replicate actions can be compared through the same exact GP variance-reduction formula.
assumptions_latex: The conditional surrogate is Gaussian with covariance \(k_t\).
The new noise is independent Gaussian with known positive variance.
The integral is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_t(x)\ge0\) is the exact one-step integrated posterior-variance reduction.

notation.meaning: integrated variance reduction from observing x

knowledge_statements.title: Unified Gaussian-Process Variance-Reduction Score

children.title: Replicate-Aware Inference
children.top_down_role: Exact computational reductions and sufficient summaries for repeated input locations.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dense linear-algebra savings from exact Gaussian aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N=\sum_i r_i\) and let \(m\) be the number of distinct sites. When exact Gaussian reduction applies, forming summaries costs \(O(N)\), while dense GP factorization uses an \(m\times m\) system and costs \(O(m^3)\) time and \(O(m^2)\) storage, rather than \(O(N^3)\) and \(O(N^2)\) for the unaggregated dense system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact aggregation changes dense GP linear algebra from total-observation dimension N to distinct-site dimension m.
assumptions_latex: The exact Gaussian replicate reduction is valid.
Dense unstructured factorization is used.
knowledge_statements.title: Distinct-Site Gaussian-Process Reduction Complexity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of mean-and-count reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Means and counts are not universally sufficient. With independent Gaussian noise and unknown \(\tau_i^2\), replicated datasets can share \((r_i,\bar Y_i)\) but have different \(Q_i\), hence different variance likelihoods. More general dependence or non-Gaussian models may require still richer summaries; sufficiency must be established for the declared likelihood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mean-and-count aggregation is exact only under its declared noise model; unknown Gaussian variances already require within-site variation.
assumptions_latex: At least one noise parameter or dependence feature is not fixed by the mean-only reduced model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((r_i,\bar Y_i)_i\) is not a universally sufficient replicate summary.

notation.meaning: within-site residual sum of squares omitted by mean-and-count aggregation

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregation Sufficiency Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient summaries with unknown sitewise Gaussian variances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Y_{ij}\mid f_i,\tau_i^2\overset{\mathrm{ind}}\sim N(f_i,\tau_i^2)\), let \(\bar Y_i=r_i^{-1}\sum_jY_{ij}\) and \(Q_i=\sum_j(Y_{ij}-\bar Y_i)^2\). Since \[\sum_j(Y_{ij}-f_i)^2=Q_i+r_i(\bar Y_i-f_i)^2,\] the likelihood depends on the data only through \((r_i,\bar Y_i,Q_i)_{i=1}^m\), which are sufficient for the site values and variances under this model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Counts, means, and within-site sums of squares preserve the independent Gaussian likelihood when variances are unknown.
assumptions_latex: Conditional on \((f_i,\tau_i^2)\), observations are mutually independent Gaussian variables.
Each \(\tau_i^2>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Gaussian Replicate Likelihood Factorization
Replicate-Aware Inference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Gaussian reduction of replicated observations to site means and counts when noise variances are known.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\sim\operatorname{GP}(m,k)\), and at distinct sites \(x_i\) observe \(Y_{ij}=f(x_i)+\varepsilon_{ij}\), where \(\varepsilon_{ij}\) are independent \(N(0,\tau_i^2)\). Conditional on the site means \(\bar Y_i\), the posterior distribution of \(f\) equals that obtained from the reduced model \(\bar Y_i=f(x_i)+\bar\varepsilon_i\), with independent \(\bar\varepsilon_i\sim N(0,\tau_i^2/r_i)\). The within-site residuals are conditionally independent of \(f\), so posterior prediction requires only distinct sites, means, counts, and known noise variances.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Gaussian noise, replicated GP observations reduce exactly to site means with noise variance divided by replication count.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) has a Gaussian-process prior with mean \(m\) and covariance kernel \(k\).
Observation errors are mutually independent Gaussian variables with known sitewise variances \(\tau_i^2>0\).

notation.meaning: replication count at distinct site i
mean of the replicated responses at site i
known observation-noise variance at site i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact replicate-reduction representation is mathematically plausible under the stated known Gaussian-noise model, but no inspectable source is supplied for the sufficiency and posterior-equivalence claim.

children.title: Observation-Based Incumbents
children.top_down_role: Incumbents ranked directly from noisy observed outcomes.

knowledge_statements.title: Observation-Based Incumbents
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization incumbent defined directly from noisy empirical outcomes at sampled sites.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For distinct sampled sites \(C_t\subset\mathcal X\), let \(n_t(x)\ge1\) and \(\bar Y_t(x)=n_t(x)^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{n_t(x)}Y_j(x)\). An observation-based incumbent is any measurable tie-broken choice \(\hat x_t^{\mathrm{obs}}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C_t}\bar Y_t(x)\). Its reported observed value is \(\hat v_t^{\mathrm{obs}}=\bar Y_t(\hat x_t^{\mathrm{obs}})\). This definition ranks empirical responses and does not identify the reported value with the unknown latent objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The observation-based incumbent is the sampled site having the smallest noisy sample mean, with a specified tie rule.
assumptions_latex: The objective is minimized and \(C_t\) is finite and nonempty.
Every \(x\in C_t\) has at least one finite observed response.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar Y_t(\hat x_t^{\mathrm{obs}})\le\bar Y_t(x)\) for every \(x\in C_t\).

notation.meaning: distinct sites sampled by time t

source_witnesses.source_title: Simulation-Based Optimization: Parametric Optimization Techniques and Reinforcement Learning

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of latent-value consistency when observation-based ranking retains nonvanishing noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two minimization alternatives with \(f(x_1)=0<f(x_2)=\Delta\) and independent sample means \(\bar Y_i\sim N(f(x_i),\sigma^2/q)\), where \(q<\infty\) is fixed. Then the observation-based incumbent selects \(x_2\) with probability \(\Phi(-\Delta\sqrt{q/(2\sigma^2)})>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed replication leaves a positive probability that noise makes the inferior alternative the empirical winner.
assumptions_latex: \(\Delta>0\), \(\sigma^2>0\), and \(q<\infty\).
The two sample means are independent Gaussian averages.
knowledge_statements.title: Persistent Misranking Under Fixed Replication

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Winner's-Curse Bias of an Observation-Based Incumbent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimism caused by minimizing noisy empirical responses over sampled sites.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar Y_i=f_i+\varepsilon_i\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\), with integrable \(\mathbb E\varepsilon_i=0\), and let \(\hat i\in\operatorname*{argmin}_i\bar Y_i\). Then \(\mathbb E[\bar Y_{\hat i}-f_{\hat i}]\le0\). If all \(f_i\) are equal and the errors are i.i.d. with a nondegenerate continuous distribution, then for \(m\ge2\), \(\mathbb E[\bar Y_{\hat i}-f_{\hat i}]=\mathbb E[\min_i\varepsilon_i]<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The reported empirical value of the selected winner is optimistically biased even when every candidate estimate is individually unbiased.
assumptions_latex: The candidate set is finite and nonempty.
All observation errors are integrable and marginally mean zero.
Strict negativity uses equal latent values and at least two i.i.d. nondegenerate continuous errors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\bar Y_{\hat i}-f_{\hat i}]\le0\), with strict inequality under the stated equal-value case.

notation.meaning: latent objective value of candidate i
empirical observation error for candidate i

children.title: Latent Posterior Incumbents

knowledge_statements.title: Latent Posterior Incumbents
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization incumbent based on the posterior mean of the latent objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given data \(D_t\), a candidate set \(C_t\subseteq\mathcal X\), and an integrable latent objective \(f\), define \(\mu_t(x)=\mathbb E[f(x)\mid D_t]\). A latent posterior incumbent is any measurable tie-broken choice \(\hat x_t^{\mathrm{lat}}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C_t}\mu_t(x)\). Unlike an observation-based incumbent, this choice ranks posterior summaries of noise-free values; \(C_t\) may be restricted to sampled sites or may equal the full decision domain when the minimum exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The latent posterior incumbent minimizes the posterior mean of the noise-free objective over a declared candidate set.
assumptions_latex: The objective is minimized and \(\mathbb E[|f(x)|\mid D_t]<\infty\) for each \(x\in C_t\).
The posterior-mean minimum on \(C_t\) is attained.

notation.meaning: posterior mean of the latent objective at x

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Posterior Mean and Probability of Optimality Can Disagree
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-candidate separation of posterior-mean incumbency from modal optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimization over \(C=\{a,b\}\), with posterior distribution \(f(b)=0\) almost surely and \[f(a)=\begin{cases}-10,&\text{with probability }0.1,\\1,&\text{with probability }0.9.\end{cases}\] Then \(\mathbb E[f(a)]=-0.1<0=\mathbb E[f(b)]\), so the posterior-mean incumbent is \(a\). However, \(\mathbb P(f(a)<f(b))=0.1\) and \(\mathbb P(f(b)<f(a))=0.9\), so the candidate most likely to be optimal is \(b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The candidate with the best posterior mean need not have the greatest posterior probability of being optimal.
assumptions_latex: The objective is minimized.
Ties have posterior probability zero in the displayed example.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Posterior-Mean Incumbent as a Bayes Action
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision-theoretic characterization under expected latent-value or simple-regret loss on the declared candidate set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given data \(D_t\), candidate set \(C_t\), and terminal loss \(L(x,f)=f(x)\), the posterior risk is \[\rho_t(x)=\mathbb E[L(x,f)\mid D_t]=\mathbb E[f(x)\mid D_t]=\mu_t(x).\] Hence every \(\hat x_t\in\arg\min_{x\in C_t}\mu_t(x)\) is a Bayes action. The same minimizers result for simple-regret loss \(f(x)-\min_{z\in C_t}f(z)\), because the subtracted term is independent of the selected \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing posterior mean latent value is the Bayes decision for expected latent value and for simple regret over the same candidate set.
assumptions_latex: The relevant posterior expectations are finite.
The posterior-risk minimum on \(C_t\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\hat x_t\in\arg\min_{x\in C_t}\mathbb E[f(x)\mid D_t]\) minimizes posterior expected latent-value and candidate-set simple-regret loss.

notation.meaning: Declared candidate set for the recommendation.

children.title: Risk-Aware Recommendations
children.top_down_role: Recommendations selected using posterior risk or conservative value summaries.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Terminal minimization using a declared posterior risk or conservative value score.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given data \(D_t\), a nonempty candidate set \(C_t\), and a declared finite posterior score \(R_t(x)\), a risk-aware recommendation is a measurably tie-broken choice \(\hat x_t^R\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C_t}R_t(x)\). A posterior-risk formulation sets \(R_t(x)=\rho(f(x)\mid D_t)\) for a specified risk functional \(\rho\). For a Gaussian posterior, the upper posterior quantile is \(R_t(x)=\mu_t(x)+z_{1-\alpha}s_t(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A risk-aware recommendation minimizes a declared posterior risk score; under a Gaussian posterior, a mean-plus-quantile-multiple-of-standard-deviation score is an upper posterior quantile.
assumptions_latex: The minimization orientation, candidate set, posterior quantity, and risk convention are declared.
\(R_t(x)\) is finite and its minimum over \(C_t\) is attained.
The quantile identity requires a Gaussian posterior marginal and the corresponding normal quantile.

notation.meaning: declared posterior risk or conservative score
posterior standard deviation of the latent value

knowledge_statements.title: Posterior-Risk Recommendation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary on interpreting mean-plus-standard-deviation scores as posterior guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a non-Gaussian posterior distribution, \(\mu_t(x)+\beta s_t(x)\) is not generally its \((1-\alpha)\)-quantile and need not satisfy \(\mathbb P(f(x)\le\mu_t(x)+\beta s_t(x)\mid D_t)\ge1-\alpha\) without an additional distributional or moment inequality linking \(\beta\) and \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mean plus a standard-deviation multiple is not automatically a credible upper bound outside an explicitly calibrated distributional or moment regime.
assumptions_latex: The posterior has finite mean and variance.
No Gaussianity or calibrated one-sided concentration inequality is assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mu_t(x)+\beta s_t(x)\) has no distribution-free posterior-quantile interpretation for arbitrary fixed \(\alpha,\beta\).
knowledge_statements.title: Conservative-Score Interpretation Boundary
Risk-Aware Recommendations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior recommendation obtained by minimizing a declared risk functional or conservative credible bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given data \(D_t\), candidate set \(C_t\), and a law-invariant posterior risk functional \(\rho_t\), define a risk-aware recommendation by \(\hat x_t^\rho\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C_t}\rho_t(f(x)\mid D_t)\), using a fixed measurable tie rule. For example, with posterior mean \(\mu_t(x)\), standard deviation \(s_t(x)\), and \(\beta>0\), the conservative upper-risk rule for minimization uses \(\rho_t(f(x)\mid D_t)=\mu_t(x)+\beta s_t(x)\). The risk convention and candidate set are part of the recommendation semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A risk-aware recommendation minimizes a specified posterior risk, such as posterior mean plus a multiple of posterior standard deviation.
assumptions_latex: The posterior risk \(\rho_t(f(x)\mid D_t)\) is finite for each candidate.
The minimum over the nonempty set \(C_t\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho_t(f(\hat x_t^\rho)\mid D_t)\le\rho_t(f(x)\mid D_t)\) for all \(x\in C_t\).

notation.meaning: posterior standard deviation of the latent value

children.title: Candidate Selection After Search

knowledge_statements.title: Candidate Selection After Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Final selection from a finite shortlist produced by adaptive noisy search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After the search stops, freeze a finite nonempty shortlist \(C\subset\mathcal X\). Using a declared score \(T(x;D)\), computed from the available search data or independent validation data \(D\), select \(\hat x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}T(x;D)\) with a prespecified tie rule. Typical scores are a validation sample mean, a posterior latent mean, or a posterior risk. Return \((\hat x,T(\hat x;D),C)\), together with the score definition and whether \(D\) was reused or independently collected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Freeze the search-generated shortlist, rank it by a prespecified final score, and report the winner plus the data-reuse convention.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite and nonempty after search termination.
The score \(T(x;D)\) is finite for every \(x\in C\).

children.title: Confirmation Replication
children.top_down_role: Additional evaluation directed at shortlisted candidates.

knowledge_statements.title: Confirmation Replication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent post-search replication of a frozen shortlist for final comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Freeze a shortlist \(C=\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}\) before confirmation. Choose integers \(q_i\ge1\), then collect fresh responses \(Z_{ij}=f(x_i)+\eta_{ij}\), independent of all search data and of candidate construction. Compute \(\bar Z_i=q_i^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^{q_i}Z_{ij}\) and select \(\hat x_{\mathrm{conf}}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{1\le i\le m}\bar Z_i\), using a prespecified tie rule. Return the winner, confirmation means, replication counts, and uncertainty intervals computed solely from the confirmation sample.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After freezing the shortlist, collect independent fresh replications and select the candidate with the smallest confirmation mean.
assumptions_latex: The shortlist and confirmation replication counts are fixed before confirmation responses are observed.
Confirmation errors are independent of the adaptive-search data and have finite variances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar Z(\hat x_{\mathrm{conf}})\le\bar Z(x)\) for every \(x\in C\).

children.title: Selection-Bias Control
children.top_down_role: Control of optimistic bias induced by adaptive search and winner selection.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Pointwise Coverage Does Not Survive Winner Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian failure of unadjusted marginal intervals for a same-data winner.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y_1,\ldots,Y_m\stackrel{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}N(0,1)\), let \(\hat i\in\operatorname*{argmin}_iY_i\), and use \(I_i=[Y_i-z_{1-\alpha/2},Y_i+z_{1-\alpha/2}]\). Although \(\mathbb P(0\in I_i)=1-\alpha\) for each fixed \(i\), \(\mathbb P(0\in I_{\hat i})=\mathbb P(-z_{1-\alpha/2}\le\min_iY_i\le z_{1-\alpha/2})\to0\) as \(m\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Marginally valid intervals can lose coverage when the reported candidate is selected as the winner from the same data.
assumptions_latex: The observations are independent standard normal variables.
The winner and its interval use the same observations.
\(m\ge2\) and \(0<\alpha<1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Pointwise Coverage Does Not Survive Winner Selection

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Conditional Validation Transfers Through an Adaptive Shortlist
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sample-splitting validity for an adaptively generated finite shortlist.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let search data \(D\) generate a finite measurable shortlist \(C(D)\). Conditional on \(D\), let fresh validation data produce intervals \(I_x\) satisfying \(\mathbb P(\forall x\in C(D):f(x)\in I_x\mid D)\ge1-\alpha\) almost surely. Then \(\mathbb P(\forall x\in C(D):f(x)\in I_x)\ge1-\alpha\). Every certificate whose falsity is excluded on this simultaneous-coverage event consequently has unconditional false-certificate probability at most \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform conditional validity on each realized adaptive shortlist implies unconditional validity after averaging over the search data.
assumptions_latex: \(C(D)\) is finite and measurable with respect to the search data.
The validation procedure has simultaneous conditional coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) for almost every realized search history.
Fresh validation randomness has the conditional law used to calibrate the procedure.
knowledge_statements.title: Conditional Validation Transfers Through an Adaptive Shortlist
Selection-Bias Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional validity obtained by separating adaptive candidate construction from independent confirmation data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the adaptive search data \(D\) generate a finite shortlist \(C(D)\). Conditional on \(D\), collect confirmation data \(Z\) independently and construct simultaneous intervals \(I_x(Z)\) satisfying \(\mathbb P(\forall x\in C(D):f(x)\in I_x(Z)\mid D)\ge1-\alpha\). Then the same simultaneous coverage holds unconditionally. Consequently, any ranking or selection certificate derived solely from the joint interval event retains error probability at most \(\alpha\), despite adaptive construction of \(C(D)\). Reusing \(D\) without selective adjustment does not receive this conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent confirmation preserves simultaneous coverage for an adaptively generated shortlist and thereby controls winner-selection optimism.
assumptions_latex: The shortlist \(C(D)\) is finite and measurable with respect to the search data.
Conditional simultaneous coverage is at least \(1-\alpha\) using confirmation data independent of the search.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional-to-unconditional coverage property is mathematically standard, but its selective-inference and independent-confirmation interpretation is a nontrivial claim with no cited source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Claim that selection adjustment or independent validation exhausts post-selection validity routes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a search-data-measurable shortlist and winner, a nominal post-search error guarantee is justified only if calibration accounts for the entire adaptive selection event or uses fresh conditionally independent validation data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposed record claims that selection-aware inference and independent validation are the only valid routes after selection.
assumptions_latex: The reported guarantee concerns a data-dependent shortlist or winner.
knowledge_statements.title: Valid Routes for Post-Selection Inference

intermediate_metadata.reason: The accepted inventory contains the random-shortlist sample-splitting theorem and the sharp same-data marginal-coverage counterexample. The proposed exhaustive two-route principle is deferred as overstated. Confirmation mechanics and ranking or selection inequalities remain in sibling scopes.

children.title: Ranking Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Post-search guarantees concerning the ordering of candidate alternatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Ranking Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous-confidence certificate for a complete ranking of finitely many candidates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For candidates \(x_1,\ldots,x_m\), suppose intervals \(I_i=[L_i,U_i]\) satisfy \(\mathbb P(\forall i:f(x_i)\in I_i)\ge1-\alpha\). A permutation \(\pi\) is a certified increasing ranking for minimization when \(U_{\pi(j)}<L_{\pi(j+1)}\) for every \(j=1,\ldots,m-1\). On the simultaneous-coverage event, these inequalities imply \(f(x_{\pi(1)})<\cdots<f(x_{\pi(m)})\). Therefore the displayed interval separation is a verifiable ranking certificate whose probability of certifying an incorrect complete ranking is at most \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise separation of simultaneous confidence intervals certifies the full candidate ranking with error probability at most alpha.
assumptions_latex: The candidate set is finite.
The intervals have joint coverage at least \(1-\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(\text{a certified permutation is incorrectly ordered})\le\alpha\).

notation.meaning: simultaneous confidence interval for candidate i

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certified Partial Order from Simultaneous Intervals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ranking certificate when only some candidate pairs are separated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\mathbb P(\forall i:f(x_i)\in[L_i,U_i])\ge1-\alpha\). For minimization, declare \(x_i\prec x_j\) whenever \(U_i<L_j\), and take the transitive closure. On the simultaneous-coverage event every declared relation satisfies \(f(x_i)<f(x_j)\). Thus the probability that the certified partial order contains any false comparison is at most \(\alpha\); overlapping intervals leave the corresponding order unresolved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneous intervals certify all separated candidate pairs without forcing an unsupported complete ranking.
assumptions_latex: The candidate set is finite.
The intervals jointly cover all candidate values with probability at least \(1-\alpha\).

notation.meaning: certified strict preference relation for minimization
