children.title: Selection Guarantees
children.top_down_role: Post-search guarantees concerning the reported candidate.

knowledge_statements.title: Selection Guarantees
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous-confidence certificate that a selected candidate is optimal or within a declared tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite candidate set \(C\), suppose simultaneous intervals \(I_x=[L_x,U_x]\) satisfy \(\mathbb P(\forall x\in C:f(x)\in I_x)\ge1-\alpha\). A selected candidate \(\hat x\in C\) is certified \(\varepsilon\)-optimal for minimization if \(U_{\hat x}\le\min_{x\in C}L_x+\varepsilon\). On the joint-coverage event, \(f(\hat x)-\min_{x\in C}f(x)\le\varepsilon\). When \(C\setminus\{\hat x\}\) is nonempty, the strict separation \(U_{\hat x}<\min_{x\in C\setminus\{\hat x\}}L_x\) instead certifies that \(\hat x\) is the unique minimizer. Either displayed interval condition is directly checkable, and the probability of issuing a false corresponding certificate is at most \(\alpha\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneous intervals certify epsilon-optimality when the selected candidate's upper bound is within epsilon of the smallest lower bound; strict separation from every competitor certifies exact selection.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite and nonempty.
The intervals jointly cover all candidate values with probability at least \(1-\alpha\).
The tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb P(f(\hat x)-\min_{x\in C}f(x)>\varepsilon\ \text{and the epsilon-optimality certificate holds})\le\alpha\).

notation.meaning: simultaneous interval for the latent value at x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical fixed-set selection guarantee under a declared minimum meaningful gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C=\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}\) have a unique minimizer \(x_*\), and fix \(\delta>0\). A selection procedure has probability of correct selection at least \(1-\alpha\) over the preference zone if, for every admissible mean vector satisfying \(\min_{i\ne *}[f(x_i)-f(x_*)]\ge\delta\), it obeys \(\mathbb P(\hat x=x_*)\ge1-\alpha\). This guarantee imposes no exact-selection requirement when the best-versus-second-best gap is below \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An indifference-zone guarantee controls correct selection uniformly when the true best candidate is separated from every competitor by at least a declared gap.
assumptions_latex: The candidate set is finite and has a unique minimizer.
The probability statement is calibrated uniformly over the declared data-generating family.
\(\delta>0\) and \(0<\alpha<1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Indifference-Zone Probability-of-Correct-Selection Guarantee

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Shortlist-Relative Scope of a Selection Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating selection within a finite candidate set from global optimization certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a certificate establishes \(f(\hat x)-\min_{x\in C}f(x)\le\varepsilon\) for a finite \(C\subseteq\mathcal X\), no bound on \(f(\hat x)-\inf_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)\) follows without additional control of \(\min_{x\in C}f(x)-\inf_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)\). If the latter gap is at most \(\gamma\) on the same event, then the global gap is at most \(\varepsilon+\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-shortlist selection certificate is not a global-optimality certificate unless the shortlist's coverage of the domain is also controlled.
assumptions_latex: \(\hat x\in C\subseteq\mathcal X\), with \(C\) finite and nonempty.
The shortlist certificate and shortlist-to-domain bound hold on the same event.
knowledge_statements.title: Shortlist-Relative Scope of a Selection Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between certification over a frozen shortlist and certification over the full optimization domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A validation certificate for \(\hat x_T\) relative to \(C_T\) does not alone bound \(f(\hat x_T)-\inf_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)\). If it certifies \(f(\hat x_T)-\min_{x\in C_T}f(x)\le\varepsilon\) and an additional search guarantee supplies \(\min_{x\in C_T}f(x)-\inf_{x\in\mathcal X}f(x)\le\gamma\) on the same event, then the global gap is at most \(\varepsilon+\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Post-search validation certifies the frozen candidate set unless a separate search-coverage guarantee connects that set to the full domain.
assumptions_latex: \(\hat x_T\in C_T\subseteq\mathcal X\).
The shortlist certificate and search-coverage bound hold on the same event.
knowledge_statements.title: Global-Regret Boundary of Finite-Shortlist Validation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface that passes a frozen Bayesian-optimization shortlist to a conditionally valid fixed-set validator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let Bayesian-optimization search data \(D_T\) determine a finite shortlist \(C_T=C(D_T)\) and a recommendation \(\hat x_T\in C_T\). Freeze \((C_T,\hat x_T)\), then apply to fresh validation data a procedure having conditional error probability at most \(\alpha\) for every realized admissible pair \((C_T,\hat x_T)\). The resulting certificate retains unconditional error probability at most \(\alpha\). The Bayesian model may generate the shortlist and recommendation, but the stated frequentist coverage is supplied by the validation procedure and its conditional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Freeze the Bayesian-optimization output and pass it to a fresh-data procedure valid for every realized shortlist; its conditional guarantee transfers unconditionally.
assumptions_latex: \(C_T\) is finite and measurable with respect to the search data, and \(\hat x_T\in C_T\).
The validation data have the conditional law used to calibrate the fixed-set procedure.
For almost every search history, the procedure's conditional false-certificate probability is at most \(\alpha\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given search data \(D_T\), select \(\widehat x_T\) without inspecting \(V\). Using only the independent validation sample \(V\), construct \(U_T\ge 0\) such that, simultaneously for every recommendation measurable with respect to \(D_T\),
\[
\Pr\!\left(f(x^\star)-f(\widehat x_T)>U_T\mid D_T\right)\le\delta.
\]
The pair \((\widehat x_T,U_T)\), together with the declared confidence level \(1-\delta\), is a Bayesian-optimization selection certificate. Its unconditional coverage follows by averaging the conditional inequality over \(D_T\); the Bayesian model may drive the search but is not itself the coverage justification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select the recommendation using search data, then use independent validation data to bound its simple regret with declared frequentist coverage.

children.title: Kernel Approximation Error
children.top_down_role: Guarantee sensitivity to low-rank, sparse, or approximate covariance structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Kernel Approximation Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform kernel error propagated to finite-design Gram matrices and regularized inverses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define
\[
\varepsilon_k=\sup_{x,x'\in\mathcal X}|k(x,x')-\widetilde k(x,x')|.
\]
For every finite design \(X_n=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), the associated Gram matrices satisfy
\[
\|K_n-\widetilde K_n\|_2\le n\varepsilon_k.
\]
For \(A=K_n+\lambda I\) and \(\widetilde A=\widetilde K_n+\lambda I\) with \(\lambda>0\),
\[
\|A^{-1}-\widetilde A^{-1}\|_2\le\frac{n\varepsilon_k}{\lambda^2}.
\]
These quantities isolate kernel-approximation error before feature-computation and numerical-solution errors are included.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform kernel error produces at most an n-fold spectral Gram-matrix error and a regularized inverse error bounded by that perturbation divided by squared regularization.
assumptions_latex: \(k,\widetilde k:\mathcal X\times\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) are symmetric positive-semidefinite kernels.
\(X_n=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\) is a finite design and \(\lambda>0\).

notation.meaning: regularized exact and approximate covariance matrices

assumptions_latex: \(A\) is symmetric positive definite with \(\lambda_{\min}(A)\ge\gamma>0\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral certificate that an approximate covariance remains positive definite.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Weyl's eigenvalue inequality gives \(\lambda_{\min}(\widetilde A)\ge\lambda_{\min}(A)-\|E\|_2\ge\gamma-\eta\). Therefore \(\eta<\gamma\) certifies positive definiteness and \(\|\widetilde A^{-1}\|_2\le1/(\gamma-\eta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An approximate covariance remains positive definite when its spectral error is smaller than a certified lower eigenvalue of the exact covariance.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Definiteness Preservation

assumptions_latex: \(A=[\gamma]\) and \(\widetilde A=[\gamma+\eta]\), where \(\gamma>0\) and \(\eta>0\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditioning boundary for converting kernel error into inverse or posterior error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even in one dimension, \(|A^{-1}-\widetilde A^{-1}|=\eta/[\gamma(\gamma+\eta)]\). Thus small absolute covariance error can have arbitrarily large inverse sensitivity when no positive spectral margin is maintained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near singularity, small covariance errors can be amplified without bound in the inverse, so a positive spectral margin is essential.
knowledge_statements.title: Near-Singularity Amplification

assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(\widetilde A\) are symmetric positive definite with both minimum eigenvalues at least \(\gamma>0\).
\(\|A-\widetilde A\|_2\le\eta\), \(\|k_x-\widetilde k_x\|_2\le\xi_x\), and \(|k(x,x)-\widetilde k(x,x)|\le\zeta_x\).
The observation vector is \(y\).

notation.meaning: exact and approximate zero-mean posterior means

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic propagation of kernel approximation to posterior mean and latent variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(v(x)=k(x,x)-k_x^\top A^{-1}k_x\) and \(\widetilde v(x)=\widetilde k(x,x)-\widetilde k_x^\top\widetilde A^{-1}\widetilde k_x\), \[|\mu(x)-\widetilde\mu(x)|\le\frac{\xi_x\|y\|_2}{\gamma}+\frac{\eta\|\widetilde k_x\|_2\|y\|_2}{\gamma^2},\] and \[|v(x)-\widetilde v(x)|\le\zeta_x+\frac{\xi_x(\|k_x\|_2+\|\widetilde k_x\|_2)}{\gamma}+\frac{\eta\|\widetilde k_x\|_2^2}{\gamma^2}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Kernel, cross-covariance, and covariance-system errors yield explicit posterior mean and variance errors controlled by the inverse spectral margin.

children.title: Feature Approximation Error
children.top_down_role: Guarantee sensitivity to finite or randomized feature representations.

assumptions_latex: \(k:\mathcal X\times\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) is a positive-semidefinite kernel.
\(\phi_m:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^m\) is the feature map used by the approximate posterior.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates finite-feature representation error from subsequent floating-point and linear-solve errors.

source_refs.source_title: Surrogates: Gaussian Process Modeling, Design, and Optimization for the Applied Sciences

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite feature map \(\phi_m\), define its induced kernel by \(k_m(x,x')=\phi_m(x)^\top\phi_m(x')\). The uniform feature approximation error relative to \(k\) is
\[
\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feat}}(m)=\sup_{x,x'\in\mathcal X}|k(x,x')-k_m(x,x')|.
\]
For a specified finite design \(X_n\), the design-restricted alternative is \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feat},X}=\|K_n-\Phi\Phi^\top\|_2\), where \(\Phi_{i:}=\phi_m(x_i)^\top\). The definition attributes only the discrepancy caused by replacing the kernel with finite features; sampling variability in randomized features may make either error a random variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feature approximation error measures the covariance discrepancy created by replacing a kernel with inner products of finitely many features.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximation-Budget Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract monotone resource allocation for kernel or feature approximations; no universal decay rate is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(B\ge0\), define the feasible set
\[
\mathcal M_B=\{m\in\mathbb N:c(m)\le B\}.
\]
If \(\mathcal M_B\) is nonempty and has a largest element, set \(m_B=\max\mathcal M_B\). When \(e(m)\) is nonincreasing, \(m_B\) minimizes \(e(m)\) over \(\mathcal M_B\). Any guarantee using this approximation must retain the certified residual \(e(m_B)\) in its error accounting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the feasible approximation budgets have a largest member and certified error decreases with budget, the largest affordable budget minimizes the certified residual error.
assumptions_latex: For every \(m\in\mathbb N\), the approximation has certified error \(e(m)\) and cost \(c(m)\).
\(e(m)\) is nonincreasing and \(c(m)\) is nondecreasing.

children.title: Posterior-Sampling Approximation Error
children.top_down_role: Validity of randomized policies under approximate posterior function draws.

knowledge_statements.title: Posterior-Sampling Approximation Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step policy distortion for posterior sampling, measured in total variation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_t\sim P_t\) and \(\widetilde F_t\sim Q_t\). For a measurable decision rule \(g_t:\mathcal F\to\mathcal X\), define \(X_{t+1}=g_t(F_t)\) and \(\widetilde X_{t+1}=g_t(\widetilde F_t)\). Then
\[
\|\mathcal L(X_{t+1})-\mathcal L(\widetilde X_{t+1})\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\le\|P_t-Q_t\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\]
For every measurable \(\ell:\mathcal X\to[0,L]\),
\[
|\mathbb E\ell(X_{t+1})-\mathbb E\ell(\widetilde X_{t+1})|
\le L\|P_t-Q_t\|_{\mathrm{TV}}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The action-distribution error of approximate posterior sampling cannot exceed the total variation error between the exact and approximate posterior function laws.
assumptions_latex: \(P_t\) and \(Q_t\) are probability laws on a measurable function space \((\mathcal F,\mathcal A)\).
\((\mathcal X,\mathcal B)\) is a measurable action space.
\(g_t:\mathcal F\to\mathcal X\) is measurable.

notation.meaning: total variation distance defined as the supremum over measurable events

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(M>0\), there exist laws \(P,Q\) with \(\|P-Q\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\varepsilon\) and a nonnegative unbounded loss \(\ell\) such that \(|\mathbb E_P\ell-\mathbb E_Q\ell|>M\). Thus TV control transfers regret only with bounded loss, uniform integrability, or explicit tail control.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of conditional posterior-sampling errors to the adaptive transcript law.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose that after every common history, the conditional exact and approximate posterior function laws at round \(t\) differ in total variation by at most \(\varepsilon_t\). If both policies use the same measurable sampled-function decision map and the same observation kernel, then \(\|\mathcal L(H_T)-\mathcal L(\widetilde H_T)\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\le\min\{1,\sum_{t=1}^T\varepsilon_t\}\). Every terminal loss in \([0,L]\) consequently has expectation distortion at most \(L\min\{1,\sum_{t=1}^T\varepsilon_t\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional posterior-sampling errors accumulate at most additively in the adaptive trajectory law.

knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Linear-Algebra Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-based deterministic certificate for covariance-system solves used in posterior means and variances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(z=A^{-1}b\), a computed solution \(\widehat z\), and residual \(r=b-A\widehat z\), the solve-error certificate is
\[
\|z-\widehat z\|_A=\|r\|_{A^{-1}}
\le\frac{\|r\|_2}{\sqrt{\lambda_{\min}(A)}}.
\]
For every \(k_x\in\mathbb R^n\), the induced error in the posterior bilinear quantity satisfies
\[
|k_x^\top A^{-1}b-k_x^\top\widehat z|
\le\|k_x\|_{A^{-1}}\|r\|_{A^{-1}}.
\]
The residual and a certified lower bound on \(\lambda_{\min}(A)\) therefore provide computable solve-error information. Any stabilization that changes \(A\) is a separate modeling perturbation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A computed residual and a positive lower eigenvalue bound certify linear-solve error and its effect on posterior bilinear quantities.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}\) is symmetric positive definite.
\(b,\widehat z\in\mathbb R^n\), \(z=A^{-1}b\), and \(r=b-A\widehat z\).

notation.meaning: positive-definite system matrix and right-hand side

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The residual of the covariance solve directly certifies its contribution to posterior variance error.

assumptions_latex: \(A\) is symmetric positive definite with condition number \(\kappa=\lambda_{\max}(A)/\lambda_{\min}(A)\).
Conjugate gradients is applied in exact arithmetic from initial iterate \(z_0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical iterative-solve convergence bound for positive-definite covariance systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Conjugate gradients satisfies \[\|z-z_m\|_A\le2q^m\|z-z_0\|_A,\qquad q=\frac{\sqrt\kappa-1}{\sqrt\kappa+1}.\] A sufficient worst-case iteration count for reducing the energy error by a factor \(\tau\in(0,1)\) is \(\lceil\log(2/\tau)/\log(1/q)\rceil=O(\sqrt\kappa\log(1/\tau))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conjugate gradients converges geometrically for positive-definite covariance systems, with worst-case iteration growth proportional to the square root of the condition number.
knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate-Gradient Solve Rate

assumptions_latex: The residual \(r=b-A\widehat z\) is evaluated in a declared arithmetic model.
\(A\), \(b\), and \(\widehat z\) have compatible dimensions, and the denominator below is positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \eta_{\mathrm{bw}}=\frac{\|r\|_2}{\|A\|_2\|\widehat z\|_2+\|b\|_2}\text{ is the normwise relative backward error when compatible relative perturbations of }A\text{ and }b\text{ are allowed}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backward-stability interpretation of a reported linear-system residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The normwise relative backward error is \[\eta_{\mathrm{bw}}=\frac{\|b-A\widehat z\|_2}{\|A\|_2\|\widehat z\|_2+\|b\|_2}.\] A small value certifies exact solution of a nearby system; a forward-error or posterior-error conclusion additionally requires conditioning information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized residual measures backward error, but converting it into solution or posterior error requires a condition or eigenvalue bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Normwise Backward Error

assumptions_latex: The intended covariance system is \(Az=b\).
A stabilized computation instead solves \((A+J)\widetilde z=b\) exactly for a nonzero symmetric perturbation \(J\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates exact solution of a stabilized covariance system from numerical accuracy for the intended system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An exact solve of \((A+J)\widetilde z=b\) has zero residual for the stabilized system but residual \(J\widetilde z\) for the intended system. Jitter, diagonal loading, truncation, or any substitution that changes the solved operator must therefore be recorded as a matrix-model perturbation rather than hidden in a zero solve tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solving a jittered covariance system exactly does not solve the original system exactly, so stabilization bias must be reported separately from solve residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization Is a Separate Perturbation

children.title: Acquisition-Evaluation Error
children.top_down_role: Effects of Monte Carlo, quadrature, and other numerical acquisition approximations.

knowledge_statements.title: Acquisition-Evaluation Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic propagation of uniform Monte Carlo, quadrature, or numerical evaluation error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_t^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}a_t(x)\). Suppose \(\widehat x_t\in\mathcal X\) satisfies
\[
\widehat a_t(\widehat x_t)\ge\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}\widehat a_t(x)-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}.
\]
If
\[
\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}|a_t(x)-\widehat a_t(x)|
\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{eval}},
\]
then
\[
a_t(x_t^\star)-a_t(\widehat x_t)
\le2\varepsilon_{\mathrm{eval}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}.
\]
The same conclusion holds on any event on which the uniform evaluation-error bound is valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform acquisition-evaluation error contributes twice to the exact acquisition gap, in addition to numerical maximization error.
assumptions_latex: \(a_t,\widehat a_t:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\), and \(a_t\) attains its maximum.
\(\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}|a_t(x)-\widehat a_t(x)|\le\varepsilon_{\mathrm{eval}}\).
\(\widehat x_t\) is an additive \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\)-maximizer of \(\widehat a_t\), with \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{eval}},\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\ge0\).

Independence across different candidates is not required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise estimator accuracy does not validate subsequent adaptive maximization.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An estimator can be exact almost surely at every fixed point yet possess a random spurious maximizer, so pointwise guarantees do not validate adaptive acquisition optimization.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(-\varepsilon_-\le\widehat a(x)-a(x)\le\varepsilon_+\) uniformly, then every additive \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\)-maximizer \(\widehat x\) of \(\widehat a\) satisfies \[a(x^\star)-a(\widehat x)\le\varepsilon_-+\varepsilon_++\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}.\] The seed is recovered when \(\varepsilon_- =\varepsilon_+=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{eval}}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An acquisition optimizer is an additive \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\)-maximizer at round \(t\) when its output \(\widehat x_t\in\mathcal X\) satisfies

children.title: Acquisition Discretization Error
children.top_down_role: Approximation effects from finite candidate sets, meshes, or restricted search families.

knowledge_statements.title: Acquisition Discretization Error
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-candidate acquisition loss controlled by covering radius and acquisition regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(S_h\subseteq\mathcal X\) satisfy
\[
\forall x\in\mathcal X\;\exists s\in S_h:\ d(x,s)\le h.
\]
If \(a_t:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) is \(L_t\)-Lipschitz and both displayed suprema are finite, then
\[
0\le\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}a_t(x)-\sup_{s\in S_h}a_t(s)
\le L_t h.
\]
Thus restricting acquisition search to \(S_h\) adds at most \(L_t h\) to the acquisition suboptimality ledger.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Searching an h-net loses at most the acquisition Lipschitz constant times the mesh radius relative to continuous maximization.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal X,d)\) is a metric space and \(S_h\subseteq\mathcal X\) is an \(h\)-net.
\(a_t:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) is \(L_t\)-Lipschitz.
\(\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}a_t(x)\) and \(\sup_{s\in S_h}a_t(s)\) are finite.

notation.meaning: candidate set whose covering radius is at most h
Lipschitz constant of the acquisition function

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(x_0\notin\bigcup_m S_m\) and define \(a(x)=\mathbf 1\{x=x_0\}\). Then \(\sup_{[0,1]}a=1\) but \(\sup_{S_m}a=0\) for every \(m\), even though the covering radii tend to zero.

assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal X,d)\) is a metric space.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General metric discretization bound; the explicit h-net assumption avoids an unjustified nearest-point assumption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an \(h\)-net \(S_h\), \[0\le\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}a(x)-\sup_{s\in S_h}a(s)\le\omega_a(h).\] In particular, if \(|a(x)-a(y)|\le C d(x,y)^\alpha\) for \(0<\alpha\le1\), the loss is at most \(Ch^\alpha\). If \(a\) is uniformly continuous and \(h_m\to0\), then \(\sup_{s\in S_{h_m}}a(s)\to\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}a(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discretization loss is bounded by the acquisition's modulus of continuity at the mesh radius; this yields Holder rates and value consistency for vanishing meshes.

knowledge_statements.title: Acquisition-Error Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive certificate combining acquisition evaluation, discretization, and finite-set optimization errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_t^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{x\in\mathcal X}a_t(x)\), and let \(\widehat x_t\in S_{h_t}\). On an event \(\mathcal E_t\), suppose
\[
\|a_t-\widehat a_t\|_\infty\le E_t,
\qquad
\sup_{s\in S_{h_t}}\widehat a_t(s)-\widehat a_t(\widehat x_t)\le G_t.
\]
If \(S_{h_t}\) is an \(h_t\)-net and \(a_t\) is \(L_t\)-Lipschitz, then on \(\mathcal E_t\),
\[
a_t(x_t^\star)-a_t(\widehat x_t)
\le2E_t+L_t h_t+G_t=:C_t.
\]
The tuple \((E_t,L_t,h_t,G_t,C_t)\), together with a deterministic-validity declaration or a bound for \(\Pr(\mathcal E_t)\), is an acquisition-error certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluation, mesh, and solver-gap bounds combine additively into a checkable certificate for exact acquisition suboptimality.

children.title: Fixed-Budget Reporting

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Budget Reporting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Terminal simple-regret report at a prespecified evaluation horizon; it is not a data-dependent stopping rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) attain its maximum at \(x^\star\), and fix \(T\in\mathbb N\) before observing the data. At time \(T\), output \(\widehat x_T=R(D_T)\) and report
\[
\bigl(T,\widehat x_T,U_T(\delta),1-\delta\bigr).
\]
This is a valid fixed-budget report when
\[
\Pr\!\left(f(x^\star)-f(\widehat x_T)\le U_T(\delta)\right)
\ge1-\delta.
\]
The reported bound must include all approximation, numerical, and validation errors used in its construction. This convention makes no optional-stopping claim because \(T\) is fixed independently of the realized history.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After a predetermined number of evaluations, report the recommendation and a valid confidence bound on its simple regret, including computational errors.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) attains its maximum at some \(x^\star\in\mathcal X\).
The evaluation budget \(T\in\mathbb N\) is fixed before observing the data.
The recommendation \(\widehat x_T=R(D_T)\) is measurable with respect to the history \(D_T\).
For \(\delta\in(0,1)\), the terminal assessment supplies \(U_T(\delta)\ge0\) with the stated simple-regret coverage.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic conversion of fixed-horizon certificates into a time-uniform stopping certificate.

Consequently, \(\tau=\inf\{t:U_t(\alpha_t)\le\varepsilon\}\) is valid whenever finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocate total error probability across horizons; the resulting union-bound certificate remains valid at the first tolerance crossing.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_1,\ldots,B_m\) be disjoint events forming a partition, with \(B_t\in\mathcal F_t\) and \(\Pr(B_t)=1/m=\delta\). Let the horizon-\(t\) statement fail exactly on \(B_t\), and define \(\tau=t\) on \(B_t\). Each deterministic-time statement has coverage \(1-\delta\), but the selected statement fails with probability one.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(\varepsilon>0\) and \(\delta\in(0,1)\). After each evaluation, compute a recommendation \(\widehat x_t\) and an anytime-valid bound \(U_t(\delta)\). Stop at
\[
\tau=\inf\{t\ge1:U_t(\delta)\le\varepsilon\},
\]
with \(\inf\varnothing=\infty\), and output \((\widehat x_\tau,U_\tau(\delta))\) when \(\tau<\infty\). On the simultaneous-coverage event, \(r_\tau\le U_\tau(\delta)\le\varepsilon\); therefore
\[
\Pr\{\tau<\infty\Rightarrow r_\tau\le\varepsilon\}\ge1-\delta.
\]
Pointwise fixed-time bounds alone do not justify this data-dependent stopping rule.

children.title: Posterior-Opportunity Stopping
children.top_down_role: Termination based on the posterior value remaining in further search.

knowledge_statements.title: Posterior-Opportunity Stopping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-step Bayesian stopping certificate based on posterior expected improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For maximization on a compact domain \(X\), let \(b_t\) be the best value accepted after data \(\mathcal D_t\), and define the posterior opportunity \[O_t:=\sup_{x\in X}\mathbb E\!\left[(f(x)-b_t)_+\mid\mathcal D_t\right].\] Given \(\varepsilon>0\), define \(\tau:=\inf\{t:O_t\leq\varepsilon\}\). On the event \(\{\tau<\infty\}\), stop and return the incumbent. Then every single additional evaluation location has posterior expected improvement at most \(\varepsilon\). This is a one-step posterior-opportunity certificate and does not bound the value of an adaptive multistep policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the stopping time is finite, stop when the largest posterior expected one-step improvement is at most the tolerance; this certifies negligible one-step opportunity, not negligible multistep value.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is compact and the displayed conditional expectations are finite.
\(b_t\), \(\mathcal D_t\), and \(O_t\) are measurable with respect to the information available at time \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On \(\{\tau<\infty\}\), \(O_\tau\leq\varepsilon\) and \(\mathbb E[(f(x)-b_\tau)_+\mid\mathcal D_\tau]\leq\varepsilon\) for every \(x\in X\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of pointwise expected improvement to certify a dimension-free posterior latent gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) alternatives have conditionally disjoint positive-improvement events. Each improves over the incumbent by \(M\) with probability \(p\), where \(Kp\le1\), and otherwise has zero improvement. Then \(O_t=pM\), while \(\mathbb E[\max_i I_i\mid\mathcal D_t]=KpM\). Thus small pointwise opportunity gives no dimension-free bound on the combined posterior latent opportunity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Many disjoint rare opportunities can each have tiny expected improvement while their combined posterior value is large.
assumptions_latex: There are \(K\) alternatives with conditionally disjoint positive-improvement events.
Each improvement has size \(M>0\) and probability \(p\), with \(Kp\le1\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain relation between pointwise expected improvement and posterior expected latent opportunity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_K\}\), let \(I_i=(f(x_i)-b_t)_+\). Then \(O_t=\max_i\mathbb E[I_i\mid\mathcal D_t]\) satisfies \(O_t\le\mathbb E[\max_i I_i\mid\mathcal D_t]\le\sum_i\mathbb E[I_i\mid\mathcal D_t]\le K O_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On K alternatives, expected best latent improvement can be as large as K times the largest pointwise expected improvement.
assumptions_latex: \(X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_K\}\) is finite.
Each \(I_i=(f(x_i)-b_t)_+\) is conditionally integrable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: O_t\le\mathbb E[\max_{1\le i\le K}I_i\mid\mathcal D_t]\le K O_t.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact one-dimensional Fourier witness for lengthscale-dependent RKHS exclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(\mathbb R\), let \(k_\ell(x,y)=\exp(-(x-y)^2/(2\ell^2))\) and \(f_a(x)=\exp(-x^2/(2a^2))\), with \(a,\ell>0\). The Fourier characterization of a stationary-kernel RKHS gives \[f_a\in\mathcal H_{k_\ell}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad a^2>\ell^2/2.\] Hence a Gaussian objective feature of width \(a\) is excluded from the squared-exponential RKHS whenever \(\ell\geq\sqrt{2}\,a\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A squared-exponential surrogate whose lengthscale is at least square root of two times a Gaussian bump's width excludes that bump from its RKHS.

knowledge_statements.title: Mean-Level Misspecification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Misspecification caused by fixing an incorrect global mean level.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the surrogate class be \(\mathcal F_0=\{m_0+g:g\in\mathcal H_k,\ \lVert g\rVert_{\mathcal H_k}\leq B\}\), where \(m_0\) is a fixed constant mean. If the truth is \(f=m_0+c+g_0\), then mean-level misspecification relative to this class occurs exactly when \[\lVert c+g_0\rVert_{\mathcal H_k}>B,\] interpreting the norm as \(+\infty\) when the constant-shifted residual is not in \(\mathcal H_k\). In that case, confidence and regret guarantees quantified only over \(\mathcal F_0\) do not cover \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An incorrect fixed mean is guarantee-relevant when the shifted residual lies outside the surrogate’s assumed RKHS ball.
assumptions_latex: \(k\) is positive definite and \(B>0\).
The surrogate mean \(m_0\) is fixed rather than inferred.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\notin\mathcal F_0\) if and only if \(\lVert c+g_0\rVert_{\mathcal H_k}>B\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact shift equivariance obtained by estimating a constant GP mean rather than fixing it.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=K_n+\sigma^2I\succ0\), \(h=\mathbf1_n\), and \(\widehat\beta=(h^\top A^{-1}h)^{-1}h^\top A^{-1}y\). The universal-kriging predictor is \(\mu(x)=\widehat\beta+k_n(x)^\top A^{-1}(y-h\widehat\beta)\). Holding the covariance quantities fixed, replacing \(y\) by \(y'=y+ch\) gives \(\widehat\beta'=\widehat\beta+c\), leaves the fitted residual unchanged, and yields \(\mu'(x)=\mu(x)+c\). Thus the fixed-mean misspecification boundary does not transfer unchanged to a model with an estimated intercept.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With covariance quantities fixed, estimating the GP intercept makes predictions shift by exactly the same constant as all observations; a fixed mean can instead turn that shift into model-class misspecification.

knowledge_statements.title: Trend Misspecification

For a true objective \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), trend misspecification relative to this class occurs when \[\lVert f-m_\theta\rVert_{\mathcal H_k}>B\quad\text{for every }\theta\in\Theta,\] where the norm is assigned \(+\infty\) when \(f-m_\theta\notin\mathcal H_k\). Guarantees uniform only over the displayed mean-plus-residual class then exclude \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trend misspecification occurs when no allowed mean function leaves a residual inside the assumed RKHS ball.

knowledge_statements.title: Extrapolation Bias
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact posterior-mean bias induced by an incorrect prior mean away from observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At design points \(X_n=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\), let observations have covariance matrix \(K_n+\sigma^2I\). If the true mean is \(m_*\) but Gaussian-process prediction uses \(m_0\), then, conditional on \(X_n\), the posterior-mean bias at \(x\) is \[b_n(x)=\delta m(x)-k_n(x)^\top(K_n+\sigma^2I)^{-1}\delta m(X_n),\qquad \delta m:=m_*-m_0.\] Hence bias persists where the kernel-weighted observations cannot reproduce the mean discrepancy, particularly at extrapolation points with \(k_n(x)\) near zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Posterior extrapolation inherits the prior-mean error minus the portion corrected by kernel-weighted observations.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(A=K_n+\sigma^2I\succ0\), the extrapolation-bias identity gives \[|b_n(x)-\delta m(x)|=|k_n(x)^\top A^{-1}\delta m(X_n)|\le \sqrt{k_n(x)^\top A^{-1}k_n(x)}\sqrt{\delta m(X_n)^\top A^{-1}\delta m(X_n)}.\] Thus observations can correct little of the local prior-mean error whenever covariance leverage at \(x\) is small, regardless of the observation count alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The correction to prior-mean error is bounded by covariance leverage at the prediction point times the observed mean discrepancy in the inverse-covariance norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Extrapolation-Bias Correction Bound

children.title: Nonstationary Objective Regimes
children.top_down_role: Objectives whose local behavior varies across the search domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonstationary Objective Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of static-objective guarantees under temporal objective variation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the value observed at round \(t\) have mean \(f_t(x)\), and define temporal variation \[V_T:=\sum_{t=2}^T\sup_{x\in X}|f_t(x)-f_{t-1}(x)|.\] A guarantee derived for a single fixed objective \(f\) applies only to the stationary submodel \(V_T=0\). If \(V_T>0\), static simple regret against one fixed maximizer is not a guarantee for the contemporaneous objectives. Dynamic guarantees require an explicit restriction on \(V_T\), the number of changes, or another drift measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Static Bayesian-optimization guarantees cover only zero temporal variation; changing objectives require a variation or change-count assumption and a dynamic comparator.
assumptions_latex: \(f_t:X\to\mathbb R\) is bounded for each \(t\).
The original guarantee assumes one time-invariant objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_T>0\) places \((f_t)_{t=1}^T\) outside the fixed-objective model unless a separate dynamic guarantee is supplied.

assumptions_latex: \(Z_t\) is independent of past observations and algorithmic randomization available before round \(t\).
The action \(x_t\) is chosen without observing \(Z_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E_\pi[R_T^{\mathrm{dyn}}]=T/2\) for every nonanticipating policy \(\pi\) under this objective process.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-point lower-bound example showing why temporal variation control is necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{0,1\}\). Before round \(t\), draw \(Z_t\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) independently of the information available to the algorithm and define \(f_t(x)=\mathbf 1\{x=Z_t\}\). For every nonanticipating algorithm, \[\mathbb E\!\left[\max_{x\in X}f_t(x)-f_t(x_t)\right]=\tfrac12,\qquad \mathbb E[R_T^{\mathrm{dyn}}]=T/2,\] where \(R_T^{\mathrm{dyn}}:=\sum_{t=1}^T(\max_x f_t(x)-f_t(x_t))\). Thus sublinear dynamic regret is impossible over unrestricted time-varying objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent random changes of the optimal point force expected dynamic regret T/2 for every nonanticipating algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Unrestricted Drift Forces Linear Dynamic Regret

children.title: Abrupt Objective Discontinuities
children.top_down_role: Sharp jumps or breaks that conflict with smooth surrogate structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Abrupt Objective Discontinuities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Step-function counterexample to guarantees assuming a continuous-kernel RKHS.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On \(X=[-1,1]\), let \(f(x)=\mathbf 1\{x\geq0\}\). If the surrogate kernel \(k\) is continuous on \(X\times X\), every member of its RKHS \(\mathcal H_k\) is continuous. Therefore \(f\notin\mathcal H_k\), and no finite radius \(B\) makes \(f\) satisfy \(\lVert f\rVert_{\mathcal H_k}\leq B\). Any confidence, information-gain, or regret conclusion explicitly conditioned on that RKHS-ball assumption is consequently inapplicable to this discontinuous objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A step objective is outside every continuous-kernel RKHS, so guarantees requiring membership in a finite RKHS ball do not cover it.
assumptions_latex: \(k\) is continuous on the compact set \(X\times X\).
The guarantee requires \(f\in\mathcal H_k\) with finite norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\notin\mathcal H_k\), so the hypothesis of the RKHS-based guarantee fails.

notation.meaning: RKHS of the continuous surrogate kernel

assumptions_latex: \(f(c-)\) and \(f(c+)\) exist, are finite, and differ.
\(g\) is continuous at \(c\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp deterministic approximation boundary for continuous surrogates at an objective jump.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:[a,b]\to\mathbb R\) have finite one-sided limits at \(c\in(a,b)\) with jump size \(J:=|f(c+)-f(c-)|>0\). Then every continuous \(g:[a,b]\to\mathbb R\) satisfies \[\lVert f-g\rVert_\infty\geq J/2.\] Consequently, continuous surrogate means cannot converge uniformly to \(f\), although pointwise or \(L^p\) approximation may still be possible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous surrogate cannot uniformly approximate a jump of size J with error below J/2.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Approximation Barrier at a Jump
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Approximation Barrier at a Jump

children.title: Local Regime Transitions
children.top_down_role: Interfaces between regions exhibiting materially different objective behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Regime Transitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Piecewise local models separated by an interface across which values or derivatives disagree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=X_1\cup X_2\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) with nonempty interface \(S=\overline{X_1}\cap\overline{X_2}\), and define \(f(x)=f_j(x)\) for \(x\in X_j\). Assume each \(f_j\) extends continuously to \(S\). A value-level local regime transition occurs when \(f_1|_S\neq f_2|_S\); then the assembled objective is discontinuous at some point of \(S\). More generally, if the pieces possess one-sided derivatives through order \(r\) and some corresponding derivative traces disagree on \(S\), the assembled objective lacks that global smoothness across the interface. A stationary surrogate couples points from opposite regions whenever \(k(x,x')\neq0\) for \(x\in X_1\) and \(x'\in X_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Locally regular pieces form a regime transition when their values or corresponding derivatives disagree at their common interface; cross-region covariance can pool observations across that transition.
assumptions_latex: \(X_1,X_2\subseteq\mathbb R^d\) have a nonempty common interface \(S\).
Each \(f_j\) has the stated one-sided value or derivative traces on \(S\).
Any claimed RKHS exclusion uses a kernel whose RKHS has the corresponding global continuity or smoothness property.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(f_1|_S\neq f_2|_S\), then \(f\) is discontinuous and hence is excluded from every RKHS consisting only of continuous functions; disagreement of derivative traces analogously prevents the corresponding global smoothness.

children.title: Stationary-Surrogate Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which stationary surrogate behavior becomes unreliable.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationary-Surrogate Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage boundary for guarantees built from one stationary kernel and a fixed objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a Bayesian-optimization guarantee be uniform over \[\mathcal F_{k,B}:=\{f\in\mathcal H_k:\lVert f\rVert_{\mathcal H_k}\leq B\},\] where \(k(x,x')=\kappa(x-x')\) is stationary and the objective is assumed time invariant. The guarantee has no stated coverage when either \[f\notin\mathcal F_{k,B}\qquad\text{or}\qquad f_t\neq f_s\ \text{for some }t,s.\] These boundaries can include discontinuities excluded by \(\mathcal H_k\), spatially varying regularity with an uncontrolled RKHS norm, and temporal drift. Posterior calculations may remain defined, but the original frequentist confidence or regret conclusion does not follow.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stationary-surrogate guarantees end when the truth leaves the assumed stationary-kernel ball or changes over time, even though posterior computations may remain possible.
assumptions_latex: \(k\) is a fixed stationary positive-definite kernel.
The guarantee is quantified only over \(\mathcal F_{k,B}\) and a time-invariant objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(f\notin\mathcal F_{k,B}\), or if \(f_t\neq f_s\) for some \(t,s\), the stated guarantee cannot be invoked directly.

children.title: Plug-In Overconfidence
children.top_down_role: Understatement of uncertainty following point estimation of model parameters.

knowledge_statements.title: Plug-In Overconfidence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uncertainty omitted by conditioning prediction on an estimated hyperparameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\theta\) denote covariance, noise, or mean hyperparameters. Under a hyperparameter posterior, predictive uncertainty satisfies \[\operatorname{Var}(f(x)\mid\mathcal D)=\mathbb E_\theta[\operatorname{Var}(f(x)\mid\mathcal D,\theta)\mid\mathcal D]+\operatorname{Var}_\theta(\mathbb E[f(x)\mid\mathcal D,\theta]\mid\mathcal D).\] A plug-in predictor replaces \(\theta\) by a point estimate \(\widehat\theta\) and reports only \(v_{\widehat\theta}(x)
:=\operatorname{Var}(f(x)\mid\mathcal D,\widehat\theta)\). It omits the nonnegative between-hyperparameter term; nevertheless, no universal ordering between \(v_{\widehat\theta}(x)\) and the fully integrated variance holds without additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Point-estimated hyperparameters omit between-hyperparameter uncertainty, but their reported variance is not universally smaller than the integrated variance.
assumptions_latex: The conditional predictive second moments are finite.
A posterior distribution for \(\theta\) given \(\mathcal D\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Var}_\theta(\mathbb E[f(x)\mid\mathcal D,\theta]\mid\mathcal D)\geq0\), and plug-in calibration requires separate control of hyperparameter uncertainty.

children.top_down_role: Loss of global consistency under repeatedly refitted prior parameters.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Adaptive Identifiability Is Necessary for Hyperparameter Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transcript-separation condition required by sequential hyperparameter estimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_{\theta,t}\) be the law of the adaptive transcript through time \(t\). If distinct parameters \(\theta_0,\theta_1\) satisfy \(\limsup_{t\to\infty}\|P_{\theta_0,t}-P_{\theta_1,t}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}<1\), no transcript-measurable estimator can converge in probability to \(\theta_j\) under both \(P_{\theta_j}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hyperparameter consistency requires the adaptively collected transcript to distinguish every consequential pair of parameters.
assumptions_latex: \(\theta_0\ne\theta_1\).
Each estimator is measurable with respect to the adaptive transcript.

notation.meaning: Law of the adaptive actions and observations through time t.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Identifiability Is Necessary for Hyperparameter Consistency

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive failure when sampling never reaches a parameter-distinguishing location.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X\) contain \(x_0,x_1\), and let two GP hyperparameters induce identical observation laws for every sequence of repetitions at \(x_0\), but different predictive laws at \(x_1\). On any positive-probability event where an empirical-Bayes policy samples only \(x_0\), the two parameter likelihoods remain identical for all time; consistent parameter selection on that event is impossible, and the plug-in prediction at \(x_1\) need not approach its true-parameter counterpart.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If sampling remains where two kernels agree, repeated empirical-Bayes refitting cannot learn their consequential differences elsewhere.
assumptions_latex: The competing models agree on the full observation law generated by repetitions at \(x_0\).
They differ in a prediction at \(x_1\).
The policy samples only \(x_0\) on an event of positive probability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pr(\widehat\theta_t\not\to\theta_0\ \text{or the plug-in prediction at }x_1\text{ remains misspecified})>0\text{ may hold}.
knowledge_statements.title: Constant-Design Hyperparameter Nonidentifiability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit topology and probability mode for inconsistency of a sequential plug-in posterior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal F,d)\) contain the true function \(f_0\), and let \(\widetilde\Pi_t(\cdot\mid D_t)\) be the plug-in posterior. It is inconsistent at \(f_0\) in metric \(d\), in \(P_{f_0}\)-probability, if for some \(\varepsilon>0\), \(\widetilde\Pi_t\{f:d(f,f_0)>\varepsilon\mid D_t\}\not\to0\) in \(P_{f_0}\)-probability. Equivalently, for some \(\eta,\rho>0\) and subsequence \(t_j\), \(P_{f_0}\{\widetilde\Pi_{t_j}(d(f,f_0)>\varepsilon\mid D_{t_j})>\eta\}\ge\rho\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Posterior inconsistency means that, in a declared function-space metric and probability mode, the plug-in posterior retains nonnegligible mass a fixed distance from the truth.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal F,d)\) is a measurable metric space containing \(f_0\).
\(\widetilde\Pi_t(\cdot\mid D_t)\) is measurable as a probability kernel of the adaptive transcript.

notation.meaning: Sequential plug-in posterior after hyperparameter refitting.

knowledge_statements.title: Metric Posterior Inconsistency

assumptions_latex: \(X=\{a,b\}\), \(f(a)=0\), \(f(b)=-1\), and observations have independent \(N(0,\sigma^2)\) noise with \(\sigma^2>0\).
The candidate models agree on the deterministic latent value zero at \(a\), but assign deterministic latent values \(-1\) and \(1\), respectively, at \(b\).
Marginal-likelihood ties select \(M_1\).
EI is computed for latent improvement below zero, and zero-EI acquisition ties select \(a\).

notation.meaning: Competing empirical-Bayes models indistinguishable from observations collected at a.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete finite-domain EI failure induced by marginal-likelihood nonidentifiability and deterministic empirical-Bayes and acquisition tie rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{a,b\}\), let the truth satisfy \(f(a)=0\), \(f(b)=-1\), and observe \(Y_t=f(x_t)+\varepsilon_t\) with independent \(\varepsilon_t\sim N(0,\sigma^2)\), \(\sigma^2>0\). Consider candidate models \(M_0,M_1\) that both assign the deterministic latent value zero at \(a\), while assigning deterministic latent values \(-1\) and \(1\), respectively, at \(b\). Initialize at \(a\). Repetitions at \(a\) give identical marginal likelihoods under the two models; let the empirical-Bayes tie rule select \(M_1\). Under \(M_1\), latent EI below the incumbent zero is zero at both points; let the acquisition tie rule select \(a\). The policy then evaluates \(a\) forever and \(f_n^{\min}=0\ne-1=f^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A specified marginal-likelihood and EI tie rule can lock empirical-Bayes EI onto a suboptimal point when sampled observations cannot distinguish two consequential boundary models.
knowledge_statements.title: Two-Model Empirical-Bayes EI Lock-In
Sequential Empirical-Bayes Inconsistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure criterion for adaptive plug-in Gaussian-process hyperparameter refitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let observations be generated by \(y_t=f(x_t)+\varepsilon_t\), while an adaptive policy chooses \(x_{t+1}\) from a posterior using a refitted estimate \(\widehat\theta_t\). Sequential empirical Bayes is inconsistent on an instance if, with positive probability, either \(\widehat\theta_t\not\to\theta_0\) or the resulting plug-in posterior fails to concentrate at \(f\). Pointwise consistency results for fixed or persistently informative designs do not imply consistency here: the design depends on previous estimates and may cease sampling locations that distinguish competing parameters. Consequently, regret or coverage guarantees requiring the true fixed hyperparameter can fail without persistent excitation, uniform estimation control, or hyperparameter uncertainty propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated plug-in fitting can steer sampling away from parameter-informative locations, so neither hyperparameter estimates nor the posterior need converge globally.
assumptions_latex: \(y_t=f(x_t)+\varepsilon_t\) under a true parameter \(\theta_0\).
\(x_{t+1}\) is measurable with respect to the history through the plug-in posterior based on \(\widehat\theta_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Pr(\widehat\theta_t\not\to\theta_0\ \text{or the plug-in posterior does not concentrate at }f)>0\) may hold.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimism over a plausible family of hyperparameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a plausible set \(\Theta_t\), define \(U_t(x)=\sup_{\theta\in\Theta_t}[\mu_{t-1,\theta}(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}s_{t-1,\theta}(x)]\) and \(L_t(x)=\inf_{\theta\in\Theta_t}[\mu_{t-1,\theta}(x)-\sqrt{\beta_t}s_{t-1,\theta}(x)]\). Select \(x_t\in\arg\max_xU_t(x)\). If \(\theta_0\in\Theta_t\) and its band covers \(f\), then \(r_t\le U_t(x_t)-L_t(x_t)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize the most optimistic plausible model and charge regret to the full envelope across plausible hyperparameters.
assumptions_latex: The true hyperparameter \(\theta_0\in\Theta_t\).
The confidence band under \(\theta_0\) holds uniformly over the domain.
A maximizer of \(U_t\) exists, or a declared optimization error is added.

notation.meaning: Robust upper and lower confidence envelopes.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Confidence-Envelope Policy

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pathwise certificate conditional on simultaneous true-parameter coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On an event where \(\theta_0\in\Theta_t\) and the true-parameter confidence band is valid for every \(t\le T\), the robust confidence-envelope policy satisfies \(R_T\le\sum_{t=1}^T[U_t(x_t)-L_t(x_t)]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accumulated robust envelope width certifies cumulative regret whenever the plausible sets retain the true hyperparameter.
assumptions_latex: The assumptions of the Robust Confidence-Envelope Policy hold simultaneously through time \(T\).
knowledge_statements.title: Envelope-Width Regret Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: True-Parameter Exclusion Removes the Coverage Guarantee
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for confidence-set robustification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\theta_0\notin\Theta_t\), validity of all bands indexed by \(\Theta_t\) does not imply that \([L_t(x),U_t(x)]\) covers the true objective. The envelope-width regret certificate is therefore unavailable unless a separate misspecification-error term restores coverage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust policy loses its guaranteed coverage when its plausible set excludes the true model unless misspecification is separately controlled.
assumptions_latex: Confidence statements have been established only for parameters in \(\Theta_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \theta_0\notin\Theta_t\implies\text{no envelope-width regret guarantee follows without misspecification control}.
knowledge_statements.title: True-Parameter Exclusion Removes the Coverage Guarantee

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixture policy preserving recurring parameter-informative sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At round \(t\), independently conditional on the past, take a prescribed diagnostic action with probability \(a_t\), and otherwise use the robust confidence-envelope acquisition. If \(\sum_t a_t=\infty\), diagnostic rounds occur infinitely often almost surely. If their realized cumulative Kullback–Leibler information diverges against every consequential \(\theta\ne\theta_0\), the policy does not permanently abandon parameter-distinguishing observations. When one-round regret is at most \(B\), expected regret charged to diagnostic exploration through \(T\) is at most \(B\sum_{t=1}^T a_t\); it is sublinear when this sum is \(o(T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mix robust acquisition with infinitely recurring but asymptotically sparse diagnostic exploration, preserving parameter information at sublinear expected regret cost.
assumptions_latex: Conditional on the past, the diagnostic-exploration coin has probability \(a_t\) and the coins use fresh randomness.
\(\sum_{t\ge1}a_t=\infty\) and \(\sum_{t\\le T}a_t=o(T)\).
Along realized diagnostic rounds, cumulative KL information diverges for every consequential alternative parameter.
One-round regret is bounded above by \(B\).

notation.meaning: Conditional probability of a diagnostic action at round t.
Number of diagnostic rounds through T.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional finite-time rate for a finite hyperparameter family under simultaneous confidence, variance-sum, and robust-envelope-width premises.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Theta\) be finite and suppose that, on an event of probability at least \(1-\delta\), \(\theta_0\in\Theta_t\subseteq\Theta\) and \(|f(x)-\mu_{t-1,\theta}(x)|\le\sqrt{\beta_t}s_{t-1,\theta}(x)\) simultaneously for all \(x\), \(t\le T\), and \(\theta\in\Theta_t\). Assume \(\beta_t\le\beta_T\), \(\sum_{t=1}^T s_{t-1,\theta}^2(x_t)\le C\gamma_T(\theta)\) for every \(\theta\in\Theta\), and \(U_t(x_t)-L_t(x_t)\le2\sqrt{\beta_t}\max_{\theta\in\Theta_t}s_{t-1,\theta}(x_t)\). Then the robust-envelope policy satisfies \[R_T\le2\sqrt{C T\beta_T\sum_{\theta\in\Theta}\gamma_T(\theta)}\le2\sqrt{C T\beta_T|\Theta|\max_{\theta\in\Theta}\gamma_T(\theta)}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite plausible model family, strong simultaneous-band, width-control, and variance-sum assumptions turn robust envelope widths into a finite-time regret rate with an explicit family-size cost.

Unknown-Hyperparameter Robustification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform-confidence route to Bayesian-optimization guarantees with unknown kernel parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Theta_t\) be a data-dependent confidence set for an unknown hyperparameter \(\theta_0\), and suppose \(\Pr(\theta_0\in\Theta_t\ \text{for all }t)\ge 1-\delta\). If simultaneous bands satisfy \(|f(x)-\mu_{t-1,\theta}(x)|\le \sqrt{\beta_t}\,s_{t-1,\theta}(x)\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\), \(t\ge1\), and \(\theta\in\Theta_t\) on that event, then a policy optimizing a robust upper bound over \(\Theta_t\) may reuse the standard optimism argument. Its regret bound must employ worst-case confidence widths and information complexity over \(\Theta_t\), rather than quantities computed at a single fitted parameter.

children.title: Noise-Misspecification Failures
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by incorrect assumptions about observation variability or dependence.

children.title: Signal-Noise Variance Confounding
children.top_down_role: Misallocation of uncertainty between objective variation and observation noise.

children.title: Latent Objective Variation
children.top_down_role: Uncertainty attributed to variation in the underlying objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Latent Objective Variation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gaussian-process signal variation before observation noise is added.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a latent process \(f\) with mean \(m\) and covariance kernel \(k\), the latent objective variance at \(x\in\mathcal X\) is \(v_f(x)=\operatorname{Var}(f(x))=k(x,x)\). Variation between two locations is \(v_f(x,x')=\operatorname{Var}(f(x)-f(x'))=k(x,x)+k(x',x')-2k(x,x')\). These quantities concern variation of the unobserved objective and exclude the conditional variance of measurement error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Latent variation is the covariance-kernel variance of the unobserved objective, excluding measurement noise.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is second-order with covariance kernel \(k\) on \(\mathcal X\).

children.title: Observation Noise Variance
children.top_down_role: Uncertainty attributed to variability in observed responses.

knowledge_statements.title: Observation Noise Variance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional variance contributed by the observation mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under \(Y(x)=f(x)+\varepsilon(x)\) with \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon(x)\mid f,x]=0\), the observation noise variance is \(v_\varepsilon(x)=\operatorname{Var}(Y(x)\mid f,x)=\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon(x)\mid x)\). Homoscedastic noise has \(v_\varepsilon(x)=\sigma^2\) for every \(x\); heteroscedastic noise permits dependence on \(x\). When noise is conditionally independent of \(f\), \(\operatorname{Var}(Y(x)\mid x)=k(x,x)+v_\varepsilon(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Observation noise variance is the conditional variance of a measurement around its latent objective value; it may vary with location.
assumptions_latex: \(Y(x)=f(x)+\varepsilon(x)\) and \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon(x)\mid f,x]=0\).
\(\varepsilon(x)\) is conditionally independent of \(f(x)\) for the variance decomposition.
