children.title: Variance Attribution Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Cases where latent variation cannot be cleanly distinguished from observational variability.

knowledge_statements.title: Variance Attribution Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonidentifiability of latent nugget variation and independent observation noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose observations occur at distinct inputs and the latent kernel contains a diagonal component, \(k(x,x')=k_0(x,x')+\tau^2\mathbf 1\{x=x'\}\), while independent observation noise has variance \(\sigma^2\). The observation covariance is then \(k_0(x_i,x_j)+(\tau^2+\sigma^2)\mathbf 1\{i=j\}\). Hence every pair \((\tau^2,\sigma^2)\) with the same nonnegative sum yields the same Gaussian likelihood. Without replication or additional structural restrictions, latent small-scale variation and observation noise are not separately identifiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At unreplicated inputs, a latent diagonal kernel term and independent noise enter the likelihood only through their sum.
assumptions_latex: All sampled inputs \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\) are distinct.
The latent kernel includes \(\tau^2\mathbf 1\{x=x'\}\) and noise is independent with variance \(\sigma^2\).
review_flags: exact nugget-noise nonidentifiability claim needs a direct source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The covariance calculation is mathematically coherent and the failure-boundary kind fits, but the exact nugget-versus-noise nonidentifiability claim has no citation.

children.title: Replication-Based Identifiability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Sampling settings where repeated observations clarify or fail to clarify variance attribution.

knowledge_statements.title: Replication-Based Identifiability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which replication separates observation noise from latent variation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At each site \(x_i\), observe replicates \(Y_{ij}=f(x_i)+\varepsilon_{ij}\), \(j=1,\ldots,m_i\), where, conditional on \(x_i\), the errors are independent and identically distributed with mean zero and finite variance \(v_\varepsilon(x_i)\). As \(m_i\to\infty\), the within-site sample variance \(S_i^2\) converges almost surely to \(v_\varepsilon(x_i)\), while the site mean \(\overline Y_i\) converges almost surely to \(f(x_i)\). Thus replication identifies noise variance at replicated sites. Identification of a parametric latent kernel additionally requires sufficiently many distinct sites and an injective map from its parameter to the covariance matrix on those sites; replication alone does not identify unrestricted \(v_\varepsilon(\cdot)\) or \(k\) away from sampled sites.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditionally independent and identically distributed replication identifies noise variance at sampled sites; identifying a parametric latent kernel additionally requires informative distinct sites and an injective covariance parameterization.
assumptions_latex: \(Y_{ij}=f(x_i)+\varepsilon_{ij}\), where the replicates are conditionally i.i.d. at each fixed site \(x_i\).
\(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_{ij}\mid x_i]=0\) and \(\mathbb E[\varepsilon_{ij}^2\mid x_i]=v_\varepsilon(x_i)<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_i^2\to v_\varepsilon(x_i)\) and \(\overline Y_i\to f(x_i)\) almost surely as \(m_i\to\infty\).

notation.meaning: Mean of replicates at site i
Number of replicates at site i

review_flags: requires a direct source for the combined replication and kernel-identifiability condition

children.title: Ignored Heteroscedasticity
children.top_down_role: Miscalibrated uncertainty and allocation under location-dependent noise.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sandwich Noise Variance under a Homoscedastic Fit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact noise-induced sampling variance of a linear GP predictor when true observation variances depend on location.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_0=(K+\sigma_0^2I)^{-1}\), let \(k_x=(k(x_1,x),\ldots,k(x_n,x))^\top\), and suppose the fitted posterior-mean correction is linear in the observed residual vector with weights \(A_0k_x\). If the true conditional observation-noise covariance is \(D=\operatorname{diag}(v_\varepsilon(x_1),\ldots,v_\varepsilon(x_n))\), its conditional noise-induced sampling variance is \(k_x^\top A_0DA_0k_x\). The constant-noise model instead attributes \(\sigma_0^2k_x^\top A_0^2k_x\); the difference is \(k_x^\top A_0(D-\sigma_0^2I)A_0k_x\), which may have either sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The true noise-induced variance of a homoscedastically fitted GP predictor has a sandwich form involving the location-dependent noise matrix and generally differs from the fitted constant-noise contribution.
assumptions_latex: The fitted predictor is linear in observed residuals with weight vector \(A_0k_x\).
Conditional observation errors have mean zero and covariance \(D\).
\(K+\sigma_0^2I\) is invertible.

notation.meaning: Inverse covariance matrix under the fitted constant-noise model
Kernel-covariance vector between sampled sites and prediction point x

knowledge_statements.title: Sandwich Noise Variance under a Homoscedastic Fit
Ignored Heteroscedasticity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Posterior calibration failure from replacing location-dependent noise by one variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For observations at \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\), let the true noise covariance be \(D=\operatorname{diag}(v_\varepsilon(x_1),\ldots,v_\varepsilon(x_n))\), but let inference use \(\sigma_0^2I\). The reported Gaussian-process variance is then computed with \((K+\sigma_0^2I)^{-1}\), whereas the sampling variance of its linear prediction error depends on \(D\). Unless a valid comparison or correction relates \(D\) to \(\sigma_0^2I\), nominal credible or confidence bounds need not attain their stated coverage. Underestimating noise in a region also exaggerates its modeled information gain and can misallocate evaluations there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant-noise model generally reports the wrong uncertainty under location-dependent noise, invalidating nominal coverage and distorting evaluation allocation.
assumptions_latex: \(D=\operatorname{diag}(v_\varepsilon(x_1),\ldots,v_\varepsilon(x_n))\) is the true conditional noise covariance.
Inference instead substitutes \(\sigma_0^2I\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_{n,\sigma_0}^2(x)\) need not equal the sampling mean-square prediction error, so nominal coverage is not guaranteed.

notation.meaning: Latent kernel matrix on sampled inputs
Posterior variance under the assumed constant noise

review_flags: needs a direct heteroscedastic Gaussian-process calibration source

children.title: Heavy-Tail Overconfidence
children.top_down_role: Confidence failure under outliers or slowly decaying observation tails.

knowledge_statements.title: Heavy-Tail Overconfidence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polynomial-tailed noise defeats sub-Gaussian confidence calibration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let independent observation errors have a centered Student distribution with degrees of freedom \(\nu>2\), scaled to finite variance. Its tail satisfies \(\Pr(|\varepsilon|>u)\asymp u^{-\nu}\), so it is not sub-Gaussian. For every fixed \(C>0\), set \(u_n=C\sqrt{\log n}\). Then \(n\Pr(|\varepsilon|>u_n)\to\infty\), and therefore \(\Pr(\max_{1\le i\le n}|\varepsilon_i|>u_n)\to1\). Confidence bands calibrated from a sub-Gaussian or Gaussian tail bound at order \(\sqrt{\log n}\) consequently cannot provide their claimed simultaneous coverage for this noise family without robustification or larger tail-dependent radii.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Student-tailed errors produce outliers larger than any fixed Gaussian-order simultaneous threshold with probability approaching one, causing overconfidence.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_n\) are independent centered Student errors with \(\nu>2\).
The confidence calibration uses \(C\sqrt{\log n}\) for a fixed \(C>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every fixed \(C>0\), \(\Pr\!\left(\max_{1\le i\le n}|\varepsilon_i|>C\sqrt{\log n}\right)\to1\).
review_flags: counterexample calculation needs a direct heavy-tail confidence source

children.title: Correlated-Replication Failure
children.top_down_role: Spurious variance reduction when repeated evaluations are treated as independent.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact dependence-aware variance of a replicate average, generalizing the equicorrelated seed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a replicate-error vector \(\varepsilon=(\varepsilon_1,\ldots,\varepsilon_m)^\top\) with covariance matrix \(\Sigma_m\), \(\operatorname{Var}(\overline\varepsilon_m)=m^{-2}\mathbf 1^\top\Sigma_m\mathbf 1\). If every marginal variance is \(\sigma^2\), then \(\operatorname{Var}(\overline\varepsilon_m)=\sigma^2/m+2m^{-2}\sum_{j<k}\operatorname{Cov}(\varepsilon_j,\varepsilon_k)\). Thus the independence-model value \(\sigma^2/m\) is correct for the mean precisely when the aggregate off-diagonal covariance is zero; a positive covariance contribution bounded away from zero prevents vanishing mean variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The variance of a replicate mean contains all pairwise covariances; independence-based precision is correct only when their aggregate contribution vanishes.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon\) has finite second moments and covariance matrix \(\Sigma_m\).
For the expanded formula, \(\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_j)=\sigma^2\) for every \(j\).
knowledge_statements.title: Replication-Mean Variance under General Dependence
Correlated-Replication Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equicorrelated replicates expose false independent-replication variance reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a fixed input, let replicate errors satisfy \(\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_j)=\sigma^2\) and \(\operatorname{Corr}(\varepsilon_j,\varepsilon_k)=\rho\) for \(j\ne k\), where \(0<\rho\le1\). Then the replicate mean has variance \(\operatorname{Var}(m^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^m\varepsilon_j)=\sigma^2(\rho+(1-\rho)/m)\). An independence model instead reports \(\sigma^2/m\). Thus the reported variance converges to zero while the true variance converges to \(\rho\sigma^2>0\), creating spurious posterior contraction and invalid replication-based confidence claims.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive correlation leaves a nonzero variance floor for replicate averages, although an independence model reports variance vanishing as the replicate count grows.
assumptions_latex: Replicate errors are equicorrelated with \(0<\rho\le1\).
Inference treats the replicates as independent with common variance \(\sigma^2\).
review_flags: equicorrelation counterexample needs a direct source

children.title: Policy-Computation Failure Taxonomy
children.top_down_role: Failures caused by inadequate exploration or inaccurate acquisition computation.

children.title: Exploitation-Induced Sampling Collapse
children.top_down_role: Permanent concentration around an incorrectly favored region.

children.title: Premature Regional Commitment
children.top_down_role: Early concentration on a region favored by misleading evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Premature Regional Commitment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-regret event caused by permanent commitment to a suboptimal region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\subsetneq\mathcal X\), and suppose a policy has an event \(E\) of positive probability on which \(x_t\in R\) for every \(t\ge T_0\). If a global maximizer \(x^\star\notin R\) and \(\Delta_R=f(x^\star)-\sup_{x\in R}f(x)>0\), then on \(E\) every post-commitment instantaneous regret is at least \(\Delta_R\), and cumulative regret satisfies \(R_T\ge (T-T_0+1)\Delta_R\) for \(T\ge T_0\). If additionally \(\max_{1\le t<T_0}f(x_t)\le\sup_{x\in R}f(x)\), then the best-observed simple regret also satisfies \(r_T^{\mathrm{simple}}\ge\Delta_R\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Permanent commitment to a positively suboptimal region forces linear cumulative regret; it also prevents best-observed simple-regret convergence when no better point was sampled before commitment.
assumptions_latex: \(\Pr(E)>0\) and \(x_t\in R\) for all \(t\ge T_0\) on \(E\).
\(\Delta_R=f(x^\star)-\sup_{x\in R}f(x)>0\).
For the simple-regret conclusion, \(\max_{1\le t<T_0}f(x_t)\le\sup_{x\in R}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On \(E\), \(R_T\ge(T-T_0+1)\Delta_R\); under the additional pre-commitment condition, \(r_T^{\mathrm{simple}}\ge\Delta_R\).

notation.meaning: Region receiving all sufficiently late evaluations
Objective gap between the global optimum and region R
Best-observed simple regret through time T

review_flags: needs a direct source connecting sampling commitment to Bayesian-optimization regret failure

children.title: Sampling-Support Collapse
children.top_down_role: Loss of meaningful sampling coverage outside the favored region.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling-Support Collapse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pathwise condition excluding dense global exploration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a realized evaluation sequence \((x_t)_{t\ge1}\) in a compact domain \(\mathcal X\), sampling-support collapse occurs if there exist a finite \(T_0\) and a closed proper subset \(S\subsetneq\mathcal X\) such that \(x_t\in S\) for every \(t\ge T_0\). If a global maximizer \(x^\star\notin S\) satisfies \(\Delta_S=f(x^\star)-\sup_{x\in S}f(x)>0\), then every post-collapse instantaneous regret is at least \(\Delta_S\). If additionally \(\max_{1\le t<T_0}f(x_t)\le\sup_{x\in S}f(x)\), no recommendation restricted to evaluated points can have simple regret below \(\Delta_S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sampling support collapses when all sufficiently late evaluations remain in a proper closed subset. An excluded positive-gap optimum then causes persistent instantaneous regret, and also persistent evaluated-point simple regret when no superior point was sampled earlier.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X\) is compact and \((x_t)_{t\ge1}\subset\mathcal X\).
There are \(T_0<\infty\) and a closed \(S\subsetneq\mathcal X\) with \(x_t\in S\) for every \(t\ge T_0\).
For the evaluated-point simple-regret conclusion, \(\max_{1\le t<T_0}f(x_t)\le\sup_{x\in S}f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\Delta_S=f(x^\star)-\sup_{x\in S}f(x)>0\), post-collapse instantaneous regret is at least \(\Delta_S\); under the additional pre-collapse condition, evaluated-point simple regret is also at least \(\Delta_S\).

notation.meaning: Time after which no sample leaves S
Objective gap between the global optimum and S

review_flags: formal support-collapse terminology and convergence implication need a direct source

children.title: Self-Reinforcing Posterior Confidence
children.top_down_role: Confidence patterns that intensify continued concentration after exploration declines.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X=\{s,u\}\) has independent Gaussian prior coordinates with unit marginal variances and prior means \(m(s)=M>0\), \(m(u)=0\).
The initial design contains a noise-free observation \(f(s)=M\), while the fixed objective satisfies \(f(u)>M\).
The UCB exploration multipliers satisfy \(0\le\beta_t\le\bar\beta<M^2\).
Ties, if any, are resolved in favor of \(s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_t=s\) at every subsequent round, while \(f(u)-f(s)>0\); instantaneous and best-observed simple regret remain at least \(f(u)-M\).

notation.meaning: Uniform upper bound on the exploration multiplier.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-point construction in which independent posterior coordinates and bounded optimism make the favored observation permanently self-confirming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X=\{s,u\}\) have independent unit-variance Gaussian prior coordinates with \(m(s)=M>0\) and \(m(u)=0\). After a noise-free initial observation \(f(s)=M\), suppose the fixed objective has \(f(u)>M\). For \(a_t(x)=\mu_{t-1}(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}\sigma_{t-1}(x)\) with \(\sup_t\beta_t=\bar\beta<M^2\), conditioning leaves \(a_t(s)=M\) and, by independence, \(a_t(u)=\sqrt{\beta_t}<M\). The policy therefore repeatedly selects \(s\), receives no information about \(u\), and remains suboptimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With independent regional prior coordinates and a bounded exploration bonus, an initially favored observation can permanently confirm its own ranking while a better alternative remains unobserved.
knowledge_statements.title: Block-Independent Confidence Trap
Self-Reinforcing Posterior Confidence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feedback loop between local sampling, plug-in confidence, and acquisition exclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an acquisition rule maximize \(a_t(x)=\mu_{t-1}(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}s_{t-1}(x)\). A self-reinforcing confidence trap occurs when there are \(T_0\) and \(S\subsetneq\mathcal X\) such that, for every \(t\ge T_0\), plug-in refitting from data sampled in \(S\) yields \(\sup_{x\notin S}a_t(x)<\sup_{x\in S}a_t(x)\). The policy then never samples outside \(S\); consequently no outside observation can correct the fitted mean, kernel, or underestimated uncertainty responsible for the strict acquisition inequality. If a positive-gap maximizer lies outside \(S\), the trap produces persistent positive regret.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Locally collected data can sustain low acquisition values elsewhere, preventing corrective observations and locking the policy into a suboptimal confidence loop.
assumptions_latex: The policy selects a maximizer of \(a_t(x)=\mu_{t-1}(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}s_{t-1}(x)\).
The strict acquisition separation between \(S\) and its complement persists after \(T_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_t\in S\) for all \(t\ge T_0\); if \(f(x^\star)>\sup_{x\in S}f(x)\), regret remains bounded away from zero.
review_flags: needs a direct source for the plug-in posterior feedback failure mechanism

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The acquisition-separation condition does imply continued sampling inside S when maximizers exist, and the failure-boundary kind fits. The claimed plug-in feedback mechanism and Bayesian-optimization failure interpretation require a direct source.

children.title: Exploration Recovery Barriers
children.top_down_role: Conditions that prevent the policy from revisiting neglected regions.

assumptions_latex: At each round \(t\), independently across rounds and independently of the past, the policy uses forced exploration with probability \(\epsilon_t\) and then draws from \(q\).
\(q(U)>0\) for the measurable neglected region \(U\).
For the finite-mass nonreturn conclusion, from some round \(T\) onward the nonexploration branch never selects \(U\), and \(\epsilon_tq(U)<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_t\epsilon_t=\infty\Rightarrow\Pr(x_t\in U\ \mathrm{i.o.})=1\); if \(\sum_t\epsilon_t<\infty\) and the ordinary branch excludes \(U\) after \(T\), then \(\Pr(x_t\notin U\ \forall t\ge T)>0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Almost-sure recovery and the finite-exploration-mass boundary for randomized forced exploration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose that at round \(t\), with probability \(\epsilon_t\), a policy draws \(x_t\sim q\), using randomization independent across rounds and of the past; otherwise it uses an arbitrary acquisition branch. For every measurable \(U\) with \(q(U)>0\), \(\sum_t\epsilon_t=\infty\) implies \(x_t\in U\) infinitely often almost surely. Conversely, if \(\sum_t\epsilon_t<\infty\) and the nonexploration branch never selects \(U\) after some \(T\), then \(\prod_{t\ge T}(1-\epsilon_tq(U))>0\), so permanent nonreturn to \(U\) after \(T\) has positive probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full-support forced exploration revisits every positive-mass neglected region infinitely often when its total probability diverges; finite total exploration can leave positive probability of permanent nonreturn when the ordinary policy remains blocked.
knowledge_statements.title: Forced-Exploration Recovery Boundary
Exploration Recovery Barriers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deterministic acquisition-ranking barrier preventing return to an excluded region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X=S\mathbin{\dot\cup}U\), where \(U\) is an unsampled region, and let \(a_t:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) be the acquisition function after round \(t\). If \(\sup_{x\in U}a_t(x)<\sup_{x\in S}a_t(x)\) for every \(t\ge t_0\), then any policy selecting \(x_{t+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}a_t(x)\) satisfies \(x_{t+1}\in S\) for every \(t\ge t_0\). Consequently, observations cannot revise the posterior on \(U\); exploration can recover only if an acquisition bonus, randomization, or approximation error eventually reverses the strict ranking.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once every acquisition maximizer remains inside the sampled region, posterior updates alone cannot restore exploration of the excluded region.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal X=S\mathbin{\dot\cup}U\) with \(U\ne\varnothing\).
\(\sup_U a_t<\sup_S a_t\) for all \(t\ge t_0\).
The policy selects a global maximizer of \(a_t\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, and the strict ranking excludes global maximizers from U. However, observations in S can revise the posterior on U when the model correlates the regions, so that consequence requires correction or explicit independence assumptions. No source with an inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Acquisition Local Optima
children.top_down_role: Policy degradation caused by consistently selecting nonglobal acquisition optima.

knowledge_statements.title: Acquisition Local Optima
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A smooth one-dimensional acquisition exhibiting persistent nonglobal local optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\), the smooth acquisition \(a_\varepsilon(x)=-(x^2-1)^2+\varepsilon x\) on \(\mathcal X=[-2,2]\) has two strict local maximizers \(\ell_\varepsilon<0<g_\varepsilon\), with \(a_\varepsilon(\ell_\varepsilon)<a_\varepsilon(g_\varepsilon)\). A deterministic local acquisition solver initialized in the basin of \(\ell_\varepsilon\) returns \(\ell_\varepsilon\), although \(g_\varepsilon\) is globally optimal. If warm starts remain in that basin across rounds, the computed policy can repeatedly select a nonglobal acquisition optimum and thereby invalidate guarantees requiring exact acquisition maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A warm-started local solver can repeatedly return the inferior peak of a smooth two-peak acquisition function.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\varepsilon\) is sufficiently small.
The local solver converges within the basin containing \(\ell_\varepsilon\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample kind fits the acquisition-local-optima leaf, and the perturbed double-well supports inferior and global local maxima for small positive epsilon. The across-round persistence and solver-basin assertions require precise conditions and a cited source.

children.title: Vanishing-Improvement Numerics
children.top_down_role: Loss of numerical discrimination for improvement acquisitions in extreme posterior regimes.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Unexpected Improvements to Expected Improvement for Bayesian Optimization
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Unexpected Improvements to Expected Improvement for Bayesian Optimization

assumptions_latex: The implementation evaluates the positive scaled-tail remainder with a stable special-function, continued-fraction, or asymptotic routine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\log\operatorname{EI}=\log\sigma-a^2-\tfrac12\log2+\log(\pi^{-1/2}-a\operatorname{erfcx}(a))\), so candidates can be compared without exponentiating the vanishing factor.

notation.meaning: Positive tail coordinate equal to minus the standardized improvement divided by square root of two.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Log-scale evaluation of Gaussian expected improvement in the negative standardized-improvement tail.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z<0\), set \(a=-z/\sqrt2\). Then \[\operatorname{EI}=\frac{\sigma e^{-a^2}}{\sqrt2}\left(\frac1{\sqrt\pi}-a\operatorname{erfcx}(a)\right).\] Evaluate the positive parenthesized remainder with a stable scaled-tail routine and retain \(\log\operatorname{EI}\) for candidate comparison. This avoids underflow from \(e^{-a^2}\) and avoids directly forming \(z\Phi(z)+\phi(z)\) from nearly cancelling tail terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative-tail expected improvement can be ranked in log scale using a scaled complementary-error representation, avoiding premature underflow and direct tail cancellation.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Log-Scale Tail Evaluation of Expected Improvement
knowledge_statements.title: Log-Scale Tail Evaluation of Expected Improvement

assumptions_latex: The predictive marginal is Gaussian with \(\sigma>0\).
The incumbent \(f_*\) is held fixed when differentiating with respect to \(\mu\) and \(\sigma\).
For the input-gradient conclusion, \(\nabla\mu\) and \(\nabla\sigma\) remain bounded along the considered tail sequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\partial\operatorname{EI}/\partial\mu=-\Phi(z)\to0\) and \(\partial\operatorname{EI}/\partial\sigma=\phi(z)\to0\) as \(z\to-\infty\); under bounded posterior derivatives, \(\nabla_x\operatorname{EI}\to0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Derivative degeneration of Gaussian expected improvement in an unfavorable posterior tail.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For minimization, \(\operatorname{EI}(\mu,\sigma)=(f_*-\mu)\Phi(z)+\sigma\phi(z)\), where \(z=(f_*-\mu)/\sigma\). Its parameter derivatives are \(\partial\operatorname{EI}/\partial\mu=-\Phi(z)\) and \(\partial\operatorname{EI}/\partial\sigma=\phi(z)\). Both vanish as \(z	o-\infty\). Consequently, if \(
abla\mu\) and \(
abla\sigma\) remain bounded, the input gradient \(
abla_x\operatorname{EI}\) also vanishes along that tail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the unfavorable Gaussian tail, expected improvement loses sensitivity to both posterior mean and posterior deviation; with bounded posterior derivatives, its input gradient also vanishes.
knowledge_statements.title: Expected-Improvement Parameter-Sensitivity Degeneration
Vanishing-Improvement Numerics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected-improvement discrimination in the extreme negative standardized-improvement regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For minimization with posterior mean \(\mu(x)\), deviation \(\sigma(x)>0\), and incumbent \(f_*\), expected improvement is \(\operatorname{EI}(x)=\sigma(x)\bigl(z(x)\Phi(z(x))+\phi(z(x))\bigr)\), where \(z(x)=(f_*-\mu(x))/\sigma(x)\). As \(z\to-\infty\), \(z\Phi(z)+\phi(z)\sim\phi(z)/z^2\), so the acquisition becomes exponentially small. If finite-precision evaluation rounds this quantity to zero at several candidates, their exact positive improvements become numerically indistinguishable; maximization may then depend entirely on tie-breaking rather than on expected improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected improvement is exponentially tiny for very unfavorable standardized means, so floating-point evaluation can erase meaningful acquisition differences.
assumptions_latex: The predictive marginal is Gaussian with \(\sigma(x)>0\).
Expected improvement is evaluated in finite-precision arithmetic.

notation.meaning: Best incumbent objective value for minimization.
Standard normal distribution and density functions.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is appropriate, and the expected-improvement formula and negative-tail asymptotic are mathematically consistent. The floating-point underflow or rounding claim and the asymptotic have no cited source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Approximation-Induced Underexploration
children.top_down_role: Exploration loss caused by approximate posterior uncertainty or approximate policy computation.

assumptions_latex: \(a,\widetilde a:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) are bounded above.
\(\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}|a(x)-\widetilde a(x)|\le\varepsilon\).
\(\widetilde a(\widehat x)\ge\sup_{x\in\mathcal X}\widetilde a(x)-\delta\), where \(\varepsilon,\delta\ge0\).

notation.meaning: Exact and implemented approximate acquisition functions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic transfer of acquisition approximation and optimization errors to exact-acquisition loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\lVert a-\widetilde a\rVert_\infty\le\varepsilon\) and \(\widehat x\) is a \(\delta\)-maximizer of \(\widetilde a\), then \(\widehat x\) is a \((2\varepsilon+\delta)\)-maximizer of \(a\). Moreover, if \(U\subseteq\mathcal X\) satisfies \(\sup_U a-\sup_{\mathcal X\setminus U}a>2\varepsilon+\delta\), every such \(\widehat x\) lies in \(U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform acquisition error epsilon and optimization error delta lose at most 2 epsilon plus delta in exact acquisition value; a larger regional margin prevents approximation-induced exclusion.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Acquisition-Error Certificate
Approximation-Induced Underexploration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent exploration loss caused by downward-biased approximate uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal X=S\mathbin{\dot\cup}U\) and let the implemented optimistic acquisition be \(\widetilde a_t(x)=\widetilde\mu_t(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}\,\widetilde\sigma_t(x)\). Suppose the exact acquisition \(a_t(x)=\mu_t(x)+\sqrt{\beta_t}\,\sigma_t(x)\) is maximized in \(U\), but approximation suppresses uncertainty enough that \(\sup_{x\in U}\widetilde a_t(x)<\sup_{x\in S}\widetilde a_t(x)\) for every \(t\ge t_0\). Exact maximization of \(\widetilde a_t\) then never samples \(U\). Thus a persistent one-sided variance error can remove the optimism mechanism needed for exploration, even when acquisition optimization itself is exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Downward-biased approximate variance can rank every unexplored point below sampled points and permanently defeat an otherwise optimistic policy.
assumptions_latex: \(\beta_t>0\) and \(\mathcal X=S\mathbin{\dot\cup}U\).
The approximate acquisition has a strict persistent ranking of \(S\) above \(U\).
The implemented policy globally maximizes \(\widetilde a_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{t+1}\in S\text{ for every }t\ge t_0\), even though \(\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathcal X}a_t(x)\subseteq U\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, and the assumed strict approximate-acquisition ranking implies no sampling in U. However, the record does not formally connect a one-sided variance error to that ranking, particularly when approximate means may also differ. A supporting source and precise approximation conditions are required.

children.title: Curse of Dimensionality
children.top_down_role: Deterioration of covering, information, and regret complexity with dimension.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Random Search Retains Exponential Dimension Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact success probability for uniform random search on a Lipschitz objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\|x\|_\infty\) on \([0,1]^d\), and let \(X_1,\ldots,X_T\) be independent uniform points. Then \(\Pr(\min_{t\le T}f(X_t)>\varepsilon)=(1-\varepsilon^d)^T\). Thus success probability at least \(1-\delta\) requires \(T\ge \log(\delta)/\log(1-\varepsilon^d)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform random search requires order epsilon to the minus d evaluations on a simple Lipschitz objective.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\varepsilon<1\).
\(X_1,\ldots,X_T\) are independent and uniform on \([0,1]^d\).

notation.meaning: Lipschitz objective minimized at the origin.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Random Search Retains Exponential Dimension Dependence

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covering growth underlying dimension-dependent unstructured optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(0<\varepsilon\le 1/2\), the \(\ell_\infty\)-covering number satisfies \((2\varepsilon)^{-d}\le N(\varepsilon,[0,1]^d,\|\cdot\|_\infty)\le(1+\varepsilon^{-1})^d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Covering a d-dimensional cube at resolution epsilon requires on the order of epsilon to the minus d cells.
assumptions_latex: \(0<\varepsilon\le1/2\).
The metric is \(\ell_\infty\).
knowledge_statements.title: Metric Entropy of the Cube

assumptions_latex: The domain is \([0,1]^d\) with a fixed norm.
The objective class is the set of real-valued 1-Lipschitz functions.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_A\sup_{f\in\operatorname{Lip}_1}\mathbb E_f[r_T(A)]\ge c_dT^{-1/d}\), so expected regret at most \(\varepsilon\) uniformly requires \(T\ge(c_d/\varepsilon)^d\).

notation.meaning: Class of 1-Lipschitz objectives on the cube.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimax dimensional obstruction for randomized adaptive exact-value algorithms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(d\ge1\), there exists \(c_d>0\) such that every randomized adaptive algorithm making \(T\ge1\) exact-value queries on \([0,1]^d\) satisfies \[\sup_{f\in\operatorname{Lip}_1([0,1]^d)}\mathbb E\!\left[f(\widehat x_T)-\min_xf(x)\right]\ge c_dT^{-1/d}.\] The expectation is over the algorithm's randomization. Equivalently, a uniform expected-simple-regret guarantee at most \(\varepsilon\) requires \(T\ge(c_d/\varepsilon)^d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even randomized adaptive exact-value optimization of unrestricted Lipschitz functions needs order epsilon to the minus dimension evaluations.
knowledge_statements.title: Randomized Lipschitz Optimization Lower Bound
Curse of Dimensionality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case evaluation complexity for Lipschitz black-box optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider noiseless value queries to an unknown \(1\)-Lipschitz function \(f:[0,1]^d\to\mathbb R\). For every algorithm that, after \(T\) adaptive queries, recommends \(\widehat x_T\) with worst-case simple regret \(f(\widehat x_T)-\min_x f(x)\le\varepsilon\), a packing argument gives \(T\ge c_d\varepsilon^{-d}\) for sufficiently small \(\varepsilon>0\), where \(c_d>0\) depends only on the chosen norm and dimension. Hence uniform accuracy requires a number of evaluations exponential in \(d\) at fixed reciprocal accuracy; noise cannot improve this worst-case dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without additional structure, optimizing a Lipschitz function to accuracy epsilon requires on the order of epsilon to the minus dimension evaluations.
assumptions_latex: \(f:[0,1]^d\to\mathbb R\) is \(1\)-Lipschitz.
The oracle returns exact function values.
The guarantee is uniform over the Lipschitz class.

children.title: High-Noise Identifiability
children.top_down_role: Difficulty distinguishing near-optimal alternatives under dominant observation noise.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Balanced Replication Achieves the Gaussian Identification Scale
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-allocation upper bound for identifying the better of two noisy alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For two alternatives whose means differ by \(\Delta>0\), sample each \(n\) times under independent \(N(0,\sigma^2)\) noise and recommend the larger sample mean. With \(T=2n\), \(\Pr(\widehat i_T\ne i_*)\le \tfrac12\exp\{-T\Delta^2/(8\sigma^2)\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Balanced replication identifies the better Gaussian alternative using order noise variance divided by squared gap samples.
assumptions_latex: The mean gap is \(\Delta>0\).
Errors are independent Gaussian variables with common variance \(\sigma^2\).
Each alternative receives \(T/2\) observations.
knowledge_statements.title: Balanced Replication Achieves the Gaussian Identification Scale

assumptions_latex: \(\Delta_T>0\), so each hypothesis has a unique best alternative.
Observations are conditionally independent Gaussian variables with variance \(\sigma^2\).
The sampling policy and terminal recommendation may be adaptive and randomized.

notation.meaning: Positive mean gap at horizon T.
Unique best alternative under hypothesis h.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-gap unique-best instances that become asymptotically indistinguishable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(T\), consider two Gaussian hypotheses with mean vectors \((\Delta_T,0)\) and \((0,\Delta_T)\), common variance \(\sigma^2\), and \(\Delta_T>0\). Under any adaptive allocation of \(T\) observations, their transcript divergence is \(T\Delta_T^2/(2\sigma^2)\). Pinsker's inequality therefore gives \[\inf_{\widehat i_T}\max_{h\in\{0,1\}}\Pr_h(\widehat i_T\ne i_*(h))\ge\frac12\left(1-\frac{\Delta_T\sqrt T}{2\sigma}\right)_+.\] If \(T\Delta_T^2/\sigma^2\to0\), the minimax error tends to \(1/2\), although every instance has a unique best alternative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive but shrinking gaps become statistically invisible when total signal-to-noise tends to zero, forcing identification error toward one half.
knowledge_statements.title: Vanishing Signal-to-Noise Identification Family
High-Noise Identifiability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-alternative Gaussian lower bound for identifying the better design.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two Gaussian alternatives with known variance \(\sigma^2\) and two hypotheses having mean vectors \((\Delta,0)\) and \((0,\Delta)\), where \(\Delta>0\). Under any adaptive allocation of \(T\) observations, the transcript divergence between the hypotheses is \(T\Delta^2/(2\sigma^2)\). The Bretagnolle–Huber testing bound therefore implies that worst-case probability of recommending the inferior alternative is at least \(\frac14\exp\{-T\Delta^2/(2\sigma^2)\}\). Achieving error probability at most \(\delta<1/4\) consequently requires \(T\ge(2\sigma^2/\Delta^2)\log(1/(4\delta))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distinguishing two alternatives separated by gap Delta requires samples proportional to noise variance divided by Delta squared.
assumptions_latex: Observations are conditionally independent Gaussian variables with known variance \(\sigma^2\).
The two possible mean vectors are \((\Delta,0)\) and \((0,\Delta)\).
The recommendation error must not exceed \(\delta<1/4\) under either hypothesis.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the identifiability leaf. Under the stated swapped Gaussian hypotheses, each observation contributes the asserted KL divergence regardless of the selected alternative, and the testing reduction is plausible. The exact Bretagnolle–Huber constant and adaptive-transcript argument require an authoritative citation with a precise locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed unique-best lower bound at a tie.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If two alternatives have equal means, no procedure can identify a uniquely best alternative with error below \(1/2\) uniformly over two labelings.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposal treats an arbitrary labeling of tied alternatives as an identifiable unique-best parameter.
assumptions_latex: The alternatives have equal observation laws.
Success nevertheless requires recovering a hidden unique-best label.

notation.meaning: Artificial labeling of statistically identical alternatives.

children.title: Vacuous Information-Gain Control
children.top_down_role: Kernel or dimensional regimes where generic capacity bounds provide little effective control.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Independent Kernel Has Linear Maximum Information Gain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Kernel example attaining linear information capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On a domain containing at least \(T\) distinct points, let \(k(x,x')=\mathbf1\{x=x'\}\). Under Gaussian noise of variance \(\sigma^2>0\), a design of \(T\) distinct points has covariance matrix \(I_T\), and maximum information gain is \(\gamma_T=\frac T2\log(1+\sigma^{-2})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an independent-value kernel, every new point contributes constant information and maximum information gain is linear.
assumptions_latex: The domain contains at least \(T\) distinct points.
Observation noise is independent Gaussian with variance \(\sigma^2>0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Independent Kernel Has Linear Maximum Information Gain

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounded-Kernel Information Control Is Only Linear
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Universal information bound that alone cannot establish no regret.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For Gaussian observations with variance \(\sigma^2>0\) and \(k(x,x)\le\kappa^2\), every \(T\)-point design has information gain at most \(\frac T2\log(1+\kappa^2/\sigma^2)\). Substitution into \(R_T\le C\sqrt{T\beta_T\gamma_T}\) yields only \(O(T\sqrt{\beta_T})\), so bounded marginal variance alone does not prove sublinear regret.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bounded prior variance gives only linear information-gain control and cannot by itself prove no regret.
assumptions_latex: Observation noise is independent Gaussian with variance \(\sigma^2>0\).
\(k(x,x)\le\kappa^2\) for every design point.
The available regret estimate has the displayed information-gain form.

notation.meaning: Uniform bound on marginal kernel variance.

knowledge_statements.title: Bounded-Kernel Information Control Is Only Linear
Vacuous Information-Gain Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: When information-gain regret bounds cease to imply sublinear regret.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose rewards have range at most \(B\), so cumulative regret satisfies the trivial bound \(R_T\le BT\). An information-gain analysis yielding \(R_T\le C\sqrt{T\beta_T\gamma_T}\) provides a nontrivial asymptotic guarantee only when \(\beta_T\gamma_T=o(T)\). If \(\beta_T\gamma_T\ge (B^2/C^2)T\), its right-hand side is at least \(BT\) and is therefore no stronger than the trivial bound. Thus kernels, dimensions, or confidence schedules producing essentially linear \(\beta_T\gamma_T\) make this generic information-gain control vacuous for proving no regret.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An information-gain regret estimate is vacuous when its capacity factor grows linearly enough to match or exceed trivial linear regret.
assumptions_latex: Per-round regret is bounded above by \(B\).
The available guarantee is \(R_T\le C\sqrt{T\beta_T\gamma_T}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\beta_T\gamma_T\not=o(T)\) prevents this bound alone from establishing \(R_T=o(T)\).

notation.meaning: Maximum information gain after T observations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is appropriate. Algebraically, the displayed information-gain bound establishes sublinear regret only if beta_T gamma_T is o(T), and the threshold comparison with the trivial bound is correct. The underlying Bayesian-optimization regret form and claimed kernel or dimensional regimes lack cited support.

children.title: Cumulative-Regret Impossibility Regimes
children.top_down_role: Unavoidable limitations for online optimization performance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymptotic cumulative-regret obstruction for uniformly efficient Gaussian-bandit policies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite Gaussian bandit with known common variance \(\sigma^2\), unique best mean \(\mu_*\), and gaps \(\Delta_i=\mu_*-\mu_i>0\), every uniformly efficient policy satisfies \(\liminf_{T\to\infty}\mathbb E[N_i(T)]/\log T\ge2\sigma^2/\Delta_i^2\). Consequently, \(\liminf_{T\to\infty}\mathbb E[R_T]/\log T\ge\sum_{i:\Delta_i>0}2\sigma^2/\Delta_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every uniformly efficient Gaussian-bandit policy incurs at least logarithmic gap-dependent cumulative regret.
assumptions_latex: The action set is finite.
Rewards are independent Gaussian observations with known common variance \(\sigma^2\).
There is a unique best mean.
The policy is uniformly efficient in the Lai–Robbins sense.

notation.meaning: Number of selections of arm i through horizon T.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Growing Alternative Sets Can Force Linear Regret
knowledge_statements.scope_note: No-regret boundary inherited from finite-domain minimax regret.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a problem class contains an unstructured \(K_T\)-armed subclass whose minimax expected cumulative regret is bounded below by \(c\min\{T,\sqrt{K_TT}\}\), then \(K_T\ge aT\) implies minimax regret \(\Omega(T)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the number of independent alternatives grows proportionally to the horizon, worst-case cumulative regret can remain linear.
assumptions_latex: The class contains the stated unstructured finite-action subclass.
\(K_T\ge aT\) eventually for some \(a>0\).

notation.meaning: Effective number of independent alternatives at horizon T.

knowledge_statements.title: Growing Alternative Sets Can Force Linear Regret

assumptions_latex: The kernel is \(k(i,j)=\mathbf1\{i=j\}\).
Observation errors are independent Gaussian variables with the variance used in the corresponding bandit model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \([0,1]^K\subseteq\{f\in\mathcal H_k:\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le\sqrt K\}\), and kernel-optimization cumulative pseudo-regret equals Gaussian-bandit cumulative pseudo-regret.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact embedding transferring finite-action cumulative-regret lower bounds into an explicitly stated kernel function class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{1,\ldots,K\}\) and \(k(i,j)=\mathbf1\{i=j\}\). Then \(\mathcal H_k=\mathbb R^K\) with \(\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}^2=\sum_{i=1}^Kf(i)^2\). Hence every mean vector \(\mu\in[0,1]^K\) lies in the ball \(\{f:\|f\|_{\mathcal H_k}\le\sqrt K\}\). With independent Gaussian observation noise, sequential kernel optimization on this domain is exactly a \(K\)-armed Gaussian bandit and has identical cumulative pseudo-regret.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A diagonal kernel on a finite domain makes noisy kernel optimization exactly an unstructured Gaussian bandit, with RKHS radius scaling as the square root of the number of alternatives.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Gaussian Bandits as Diagonal-Kernel Optimization
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Gaussian Bandits as Diagonal-Kernel Optimization
Cumulative-Regret Impossibility Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimax online-regret obstruction inherited from finite noisy domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\ge2\) and \(T\ge K\). For stochastic optimization on a \(K\)-point domain with independent unit-variance Gaussian observations and unknown means in \([0,1]^K\), every adaptive policy has an instance whose expected cumulative regret satisfies \(\mathbb E[R_T]\ge c\sqrt{KT}\), for a universal constant \(c>0\). Since a finite domain is a valid Bayesian-optimization domain and can be represented by a diagonal kernel, no general noisy Bayesian-optimization guarantee over this class can improve the minimax order without additional structural assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even on a finite noisy domain, every policy suffers worst-case expected cumulative regret of order square root of K times T.
assumptions_latex: \(K\ge2\) and \(T\ge K\).
Each selected arm yields an independent Gaussian observation with variance \(1\).
Arm means lie in \([0,1]\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits this impossibility-regime leaf, and the finite Gaussian-bandit lower-bound order is standard. The precise parameter regime, universal-constant claim, and transfer to a diagonal-kernel Bayesian-optimization class require sources specifying the associated function-class assumptions.

children.title: Simple-Regret Impossibility Regimes
children.top_down_role: Unavoidable limitations for terminal recommendation accuracy.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Growing Alternative Sets Prevent Vanishing Uniform Simple Regret
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency boundary inherited from the unstructured finite-domain minimax rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a noisy problem class contains \(K_T\) independent alternatives and has minimax expected simple regret at least \(c\min\{1,\sqrt{K_T/T}\}\), then \(K_T\ge aT\) implies a nonvanishing minimax lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With proportionally as many independent alternatives as observations, terminal simple regret cannot vanish uniformly.
assumptions_latex: The class contains the stated unstructured finite-domain subclass.
\(K_T\ge aT\) eventually for some \(a>0\).

notation.meaning: Number of effectively independent alternatives at budget T.

knowledge_statements.title: Growing Alternative Sets Prevent Vanishing Uniform Simple Regret

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact relation between terminal recommendation probabilities and expected simple regret on a finite domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(i_*\) be the unique best alternative, \(\Delta_i=\mu_*-\mu_i\), and \(\widehat i_T\) the terminal recommendation. Then \(\mathbb E[r_T]=\sum_i\Delta_i\Pr(\widehat i_T=i)\). If every suboptimal alternative has gap in \([\Delta_{\min},\Delta_{\max}]\), then \(\Delta_{\min}\Pr(\widehat i_T\ne i_*)\le\mathbb E[r_T]\le\Delta_{\max}\Pr(\widehat i_T\ne i_*)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected simple regret is the gap-weighted probability of recommending each alternative.
assumptions_latex: The action set is finite.
The best alternative \(i_*\) is unique.
\(r_T=\mu_*-\mu_{\widehat i_T}\).

notation.meaning: Smallest and largest positive suboptimality gaps.

knowledge_statements.title: Identification–Simple-Regret Conversion
Simple-Regret Impossibility Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimax terminal-recommendation obstruction inherited from finite noisy domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\ge2\) and \(T\ge K\). After \(T\) adaptive observations from a \(K\)-point domain with independent unit-variance Gaussian noise and an unknown mean vector in \([0,1]^K\), let \(\widehat i_T\) be any terminal recommendation. There exists a universal constant \(c>0\) such that every sampling and recommendation rule satisfies \(\sup_\mu\mathbb E_\mu[\mu_* - \mu_{\widehat i_T}]\ge c\sqrt{K/T}\). Therefore a uniform expected simple-regret guarantee of accuracy \(\varepsilon\) requires \(T=\Omega(K/\varepsilon^2)\), absent further smoothness or correlation structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Terminal recommendation error cannot uniformly beat order square root of K over T on an unstructured noisy finite domain.
assumptions_latex: \(K\ge2\) and \(T\ge K\).
Observations have independent Gaussian noise of variance \(1\).
The unknown reward means belong to \([0,1]^K\).

notation.meaning: Number of alternatives and observation budget.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits the terminal-recommendation impossibility leaf, and the stated square-root K/T rate is plausible for an unstructured Gaussian finite domain. No citation supports the exact minimax formulation, parameter regime, or resulting sample-complexity statement.
